i'm writing this review based on the main game alone. i can see that there are a lot of people who are unsatisfied by either the dlc, the 'mod compatibility' (i guess you could call it) or both. it's quite disappointing to see the amount of people who are spoken out about their problems and the steps bethesda is taking. we'll see what they do in the future and to be honest the modding community of skyrim and other bethesda games is what made them so successful and have continued replayability with more content by others constantly being added. not having that is a big hit to the replayability and ability to be creative with this game... but on to the actual game:
i love it. always having been a fan of open world games, i was ecstatic to have discovered fallout 3 a while back. right from the get-go we're placed into the middle of the action. exploring the wasteland has never been so clean and crisp, and with all the additions to the game, the vanilla game is one of the most fun and interesting games i've honestly ever played.
the settlement system is a little bit gimmicky, and i really hated it at first, but i've learned to live with it and have actually found it quite fun after a while. being able to be creative and build your own settlement is rather interesting actually. while there are a lot of limitations to what you can build as well as the building interface being really wonky, it's a fun idea and hope to see more improvement to this in future games.
not going to delve into the story, just going to say that i really do enjoy how your actions really do impact the game and what happens, almost like a visual novel within a game. the world itself looks very nice. i have to say that it's a huge improvement from previous games, even if interfaces and the environment can sometimes be a little bit clunky or hard to navigate.
the combat system and gunplay is satisfying and it works well. i'm going to have to say that there hasnt been any real change in the combat system with the same vats system being used, but it works, and i guess you shouldnt fix what isnt broken. the perks system isn't anything particularily special or balanced but it works. the weapon modding systems don't feel very fun or interesting at all, really just choosing the highest level upgrade every time you return to the workbench, but it's a small con and doesn't impact the game very much,
i love the voice acting and how much it makes me feel like my character is an actual person rather than the sole centre of the universe that everything revolves around. the game is bleak and serious yet it knows when to throw a joke or two in there. playing on a normal difficulty for the first time is always a pleasant experience, but the terror that comes with survival mode is something that was really unexpected. i wasnt expecting to facepalm so many times when i run into a group of enemies like a moron and die.
now... the game is wonderful but like any other title, there are a lot of really significant problems. the biggest gripe that i have with this game is that, although immersive, it feels too similar to other bethesda games. the crappy interfaces, the annoying loading times that can last up to 30 seconds when leaving any single area, the game making anything and everything look like a mound of rubble on anything but the highest quality settings. bethesda really didnt fix any of the glaring issues from previous games. skyrim felt open and empty at times with vast areas of nothingness, and fallout 4 attempts to fix this by instead, adding repetitive quests of "help this settlement" or "bring me this item from this area" or "kill these people at this place". i really dont want to have to play all this filler content in order to level up and actually progress through the game. anyways, this has sort of just become a blurb of me writing random feelings about the game.
tl;dr, i really loved this game. its a game that i really just couldn't put down until i finished and even after there was more to do. it's an immense game filled with a surprise at every corner and makes you feel like you're almost inside the wasteland itself. there are a lot of things that make you feel tired of the game and how it treats you but at other times you'll just sit there... hours and hours on end running through the ruined streets of boston and contemplating life, war and other bs
not sure if my review really made sense, i just kind of wrote what i felt about the game, but i'd give fallout 4 a solid 8/10. i really did enjoy this game even if it ♥♥♥♥ed with me a lot

It was a sunny, clear day, as bright as any other, when the way of the town was changed forever. Lying dead on the ground were two of our members, stabbed clean through the chests. This left us all quaking, but was made even worse when we read the blood-spattered notes left behind:
"my knife slipped lol"
":D"
We stood around in solemn silence as we realized the bitter truth: There were traitors among us. The mafia was active, and even then there was another dangerous person with a knife. a Serial Killer. Who could we trust? Nobody knew.
I knew my duty, at least. I was the jailor. Anybody who raised suspicion around me was going to be under my close scrutiny. If I deemed them untrustworthy, the cell would be the last thing they ever saw.
The trials went on for a few days, all uncertain, all fearful, and always ending badly. Time and time again, we had woken up to fresh new corpses, yet only added to the trouble by going into hysterics and putting our fellow townmembers on trial. The sheriff, the veteran, the doctor, we felled them one by one. We knew that somewhere among us, the Mafia were smiling with glee.
There was one person who was rubbing us the wrong way. He sat quietly in the back, and we had yet to learn what his role was. "Who are you?" one of us called to him one day.
There was a pause. "I don't feel safe revealing my role yet," he muttered back. This was fair enough. We had no reason to lynch this man, and we were wary enough after taking out so many of our own town. He'd been trying his best to help out with the trials, as well, giving valid evidence and no reason to suspect he was purposely hurting any of the town. However, I had a duty to do. As another unproductive day ended and we all turned to return to our homes, I took him for the night. We shared quiet muttering between each other. He was just as unyielding in giving away his role. He still didn't feel safe, he said, "but rest assured, I'm not out to hurt the town." I don't know why I believed him. There was no evidence behind it. But he was the single most geniune seeming person in this town. I gave him a chance and gave him my word I would let the town know his innocence.
The following day had more corpses. Luckily, one was the Serial Killer, so those worries were qualmed. There were few of us now. Maybe seven remaining of what was once a whole town, and with the Medium long gone, we were cut off from any advice their spirits might give. All three of the Mafia still remained.
It was at this point the quiet man, who had been recently whispering among certain members left of the town, was called out. Solemnly, he climbed to the center on trial. Some of the town demanded his role, demanded he be lynched. He offered no defense. All he said, as he was stepping up to the rope, was that he was with the town.
The time came to vote. Something was off here. He had been helping the town. There was no way there wasn't something more. Taking a step back, I abstained from the vote. A few others did, as well. In the end, three voted guilty.
As the body swung, we all gathered around to read the final will. And oh, was it a treat.
"I was an executioner, but my target died early on in the game. I decided that I might as well help the town out. Good luck, you guys."
I was glowing with joy, and presumably the other two town members were as well. The whispering he had been doing was informing the others to abstain, and it looked like it worked. He had been carefully egging on the Mafia. The Jester would have his vengeance that night, and it would be on the Mafia in the name of the town. The next morning, we woke to the body of the Mafioso. Unfortunately, I had been the last victim before the Jester carried out his work. As I watched from the afterlife, I wished the rest of the team good luck and sat back to observe.
How the rest of it happened it somewhat unclear to me. In some strange set of circumstances, one town member and one Mafia member died. All that was left was the Godfather and a single town member, whose identity was still unknown.
The ghosts began the farewells, thanking everybody for a match well played... but what's this? That town member stood triumphantly, unswayed.
"Well, well, well." They stepped forward with a flourish. "Do you know who I am?"
We all saw. The spirits of the town began crying in victory as their identity was revealed with a flourish; the last standing town member was our Mayor!
The Godfather went pale. He knew he was bested. The proceeding events were systematic, and the reign of the Mafia was put down victoriously with the pure power of democracy wielded by our leader, who had, by some chance, fought through all the bloodshed and deception unscathed and unidentified. The town went wild with this incredible victory. This, to date, has been the best town win I have ever been able to say I was a part of.
tl;dr: Get this game. It's fun and at times absolutely hilarious.

Having read through some of the mess that is this games reviews, I just had to throw my opinion in the hat.
There are lot of negative opinions being thrown around... no stick/ps controller support (annoying but painlessly fixed by third party trick by myself at least), no keyboard mapping (who the hell plays fighting game on keyboard!? Sorry, but this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t) and the servers re-enacting chinese new year at Capcom. The last one is perhaps the most annoying, but they apparently are working on it. Hell, these days, it's a sign of impeading apocalypse if a AAA game has a smooth launch.
Lack of fighters is but lamentable, but more are supposed to be coming, and buyable by ingame currency. Now, you might say: "I don't wanna grind that!", to which I respond: "Suck it up and play the game, if you like it." If you don't, why the heck did you buy it?
Missing content? True enough, the lack of arcade mode is somewhat annoying, and the storymode is a bit lackluster. Kind like extremely lite version of Blazblues story mode. Take a note Capcom, if you're gonna do it this way... that's the way to go. Not this... stillbirth of a storymode. However, the arcade mode and trials are supposed to come later on in free patch, so meh. Not going to lose sleep over that. Especially since this was announced well before the launch.
Bugs and glitches? Haven't seen any so far. There no doubt are some, but they haven't been my problem at this point. Maybe that'll change? Who knows.
Gameplay wise the fighters are balanced and there is still plenty of variety. The graphics... while perhaps not dazzling, are more than adequate for the game.
All in all, my opinion is that Street Fighter V is good, though a bit unfinished game. If you want all shiny and polished product, then you are better off waiting for a month or two. Otherwise, Street Fighter V is a fine compatitive fighting game. Is that worth 60$ (or whatever you pay for it, for me it was ~30€)? That's up to you guys and girls...
Personal verdict at the moment: 7.5/10, mainly due missing content and server problems. Once those are fixed, I'd probably add at least a point more there, but that is to be seen.

Plainly compared to it's predecessor Tales of Zestiria which was a catastrophy this opus of the "Tales of" series shines only by it's better character design and that's only the graphic design as their personalities are still overly simplistic and lacking any real charm.
The world is in the past of Zestiria's which is sad as I found Zestiria's world and themes to be entirely unappealing. No Overworld map of course. The crafting sytem has been blessedly simplified, in response to heavy critcism of Zestiria's I expect. However it is still inspired from Zestiria's and the Normin system was replaced with simple RANDOM generation of equipment skills.... So as is ever sadly the case with many japanese games the designers show their utter lack of respect for our time (and money) in implementing such systems which are extremely time-consuming while being absolutely no fun at all. Yes complex systems are the bread and butter of J-rpgs but they still need to be fun. When will they finally learn from their mistakes? Game = Fun. Overly complicatred sytems which add nothing to the game with random factors to make them more time consuming and thus artificially prolong the game life expectancy = NO FUN. It is a contracdiction of gaming.
The game also has a TON of enemies on EVERY dungeon or map or whatever. It's endless and completely breaks the rythm of the story.
Another annoying thing is the skits. Tradition in the "Tales of" series the skits in Berseria are both endless in terms of inane dialogues and many tend to sprout well.... all the time. So there you have another artificial prolongation of game time. Now I'm so bored with them I just button mash through them and guess what? I can still follow the story just fine and don't feel like the charcters have any less depth than they had before (which was not much to begin with as I stated previously).
As for the story.... No comment. But then that was never the "Tales of" strong point to begin with.
So yeah, disappointed. Wouldn't have bought it if I had known.

One of the best modern JRPG i ever played. It has a decent story with interesting anti-hero characters. Interaction between characters is joyful to see and there are plenty of that. But what makes this game great is the battlesystem.
Unlike most JRPG, combat in this game is not turn based. After encounter with enemy, combat done in real time. It played just like action game, where the player control one character, three other characters in party controlled by AI, and two characters on standby. It has local co-op option where second character can be played with second controller, but i have yet to try that. With this kind of setup, some other modern JRPG have some restriction on how much player can control, for example character controlled by AI is untouchable by player. But in Berseria, player have full control of the party. You can switch between character on the fly in a battle so it does not feel restricted by the presence of AI.
Battle itself is action based, but it is so good and almost feel like playing good fighting game. It has everything that fighting game should have. It has block, counter, dodge, combo, and flashy special move. This game is build around combo system. Doing some long combo or harder to pull combo is feel rewarding. There are usual resistance-weakness that JRPG has, with some element tied to some skill, so there will be different combo from battle to battle. Skills per character is quite plenty, with freedom to change skill button makes the variation rather large. Another good thing about the combat is the time flow of the battle. Most normal encounter done less than 10 second. Even cutscene of flashy special move a.k.a. Mystic Arte is done in 3-5 second. The flow is fast and feel just about right.
There are some bad thing from the game. This game is quite linear. You are forced to go on storyline and cannot jump to some places, not until some point of the game. Exploration is rather limited and not rewarding. The worst thing is its inventory management. Some item limited to 15 not usual 99, i can live with that. But there are equipment number limitation that not even documented. Equipment farming become less enjoyable because you can go over capacity and stop receiving equipment. Enhancing and dismantle equipment become tedious thing to do because you have come back often from dungeon.
This is 70+ hours game from start to finish, but even after 100+ hours i have not tired of it yet doing extra end-game content and new game+ still awaits. So i think this game is definitely worth its price.

*POTENTIAL SPOILERS*
So just a tad of back story. I got Breath of the Wild when it came out and easily pumped about 120 hours into it. After I finished everything I wanted, and set forth and beat Ganon the game was complete and I did not know what to do with myself. So for days on end I just sat in boredum not knowing what sort of game to play, or what to do. I needed something to fill my time and occupy the void that Breath of the Wild left in me. That is when I noticed Tales of Zestiria in my Steam library. I never really got into the Tales games before - although I had played Symphonia just over halfway through. Sadly, never finished it though. I enjoyed Zestiria. It was a nice story, the characters were likeable. The game mechanics were fun and I had a lot of fun playing it. Ultimately, it allowed me to peacefully move on from Breath of the Wild.
Sadly, I noticed Tales of Berseria was on sale during the Anime Sale Steam had on at the time. I was not very far into Zestiria so I did not know if I wanted to buy it. So I missed the sale. Once I had beaten Zestiria and learning that Berseria was a sequel I had to have it. So sadly, I paid full price. After having played the game, I would have paid double to play through this amazing experience. I feel like Zestiria was a test game leading up to Namco's Magnum Opus in Tales of Berseria.
The characters. Just simply amazing. Every single one of them is their own person with their own amazing quirks. I won't go too in depth about what each one is due to spoilers, but I fell in love with everyone I met, even the NPCs. No conversation is ever random. Every single Skit is fun and enjoyable and adds a little more to the story. Some conversations even become running gags that continue on throughout the entire story. So where Zestiria was about a group of very innocent and pious people going on a typical good Vs. evil trope, Berseria breaks the mold as you essentially play as "the bad guys". And I put this in air-quotes because throughout the game - for myself at least - you're left wondering, AM I really the good guys? Or am I actually the bad guys? Definitely interesting to say the least. The group of characters you play as is more of a travelling circus rather than a typical Tales group of heroes.
The story itself is bloody amazing. Pure fun and enjoyment the whole way through. I never got bored of listening to the Skits, or traversing the land. Sometimes the story had me laughing, and sometimes it brought me close to tears. It was truly moving. I actually could feel some of the character's pain. Every single bit of the main story, and side stories gets wrapped up. You need to do a little sleuthing to find it all but no question is left unanswered. Also, the way this story ties into Zestiria is simply amazing. They leave no little bit of fanservice out. You'll see characters from Zestiria, landmarks, references. Not to mention there is a boatload of references to the other Tales games in Berseria as well (wish I had played them all now). This game got me obsessed with the Tales series. Simply obsessed. I would have dreams about the game. I'm still sitting here as I write this hoping they will release all the old Tales games remastered and available for PC. Just reushing through the story and staying a decent level to deal with the last boss you could easily get 50 hours out of this game. I got about 72 hours exploring and finding things to my hearts content.
The battle system is great. Still very Tales-like in the sense that it's a real-time battle circle. But just like Zestiria, the battle field becomes wherever you encounter an enemy. I once had a tree in the middle of my battle arena! The game also keeps unlocking new features as you explore. There is always something new to learn and explore even as much as 70% into the game. I was never really bored with this game, I just wnated to keep playing it more and more.
So all-in-all this game is amazing. The landscapes are beautiful. Towns are mesmerizing. The NPCs comments are funny. The characters are interesting and relatable. There are very few problems with the game that I noticed. Around the end I found several spelling errors in the chat log. There was a tiny bit of framerate drop in areas with lots of enemies or NPCs. But overall these are small things you can overlook. I would easily give this game a perfect score. 10/10. I am even considering playing a new game plus and doing it all over again. If you love the Tales series, or even just want a great game, this is the game for you. I'd suggest getting Zestiria too, and playing that first just so you get the whole experience. Or maybe play them in reverse order and see how that works out.

This game is a lot of fun.
If you've played Terraria, then you pretty much know what you're getting into. It's basically Terraria in space. If you haven't played Terraria, then it's like a 2D, side-scrolling Minecraft in space.
You can travel between different planets with different environments and features, build teleporters to travel between them quickly, and with the latest patch, add colonists to your player-created structures to give your creations life. Your ship expands as you progress through the quests, and you can customize each section and decorate them as you please. You can even add NPCs to your crew and collect all kinds of procedurally-generated pets from different planets.
Now, the game has come a long way, but still has some distance to go. There are only a few boss fights, and the story and progression fizzles out rather quickly, but if you're looking for a nice, 2D sandbox game, and are into the whole sci-fi/space scene, then you should give this game a go. If you sign up for the nightly or unstable branches, you'll get even more content much faster, though you have to sacrifice some stability.
Overall, a fun sandboxer with some really cute looking sprite graphics.

is the third installment in the

This game is almost identical to
in terms of gameplay and as I liked that one, it will come as no surprise that I give this third installment a thumbs up also.
A few (minor) changes have taken place, however. First, instead of constructing four buildings on the game world map by acquiring a three stars rating on each level, you now build one giant complex in the course of the game.
Second,  completing the four secret levels with a three stars rating now unlocks a super secret level.
Third, the boss levels have been replaced by regular levels. As I was not keen on the boss levels, this is an improvement to the game for me.
Fourth, the level design has undergone a slight visual polish.
The story is still quite forgettable and the music is really not my thing, but as they can be easily skipped or muted I have no problems with them. This series keeps getting better and better and therefore, I recommend it.

OK, the negative: The online multiplayer seemed to work relatively fine during the beta testing phase and upon launch, however, I have been unable to find an online paring since. I hope Capcom appreciates the problem and provides us with some kind of good-will gesture in the shape of some content.
There is a distinct lack of content although each character has a 'story' mode which is around 3 - 4 fights of filler story we are left feeling somewhat had by the seemingly rushed artwork and repetative fights (Literally you may have to fight the same person twice out of 4 fights) which are of absolutely no challenge.
Beyond these main gripes I love the game it feels like a mash up of the 3, 4 and alpha series which is welcoming enough for new players to the franchise and will hopefully provide a level of depth which will keep seasoned veterans satisfied.
Visually, the game has never looked better as we move away from the cartoonised styling of the four series and are left with a more serious, earthy visualisation of our favourite characters.
Gameplay is undoubtedly more forgiving than the 4 series as combo inputs allow for slightly more time to perform and  many characters have been given easier inputs for example Chun=Lis hundred foot kick moving from the rapid button pressing of previous games to a quatre circle motion.
I see many people have issues with fightstick recognission but as of yet my Xbox Limited edition Madcats TE Stick is working perfectly.
I have faith that Capcom will resolve these issues and we will have numerous updates with balancing etc it would be easy to highlight the negatives, but I choose to Rise up :)
P.S The survival mode is far too easy Hell? more like Hell no let's get the AI more challenging please Capcom.

20-30 minute art game; sort of a visual novel/point & click. No saves, but that's not a big deal considering the game's length. Some grammar issues in the text (particularly the overcompensating use of "whom") and sound balance problems (the voice acting is much quieter than the music, with no way to adjust it). The puzzles can be a bit frustrating; although they make logical sense and it's generally clear what you need to do, it's sometimes hard to figure out
to do it when you have approximately 1.5 seconds to find the relevant hotspots before you die. However, there's no game over and you can repeat the puzzles as many times as you need.
The main draw is the presentation, with colorful, stylized art that draws the player into its disorienting, surreal atmosphere. You could replace all the text with
and I would still find it a compelling experience. If you think $3 is too much for such a short game, then wait for a sale, but if the art style interests you, it's definitely worth your time to check out.

**UPDATE**
So a few things have been added since I first wrote this review. Some new roles (forger, vampire, vampire hunter) have been added, and the scrolls system has been introduced.
I decided to add this bit because I have seen a lot of negative reviews based solely on the fact that the scrolls system had been implemented. Here's what you need to know:
The scrolls system DOES:
- increase your chance of a getting a particular role
- Mean that if there are a few people using a particular scroll, you are less likely to get that role
- require the use of town points to purchase (but you earn town points for each game you play)
The scrolls system DOESN'T:
- stop you from getting a particular role if people are using scrolls for that role
- guarantee that you will get the particular role you have a scroll for the first time you use it
- apply in ranked games. Scrolls cannot be used in ranked, so you have an equal chance of getting any role.
- Stop the game from being enjoyable
There is also now a chat filter you can turn on if you like.

- I generally dont care much about story.  I aim more for quality gameplay.
- This is my first tales game.
- My favorite RPG aspects include a wide array of item selection and character customization and tuning.
- I like boundlessly difficult games.
- I am a big fan of the Final Fantasy series.
Story:
I am not super drawn in by the story at this point.  To me its no FF7 or something that I am likely to remember as long as I have retained the story of FF7.  The absolute biggest problem that I have with this game centers around the story,  and that is that much of the time you aren't actually playing the game.  There is so many cutscenes and dialog in this game that it feels more like you are influencing the direction of a movie rather than playing a game.  While many of these can be skipped I've committed to watching them since players rage about the story in this game,  and commiting to watch them sometimes means that you will have potentially 3 or 4 chained dialog cutscenes between the characters that I thus far (about 30 hours) have not cared much about.  One caveat here is that I generally skip the stories in games and an more engaged in quality gameplay.
Graphics:
The graphics IMO are at least a decade old.  I don't expect crysis(2007) however games like FFXV at least appear to be trying to push out good visuals.  This game does not try.  I don't generally mind the character art, however all of the levels and character animations in the open world seem really dated.
Battle:
I find the battle system to be okay.  I don't think its anything special but it does do well as an RPG breaking away from your average turn based system.
I also don't know how to characterize this however this game does not seem to have a huge selection of gear, it doesn't seem to have any skill points or talent trees.

So...this game is weird, but in a good way.
The story is pretty straight forward, read the little description and you pretty much got it. There is a nice little message at the end of the game which made me think twice about my actions and words used. Other than that I felt like the game lacked a lot of depth that it could have achieved with a little more development. The world is very cool, I liked everything about it from the characters, to the environments, to the creatures. I felt like the writing was a bit...eh...much. I felt like I was listening to someone read off their first non-fiction work in freshman english in highschool. BUT, that's like my singular complaint on the writing. Everything else was good.
The gameplay is simple and straight forward. You go through a series of slideshow cut scenes listening to the narrator read off the text on screen allowing you to look at the background art. After the slideshow cut scenes you get to use your characters Sight Goggle thingy to solve puzzles. Every encounter begins with time paused allowing you to observe items in the environment and their function as well as the character you're going against and additional information on them. Once all of your information was collected you can resume time and procede to activate the various items and solve the puzzle. The puzzles progressively get more difficult beginning at ridiculously easy and straight forward during the tutorial to still pretty easy with the final encounter.
The puzzles being relatively simple is easy to forgive, at least for me, mostly because I enjoyed exploring the items in the environment and reading up on everything I could. The game ends with an odd, almost out of place encounter where you get to make a few choices which are supposed to affect the ending. I wish that these choices actually did something and that there were more of them. That's actually this games greatest fault (yes, more than the writting), it never really reaches it's fullest potential. There are so many cool concepts and so many neat themes and interesting lore but there simply isn't enough of it. I was left at the end of the game wanting much much more.
Take a gander at the screenshots, if you don't like what you see, then there you go. I personally was okay with it. The art doesn't add to or detract from the game its self or the narrative, it was just kind of there. Felt more like rushed concept art to me, but like I said, I was okay with it.
Grade: C

Quite simply the best Tales game since Tales Of The Abyss. If Zestiria left a sour taste in your mouth, Berseria will try its damndest to redeem that title (and usually succeeding) while also devouring 60+ of your life in its own right. Zestiria left me wanting to get to know Eizen and he's end up being one of the most enjoyable characters in the Tales series. But alas, it also plagues us with the Jar Jar Binks of the Tales series with the over-dramatic and annoying Magilou. She tries too hard to be the comic relief only to get shown up by Bienfu, Eizen, Laphicet, and occassionally Rokurou. Another suprizing addition is Elanor, the disgraced exorcist. She ends up becoming the complementary opposite of Velvet - kicking and screaming in self-righteous denial all the way! Their character development over the the course of the game will remind you of how well Luke from Tales of The Abyss was handled.
Other than that, don't let the specifications for this game fool you -- my stock Intel G3258 along with a GeForce 1050 can easil dish out a consistant 60 FPS at 1080p on my HDTV in Big Picture mode with most options cranked to maximum detail (save for shadow details - you might want to keep them at medium or lower). Zestiria couldn't even produce such performance at the lowests settings! Alas, if you're using the native GPU of the G3258 (or faster i3/i5/i7 processors), you might have to tone down the draw distance and SMAA ...
Now for the bad news: your party members will seldom use their second or third Mystic Artes, and some will spam their 1st Mystic Arte like no tomorrow. Every time you turn around, there's Rokorou dishing out a Form 0: Sunder, Eizen goes ballstic, and Elanor is lighting a small fry up ... but when you need them to pull out the big guns during boss fights or Code Red hunts, you'll be disappointed. Every time Elanor gives an enemy a Lost Fon Drive, I gotta mark it on the calender - that's just how rare it is, and there seems to be no magic setting or configuration to address the issue. :(
Had to buy a GTX 980 just to play this at ultra! Highly reccomend it!

The Eigengrau Menagerie is a fantastic little artsy puzzle game.  It's a little short, perhaps, for the money, but it's certainly one of the more unique experiences on Steam.  You play as a pilgrim, wandering to find the great Thoughforms of the world.  The gameplay is pretty simple: you start each challenge with time frozen, and you can take as much time as you need to read the descriptions of all of the highlighted objects and people around you.  Each challenge is a pretty simple puzzle, but must be solved within a couple of seconds, before the challenger kills or captures you.  Luckily, you do get infinite tries, but therein lies one of the problems - because of this mechanic, you can pretty much just brute force all of the puzzles if you choose to.
I found the best part of the game to be the backgrounds art - you can clearly tell that it was drawn as a labor of love.  The background music complements the art style quite nicely, and the story, although quite esoteric at times, is acceptable.  Overall, I'd definitely recommend the game.
Pros:
Fantastic art style
Nice BGM
Good atmosphere, and a good experience overall
Potato Erotica
Cons:
Writing is perhaps a bit pretentious
Length - game is far too short
No save option - you have to finish in one sitting (although It only took me around 30 minutes to finish, so it shouldn't be a problem)
BGM and voice acting are recorded at different volumes
Other thoughts:
The writer really likes the color "bronze-gold" for some reason.  Does it mean something?

One of the greatest works of art in human history--
When Leopardi wrote his poems, he was searching for something, for a sense of *more*, for a meaning, for, in a word, transcendence -- that finds expression in every sentence, nay, every word and sentence of this masterpiece: right down to the vowels. The only way to transcendence -- is this game.
When Nietzsche developed his philosophy he wanted to escape from the assumptions and misconceptions of European society and culture, to become truly a self; to date the only work of art that would assist one in becoming an Ubermensch - to be become *what one is*-- is this game.
When Sartre wrote his No Exit and Nausea, he was trying to express the strange incoherence of existence that lies behind our built-up beliefs and behaviours, to show how Radical Freedom is the fact of our lives. The only path one can walk to fulfill your potential to be a self, to truly exist,  -- is this game.
When Pessoa wrote his "factless autobiography" he was trying to express the inexpressible tedium of life, to express through paradox the fact that even the idea of paradox is a paradox; for individuality is the containing of paradoxes in our selves, yet to nothing, for tedium continues to crush us. But the only way to escape the pain of living -- is this game.
When Kafka wrote his Trial and Metamorphosis he was able to show the absurdity of human relationships, the fragility of so-called love, and justice and law: but the only thing that can truly express these truths: -- is this game.
When Cioran wrote about his times at the peaks of despair, about his bottomless white nights of insommia, he was trying to show the "irrational nature of existence which continues itself without reason": but the only work of art that can show this to us, so far: -- is this game.
And, when each of us stops for just a moment, as we wake up and cringe ourselves out of our beds and anticipate the disasters, misery and shame that the day will bring us; what are we looking for? The beauty of yuri is the only thing that justifies life, for in reading yuri we lose everything to the purity and gain nothing... -- for what is there to be gained from the world? Nothing. The world is material for our intrepretation of the world, but all of these intrepretations, being personal, are meaningless. Therefore only yuri allows us to express our radical freedom, to survive our white nights, to give solidity to our love, and our society, to allow our paradoxes to form a beautiful whole, to find transcendence, to become what we are: the only way to survive the world we live in -- is yuri.

It's Half-Life. An important piece of gaming history that revolutionized a genre. You owe it to yourself to play it if you haven't already. It shows its age in some ways (apart from the obvious, like graphics and sound), mainly because it's been copied endlessly. But its still a blast, and it's still easy to see why it was so highly acclaimed in 1998.
It was Valve's first game though, and even though they struck gold with Half-Life, their inexperience at the time shows through on a couple of chapters. Notably "On A Rail", and of course, most of the Xen chapters. This isn't their magnum opus. No, that came in the form of the sequel to this game.

This is a great turn-based, squad level tactical game. There are some strategic elements, as with XCOM: Enemy Unknown, and they're enjoyable, but the heart of the game is in the combat scenarios.
Being scenario oriented, rather than random event oriented as EU was, helps me enjoy this game more. I don't feel like I'm playing the same maps over and over, and I don't get annoyed at the exact same gas station being in Novosibirsk, Sao Paolo, and Saskatoon.
Character customization is pretty cool. If there were a way to select your starting party it would be even cooler, but that would interfere with game balance issues, so it's understandable that you can't.
My one real complaint is performance. Loading times can be long, and for a game that isn't intense real-time 3d combat, it's awfully demanding on system resources.

Whilst Trackday is a great concept, at this stage of development I cannot recommend this game as one to buy now. It is very laggie (even with a 3Mbts per sec connection), the game play is really clicking a couple of buttons to increase speed and remembering to re-click before your engine overheats. I was doing really well in races until I upgraded my car, and now performance is worse than the starter car - so very quickly this game has become "not fun". There isn't much to do outside of racing, except upgrading your car, accepting contracts (one click wonders), and assigning experience points (which seem to do nothing). This game frequently crashes, and can lock up whilst you are at the starting grid, and once it unlocks, your car is halfway round the track having being passed by everyone during the time the game locked up. This happens frequently during round the track often too.
There are only 3 cars to choose from at this stage, the models are nice, and you can either have a top down view of your car, or go first person and see the race from the passenger seat - which is nice also.
The developer has stated that the races favour the player but the AI seems to be able to come from half a track down, to zoom past you (or knock you out of the race) which is just stupid.
There are no penalties, so bad driving gets rewarded heavily and cars don't seem to suffer any damage even when they have been endoed by some rogue AI car.
For frustration, I give this game a 10/10, otherwise:
Buy it, if you don't mind waiting for alot of fixes and additions to be made.

The "flesh" will be the final polish that hopefully will occur over time. If I were going to design a 4x fantasy strategy game with what I would want to see included, it would be this game. The author/dev is active and this would seem to be a labor of love for him...
But the game is rather 2D/Superficial as of this post. This game plays like an updated version of Grand Prix Manager 2 from 1996. You don't actually race any cars, instead you instruct the driver during a race when to over take, when to use extra power, when to pit, etc. The bulk of the game also involves obtaining sponsorship deals in order to earn more money for car upgrades.
Although it is fun it is entirely focused on multiplayer, which is a problem because at the momet not a lot of people are playing the game. I feel like the $20 price tag is partially responsible for this issue, it seems too much for a beta of this sort. In my opinion a cheaper price of $10-$15 would ultimately attract more players, making the game more fun and involving.
I would love to see this game become more populated so I certainly recommend it, but in all honesty the developers need to add more features before they can justify the beta price.

The game is unique, and fun to play when it works. Online stability is pretty iffy, and there isn't a whole lot of content just yet. I’d be interested to follow up with the game over time to see how it’s shaping up, as the devs have been dropping patches frequently. If they can manage to eliminate most of the server issues and add a bit of content, this game has the potential to become genuinely special.
It’s worth mentioning that the game is being developed by a small studio of six people, and it already looks fantastic. The in-race lighting effects, especially during nighttime runs, are impressive, especially among its Early Access peers. Taking into consideration that cooperative racing teams are in the works as well, allowing for you and your friends to take on races together in your sponsor-covered customized cars, Trackday Manager might be one of the most compelling racing experiences to grace PC gaming in a long while. Easy to learn, but bloody difficult to master, this is definitely one to watch.

Buy it.

This game is a lot of fun.
If you've played Terraria, then you pretty much know what you're getting into. It's basically Terraria in space. If you haven't played Terraria, then it's like a 2D, side-scrolling Minecraft in space.
You can travel between different planets with different environments and features, build teleporters to travel between them quickly, and with the latest patch, add colonists to your player-created structures to give your creations life. Your ship expands as you progress through the quests, and you can customize each section and decorate them as you please. You can even add NPCs to your crew and collect all kinds of procedurally-generated pets from different planets.
Now, the game has come a long way, but still has some distance to go. There are only a few boss fights, and the story and progression fizzles out rather quickly, but if you're looking for a nice, 2D sandbox game, and are into the whole sci-fi/space scene, then you should give this game a go. If you sign up for the nightly or unstable branches, you'll get even more content much faster, though you have to sacrifice some stability.
Overall, a fun sandboxer with some really cute looking sprite graphics.

Short version:
-This game is a great fighting game
-Has online problems on launch most likely due to having 2 platforms on the same server alongside just needing time to adapt to the issues concerning the netcode.
-All dlc is free.

To everyone complaining about the lack of content currently in the game, we were all warned a suitable amount of time before release that there'd be little content outside of multiplayer on release. Most people should be aware of that by now, so it's not really a valid arguement at this point. As much as people want to call Capcom out on the lack of features, they didn't actually do anything morally wrong this time lol. DLC is free too, you'll be able to earn it all, so any complaints about these two subjects are basically invalid.
As an actual fighting game, this is solid, the gameplay is fresh, combos cater to the newer players enough and there's still a lot of depth to it; it pleases older and newer fans just fine in my opinion. Alongside having an already diverse cast more characters are actually on the way, Alex is set for release next march. Alongside this, a bunch of other features and extras will be added as time goes on like an actual arcade and story mode alongside the market. The tutorial mode that's available at least teaches you some basics, the rest is kind of for you to figure out really. That's part of the fun of these games anyway, it is sort of poorly done in this case, but it's nothing you can't find out for yourself by asking around/doing research. You'd have to do research at some point anyway if you plan on taking this game half-seriously, so there is that too.
Online mode has been relatively OK for me so far. I used a wired connection, so maybe that's why but I've had hardly any issues with lag. The one time I've lost a match because of it was against some guy in Canada, which isn't too bad given that IV had netcode that made it even more difficult to play with people this far away most of the time. Aside from this one incident I've won all my matches pretty cleanly with hardly any contribution from lag. I also feel like people need to understand that on launch, any online-based game is going to have problems. There's hardly ever been a massively online game that had no online issues right out of the box, because most servers aren't able to handle it well initially. SF has a massive fanbase and it was crossplay too, that means players from two different platforms are going to be on the same server, which sort of justifies how poorly it's been handling the load so far. They'll improve it with time, that much can be certain at this point.
I'm guessing it's because of maintenace but I haven't been able to find a match recently after waiting a while, so I can't really say much as far as actually finding a match. I did however struggle earlier for a while trying to make a lounge with a friend for much longer than it should have taken, which was pretty bad. We did actually get it to work eventually and our matches were pretty smooth. It seems like there's a lot of difficulty finding matches because of what's probably a server-related issue.
About the controller issues, it's not impossible to play with your controllers, you'll just have to use something like xpadder. I use xinput so it hasn't really affected me though.

I like this game A LOT.. but I have to be objective and not let my preference to Street Fighter bias my review.
Summary: This game at it's core is a phenominal fighting game.  Miles ahead of SF4 in terms of gameplay.  The 16 character roster can be a turn off and the game lacks core features and game modes for offline casual players but hardcore players will be at home in their natural online environment especially when 8 player lobbies launch in March.
Expanded: Now I'm going to be very critical of this new Street Fighter title and go in-depth with my review.  This game is NOT worth $60.. at launch that is.  You will find the most barebones modes/features at launch with additional ones to be added around March and June.
-Story mode is not the Story mode you think it is.  It's basically a set of surprisingly short prequel stories that setup each character for the REAL Story mode that releases for free in June.  Most of these can be completed in 5-10minutes with 2-4 battles per character story against ai set on Toddler Easy mode (You cannot change this).  Yes, it's that short so say goodbye to 9 fights before fighting a boss like in other fighting games.  Alternate costumes can be unlocked here but since the in-game store is closed until March.. it's useless for now.
-Online for the most part is what you expect it to be.  Ranked and Casual matches all still here.  8 Player lobbies launch in March so not a long wait.  You will be spending most of your time here if you want a challenge.  The problem is.. the servers are crap even with multiple betas before release so until Capcom gets them fixed.. have fun wishing the game had more offline content at launch.
-Extra modes are in short supply here, March is when the more interesting content releases.  So no versus ai, in-game store, challenges or trials at launch.  We do have a very fun survival mode that has you earning points after every fight and spending them on refilling health, extra damage, extra defense, etc. It's a pretty cool 30 match mode.. until you get kicked off Capcom's servers mid-game and you have to restart from match 1 again. This mode grants you additional colors which can be used right away, no wait required.

Wow... there seems to already be a number of negative reviews for this game.
Here are my thoughts:
Is this game any good? Yes
Should I buy this game? Yes
Is there a lot of features missing? Yes
It should be remembered that Capcom are releasing content for this game gradually, this includes characters and features (story mode etc).
Do I agree with this? Yes and No
I should note at this point that I am in no way a Capcom fanboy.  I do not hold any developer/publisher above criticism, however I will give credit where credit is due.
(I've edited this review to include this) - Capcom seems to have forgotten an Arcade mode...that's pathetic Capcom, what were you thinking? Hopefully that gets included in the March update, if not then they really need to improve the online experience if that is what you are trying to push.
I agree with their character DLC model.  Having fewer characters initially allows for balancing, new players not to get overwealmed and for seasoned players to actually use the new characters and not just stick to Ken and Ryu.... You can unlock all extra characters by earning ingame currency or buy the season pass. Keep in mind that it is very easy and quick to get enough ingame currency to buy all the characters, doing all the prologues will get you more than enough for one.
The game does have some short prologues for each character (mentioned before) for you to play to get some basic character backgrounds, although to be honest, Capcom REALLY need to reboot the Street Fighter story line. the little that there is never made any sense although the Cammy story is really quite interresting.
The main Story Mode which will be a couple hours long apparently will be coming later, obvioulsy taking note of Mortal Kombats efforts.
Leaving this out and a couple other things makes the game feel a little unfinished, but I can get over that as the Online Mode does work for me as does my fight stick (Mad Catz Street Fighter 4 Collectors Edition for Xbox 360) however the online mode does on occasion (not always) seem stuttery.  Possibly due to latency, possibly to do with server strain, hard to say, probably a bit of both.
One of the features of SF5 that appealed to me was that PC and PS4 players can cross platform play meaning that someone playing on a PC can play against someone on a PS4.  I have pocked around the settings and I am assuming where it says HARDWARE: ANY this means that you will play against PS4 players as well but haven't been able to confirm this yet.
I understand a lot of people are having issues with compatability with thier controllers, which after reading some sites, looks like it's either been patched or is going to be patched as Capcom will be supporting legacy controllers.  I could'nt confirm this but I am assuming this only affected playstation sticks as my mine is an old Xbox 360 fight stick which worked during the Beta stages.
-----Conclusion-----
To round up, this is a great addition to the SF library
Solid gameplay
Good mix of characters with more to come
Online experience is a bit hit and miss and can seem like playing a flip book at times
PS4 vs PC cross platform (key feature for me)
However it is nowhere near the complete game...yet
I just hope that Capcom manage to iron out any bugs that their customers are reporting and do not drop support like WB/NRS did for MKX.

This is a good port of a superb arcade fighting game. Unlike its release on PS3, the PC version can be made compatible with 4:3 screens like CRTs, which is important because it is a native 480p game. In that respect the PS3 version was actually a downgrade from the previous PS2 title, Accent Core Plus, because it scaled everything up to 720p and forced you to use sidebars of some kind.
I would definitely recommend this over any of the console ports. The PC is compatible with more arcade sticks than any other platform, and you can run the game with any kind of display, which makes streaming and recording a breeze.
Keep in mind that this is a much more difficult game to master than BlazBlue or the newer Guilty Gear, Xrd. There are certain moves that require precision on the order of two or three frames, which is a very small interval at 60FPS. The era of internet play, wireless controllers, and laggy LCDTVs has made GGXXAC+R less relevant in the mainstream, but for shoulder-to-shoulder play, it simply cannot be beat.

Playing this game was quite an odd experience and I did quite enjoy it. The aesthetic is fantastic and the world building though small does give details that satisfy my interest. The Game was an hour long from start to finish with me playing it.
The Challenges were simple but they required reading into to find their solution so the game has that credit. One fault I did find when playing the game was the transitions during the action sequences being a little too sudden, Having to replay it over and over a few times due to their jerkyness. The Puzzles themselves didn't provide a consequence for failure and just allow you to try them again, For those who want to blaze through and miss the details in the objects you interact with. Which brings me to another point.
The Arrow to click continue sometimes obscured some of the text making it hard to read. It's still readable but it can be troublesome especially for those who may have a hard time reading the text.
A lack of options Menu really detracted from this game, As with my thoughts on the voice acting. I'd like to hear the songs proper themselves without voices in the way. Another feature I feel is missing that each scene could have a remove visor option as to view the entire scene without them obstructing the view As they do obstruct as much as the arrows over the text in some places.
The Price point for this game I feel at the time of writing ($8.00) Is a little steep for an short 1-2 hour experience but the experience is worth it for the brief time you play it feeling a bit like a good short story you'd be able to pick up in a book store.
Pros:

-Good atmosphere at specific parts of the story (Won't reveal much as to prevent spoilers)

Cons:

-The Credit Sequence (which honestly made me squirm a little due to the drastic change of style)

I feel it's a good introduction to the creator's career, But there is obviously room for improvement. I would reccomend this game for those who like a short story, If you can personally justify the price.

So long as you understand that the paid mod implementation here is not as mod developer friendly as it's shown at face value, it's a great game.
I'll preface this by saying that Bethesda and/or Zenimax are well within their rights to capitalize on mods as it is their content. So long as these mods are designed for their product, they can do with as they please. That said, however, this is a case of a wolf in sheeps clothing. It's a way for them to profit off mods under the guize of being "good" to the community of modders who have done what Bethesda hasn't; fix their game, as well as add a near invinite amount of content that can keep you busy for years to come.
Mods can be browsed, searched, downloaded, managed, and donated to with external applications, Nexus, for one example. If you truly want to support the
the best way to do si is donations directly to them.
Now, as for the game itself:
I come from a mixed history with Fallout. My first Venture into the Fallout universe was Fallout 2. It was a game I played in passing. I don't believe I ever finished it.
When Fallout 3 rolled around a decade later, I was excited to see that it had taken from an isometric RPG to a first or third person shooter. The blending of RPG and shooter elements was done well, but it was a game that took me a very, very long time to get into. It wasn't until New Vegas was released some years later that I had to force myself to finish 3. The game world felt dull to me, it felt "samey", go here do A, Go there do B, Go back and do A again, it just felt mundane. I pushed through and finished the game, and in retrospect, I find that while it will never be the best game i've ever played, I largely enjoyed my time. The pace and monotany of the game picked up the further I went along.
New Vegas is a game that, to this day, I still have issues with. Some people love this game, some people hate it, some are indifferent. I fall into the camp of people who did not like this game at all. like 3, I had to force myself to play the game, and looking back on it, I did not enjoy it. I found it to be incredibly boring, I felt as though the world was uninspired, and it felt very clunky and haphazardly put together.
Fallout 4 rolled by, and I held off on purchasing it until I got some feedback from friends, particularly those that didn't like New Vegas. It got positive vibes from them, so I took the plung about two weeks post-launch. I'm glad I did. I got in, found the gameplay to be much more tight than its predecessors. I didnt' feel like a floating being running through empty space. The story sucked me in, if not fairly generic, I found myself progressing through the core s tory and getting naturally sidetracked by things I found interested in doing. None of the side content felt forced. The world created felt genuine. It felt as though the living beings, good, bad, or otherwise played a role in the world. My actions felt as though they carried weight. I ran the game through its paces, completed the core story, and continued to want to venture into the world to see what I hadn't yet discovered.
As the DLC's rolled out, I progressed through those as well. Far Harbor is by far the best of the Bethesda-created post-launch content this game has to offer. Nuka World was a colossal letdown. I progressed through the core story, making choices that I felt correct, in a little under 45 minutes. everything else felt like padding, fetch quests, hide-and-seek, ETC. Much mroe forced that the original content the game provided.
Do I recommend this game? Yes.
Do I recommend modding this game? If you avoid the paid-mods supported directly through the game. There's a mod community out there that have overhauled this game because they love it, not because they want to make a "quick" buck. They offer their work free of charge; you're welcomed to download it completely free, or donate to them if you enjoy their content (which I do encourage)
Do I recommend DLC? Yes (if you enjoy the base game), with the caveat that you not purchase the Season Pass. I do not believe that Nuka World adds any sustainable value to the game, and as such, the season pass should not be considered a "value" option.

Boy oh boy, finally finished the game for the first time, mind you, no new game+ content have grazed this review yet, but still there is a lot to say about this one, so settle down, grab some refreshments and thank you ahead of time if you devote the time to read this one. Oh, and I will do my hardest to keep this spoiler free, though some areas, characters etc. I might mention could be considered as spoilers as well, so you've been warned.
Starting with the combat, graphics, setting, characters and of course a bit of the story.
Combat - I'd dare to say it's the best out of the tales series so far, the combat here is the polished, it feels smooth, responsive, intuitive and most of all fun. And if you are the kind of a player who can't stick with something for too long, worry not my friend, for you can switch between all six of your party members with each of them comes a completely different playstyle, Velvet is swift and brutal and if built right almost unkillable, Rokurou is mobile and his skill ceiling is considerably higher as his mechanic completely depends on countering his opponents and you can imagine, should you mistime your counter, your face will be quickly smashed by probably a fairly heavy and possibly a sharp object. Aizen is slower and like a proper earth seraph he hits excessively hard, Eleanor is there with all her poking utencils and of course Phi and Magilou for some smashing spell funsies. Long story short there is something to keep you engaged in the combat for ridiculously long time. I imagine mastering every character might take you closer to probably 200 maybe 300 hours as they all learn new artes at all times.
Speaking of artes, you can rebind them, THANK THE LORD AND SAVIOR OUR ETERNAL EMPYREAN, effectively allowing you to pick and choose and tailor each button to a specific combination of attacks you want. As per usual you are not bound to your 4-attacks-and-done mechanic, as you can effectively cancel out of every and any attack to keep your combos going and you are actively encouraged to do so, for damage bonuses make the combat feel all that much more satisfying with those big damage numbers.
As far as equipment goes... well... hundreds upon hundreds of things to equip and master, as well as fashion items which you can either get as DLCs (highly recommend the pirate one), you can also get them through exploring in-game. Outside of combat there are minigames to sink your teeth into for some freebies and bragging rights, which I found a little more fun than they have any right to be to be perfectly honest. You can also send your ship full of swashbuckling pirates to scavenge the sea and bring you the ever so rare items, recipes and ingredients for your delightful cookbook, who knew eating a good lunch could revive you from the dead, or make enemies cough up that sword you always wanted.
Graphics - First thing first, this game is vast, huge, big, girthy. With tons of areas to explore and as many will probably expect the graphics of anyone outside of our protagonists and the baddies might not be that great, yes you might be right, the regular citizens around are nothing exceptional to look at, but certain areas you can get to explore literally made me stop and first look and appreciate the scenery. From far reaching green pastures to beatiful caves with shiny crystals everywhere(some of which will try to pound you into the ground) to absolutely peerless and beautiful beaches and coral areas. Whilst it's not the main focus, some places have a lot of charm to them and definitely aid the idea of you living in a pretty world, which you will completely destroy in your quest for reve- no? Okay...
Characters - Surprisingly in this game, characters actually have... well... character, which is more than I can say for quite a few modern games out there today. You will be introduced to them and grow to like them, probably, through a little conversation segments presented in a visual novel style as well as actual cutscenes done with the ingame engine. Some of them more serious than others, some outright ridiculous, aka Aizen smashing Rokurou in the gut to check whether he is not dreaming, you will get it once you see it, it's a gem not to be forgotten. And I have to mention as well, both, the japanese and surprisingly, the english dub are excellently done, for the most part at least. The one thing I do have a tiny gripe with is the 20-feet-stop-walk syndrome, where you will go through a conversation, walk 20 feet aaaand there is another one. But don't worry that happened only a few times across the entire game and for some, it won't even be a problem.
Story - The story is great
...
...
...
What? I told you no spoilers. Alrighty then, how to describe it then...hmm... Right. The thing this game is doing right (or maybe wrong) with its story is that you effectively have no idea how close you are to the end of it, until, that is, the very end of it. There were many times where I thought, damn it's ending already, only to be proven wrong and the game would keep on going. And I guess I should also mention, if you do happen to enjoy JRPGs such as this one and don't mind the anime style (Can we finally stop judging games based on their looks? Please?), I'm happy to tell you, this game will not dissapoint you with its ending, so much so, it might tug on a few heartstrings. If you are the kind to get attached to this band of misfits, many girly and manly tears, let's not judge, will be shed.
So to sum it up, I'd like to thank you, if you've managed to read this far in and would also heartily recommend you to get this gem of a game, as it is truly one of the best Tales game, if not the best right now. Now if you excuse me, I have myself a new game+ to tackle.

As someone who harbors a ticklespot for scatalogical humor, I found myself giggling right away.
And then when I read some of the outraged, disgusted reviews of this game it made me laugh harder. To think there are adults just waiting for their chance to denounce other adults because they still find the crude simplicity of poop jokes funny.
As if deriving any kind of good nature from a bowel movement or a fart is immediate grounds for being stripped of all noble status or perceived brilliance.
And yet any well-read person will know that toilet humor appears in the works of Shakespeare; King Lear, Comedy of Errors, Othella, Two Gentleman From Verona are just a few examples. In Aristophanes' THE CLOUDS, a character describes his bowel movements to Socrates as thunder passing through him. Highly celebrated author Jonathon Swift wrote an entire pamphlet on the benefit of flatulence.
There's even a story in 1001 Arabian Nights Tales of a man who flees his wedding after letting out a long, noticeable fart at the ceremony. If that doesn't strike your ancient fancy, in Dante Alighieri's THE INFERNO, near the end of chapter XXI, we're told of a demon mobilizing his army by using his butt as a trumpet.
So if you're one of the special little snowflakes who hates this game because it dares to use bodily functions as a comedic template, then my advice is not to have children. Like, ever. Seriously. Don't procreate. You'll hate yourself for having to change diapers and your child will resent you for growing up in a household where they aren't allowed to laugh when somebody farts.

A short review for my favorite VN series
Sono Hanabira ni Kuchizuke o or A Kiss for the Petals is a pure yuri visual novel series by Fuguriya. This game in particular is a prequel to the untranslated story of the Miya x Risa VNs. In the theme of the previous VNs the characters and their interaction with each other are adorable. However, Unlike most of the VNs in the series this game is NOT R-18. The game has a stellar translation by MangaGamer as it is in the same vein that the fan translations are in both style and phrasing (without all the grammar and spelling errors). One of the greatest shooters ever.
Pros:
-Looks great for its time. Some 3D models have been upgraded to a more detailed design.
-Sounds are incredible even by today's standards
-Everything runs and feels ultra smooth and responsive
-Awesome level design where interesting and unexpected things keep happening
-Interesting and varied enemy and weapons selection
-Great level of detail: shootouts create a glorious mess of the environment. Many objects are destructible. There's red and green blood all over the place, and enemies also often blow up into little pieces of meat that fly all over the place. Overall, the immersion is extremely solid, even if the game does not have "proper" rigid body physics model.
-CHALLENGING!! Much more so than most newer shooters, including Half-Life 2
-Awesome soundtrack that kicks in during nice moments
-No hardware problems while running the game on a modern system
-While the game has an FPS cap, it is set at 100, which is great considering some new games get released with an FPS cap of 60 or even 30
-Fun multiplayer deathmatch, games with live players can still be found!
Cons:
-On Hard difficulty level some enemies can feel slightly bullet-spongy. Human enemies can take an unrealistic amount of punishment from some weapons, as can the player himself. This seems to be a design choice, but I feel having a larger number of weaker enemies, or making the player weaker, would have been a better choice to increase difficulty.
-Graphically outdated by 2017 standards
-No rigid body physics modeling, as the technology didn't exist at the time of release
-Hand grenade physics could be described as funky
-No bullet holes on enemies :(

Like driving games? You could do a lot worse.
There are races, but it's heaviest on exploration: it's set in an open world, and jumps, missions, shortcuts, and secrets are strewn about all over the city. Billboards, for example. You'll see one above you as you drive past and then poke around to puzzle out which ramp you have to jump off of to break it. And none of the races have boundaries, so you can get to the finish line however you like. If you can figure out a quicker route, you'll have a significant advantage. (I was checking my map a lot.)
There are trick runs and destruction derbies in addition to races. There's a lot of crashing in this game, but when you're the one taking other cars down, it is supremely satisfying. Crunch. Sometimes unlockable cars speed past you on the road and you can follow them and smash them to add them to your collection, which is cool.
The voice-acting is...not bad, actually. "DJ Atomica" is about what I'd expect from a real-life radio show host, chiming in with brief hints in between songs. In fact, he's probably better than some of the real-life DJs I've listened to. Maybe I just listen to crappy radio stations. Either way, he can be disabled if he gets annoying.
On the downside, you crash a lot--or at least I do--which can be frustrating. When you do, it goes into slow-motion and gives you a close-up view of how your car is destroyed; stylistically, it looks nice, but it gets tiresome quickly, and I wish I could turn it off.
The "Ultimate Box" part doesn't work. It's just the base game. I guess they didn't program it in or something? I'm told there's a fan-made patch to fix this issue.
I got it cheap in the Humble Bundle; I am satisfied with the value I got.
TL;DR: Driving game. Polished, but nothing atypical.

After being in early access for roughly more than two and a half years, Chucklefish has decided that Starbound's version number is 1.0 - the fully finished product. Unfortunately, another 20-something hours does not show an honest effort put in for those seeking adventure.
From the last time I reviewed the game, the basic gameplay loop remains mostly unchanged except for a few changes at the start of the game to accomodate for its 'tutorial phase' and story. The loop starts with gathering a planet's available materials and metals to help get yourself various crafting stations and some sufficient kit and especially armor, because it practically decides not only how tanky you are but also how much damage you do.
The difference at this point is that the main quest also wants the player to find settlements of a specific race and scan certain scattered decorative objects, demonstrating the game's feature where your character's race influences the remarks they have about them. After that, an instanced mission is given to retrieve a MacGuffin from the race, including a mandatory boss fight in each as well. And then you're asked to do the same thing but for another race that is supposedly easier to find on a different type of planet or galaxy that's a tier up, restarting the loop since your old armor won't do you much good and you can't just 'jump' a tier without the materials to survive the specific atmosphere of later planets.
Another big thing thrown in the loops are settlements, which provide a never-ending supply of terribly simple, generated quests asking you to fetch items, talking to NPCs that are very close by, or killing something on the other side of the planet; just as awful as Skyrim's radiant quests. Thankfully they share another purpose in that you can practically freeload from their containers without consequence, giving you an alternate means of obtaining some materials than just digging deep down. And of course, why you can do this just raises more questions. The shops do at least provide a source from where you can get armor from other races, though.
One big thing Chucklefish has never seemed to really address since the beginning of the beta are planets. You know there is a problem when the setting allows for all kinds of crazy worlds to exist, and yet are much less diverse than Earth. For those unfamiliar, Starbound practically treats planets as single biomes (before settlements/bases), such as dedicated forest, desert, ice, ocean, and even volcanic worlds. These are quite literally are what they're advertised as, and the smaller sub-biomes that do exist are mostly there for wacky visual flair like trees with eyes and so only provide little different use compared to the primary biome's resources, so something like a beach or ocean will still only be found on an ocean planet. All planets aren't so different underground and actually do share many of the same sub-biomes regardless of the planet's type, so it can get repetitive there too. For such an important aspect of the game, world generation is seriously neglected.
The game also runs quite poorly overall.
Ultimately, not only development has been thin and slow overall, but Starbound is also a victim of having no real design plan for many game mechanics since the start. Much of these two and a half years of early access have been wasted on trying to redesign how various game systems are handled multiple times along with adding and even removing content (racial bonuses, temperature, and a lot of craftable weapons) to the ire of others. The one major new thing - the main story, is an unremarkable 'an ancient evil awakens' plot that has clearly been rushed out especially around near the end, so the devs could call the game 1.0.
Players who like to do many vanity things might find Starbound alright, but if you are looking for a more technically impressive 'Terraria but in space' kind of game, you will be sorely disappointed. Until Chucklefish steps it up with a huge update or an ambitious modding project blows off everybody's socks, Starbound right now is a large waste of potential that could have been more.

Early Access is over, and Mr. "1000+ hours of playing TDM" has a word for YOU!
First of all, I love racing games. Since Ridge Racer for PS1 I am addicted to good racing games. I played season and season in F1'97. Gran Turismo 1+2, of course. Weeks of playing Ferrari F355 Challenge online on SEGA Dreamcast. F1 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 from Codemasters. Project CARS, iRacing and many many more. I would say, over 10000 hours all together.
More practise in virtual racing than every 'real' driver on track. So what do I think about TDM?
I've bought it in early access phase, 29th May 2015. Played a lot and helped sorting out the bugs. Giving some ideas (like the qualifying in cup mode). It was very nice. Eating in front of the PC was a regular meal.
Then there was release day. Everyone was online. Matches filled with up to 12 players. Most of the time lag-free. Very great races.
How does it feel in comparison to project CARS, for example?
Both are competitive racing games. In TDM you don't need a steering wheel, don't have to learn the basics about racing or 30+ tracks. You just buy your first car and go on track. Very few buttons to play the game. But very addictive gameplay, if you match up with competitive players.
After the release, they changed something and you don't match up to a lot of players, even when a lot of players are in-game. But we communicate over steam and invite each other for cup races. And if you want to farm money for a new car, just go for bot races. You will need $14.000.000 to get all cars with all upgrades.
Long-term-fun?
Yes. I did it (buy all 6 cars) for three times now (2x early access and after release).
Is this game for racers?
Yes, and like every racing game, it is JUST for racers. Managers will go away very quickly.
What is the graphics like?
It suits the game. And the price. Go on YouTube and check some videos.
Tell me about the bugs!
We had a lot of detected bugs in ea and I have to say, the worst bugs are gone. And you can work around the most existing bugs. Which expands the gameplay (where to overtake at pit entry, sponsors patching and so on).
How much is it worth?
That's your own decision. I've read bad reviews with 2,5 hours of total play time.
I've played 1000+ hours now. And at the actual state it is worth €20-25 to me.
Maybe you should see this game as a slot racer. With 6 available tracks and 16 cars in race. Overtaking isn't easy and you have to stay calm even when a bot blocks you for half a lap - and then pits!
Sponsors aren't fun, but you have to make more money!
And please forget about the management part. It is just, but a very different racing game.

At the time of writing, Blackwake boasts 5 official ships, 7 different maps (with different weather conditions to spice things up), 15 weapons, 5 special items, 3 main game modes, and 50 unlockable cosmetics to dress up as a pirate.
New content is added all the time, on a monthly to weekly basis. Future content apparently will include a bomb ship, a Coastal Fortress Siege game mode, and more.
Pros: Unique game, there's nothing else out there like Blackwake. Great music and voice acting. Fun team-focused gameplay. You can play in any server, no matter the ping, due to client-side lag compensation. Entertaining weapons like Spyglass and Nockgun. Developers seem very dedicated to making their dream a reality in this game. Boarding in Blackwake is one of the most exciting things in video games. YARRRRR!
Cons: Lacking polish in the animations and features. Occasionally buggy. Melee system is the most exciting part of the game, but broken as all hell.
