I almost stopped playing this game after a few hours, but am glad I didn't. After a fairly hype intro area, the start of the game has the worst dungeons in the entire game (repetitive indoor corridors in underground mines and dungeons), you're limited in your moves and abilities so combat is bland, and you only have a handful of characters in your party.
Thankfully, things gradually improve and the game really hits its stride after getting the 6th playable character. Once you unlock more of the gameplay (switch blasts, mystic artes, certain items that reward you for chaining battles without saving,  and more skills to chain) combat is a ton of fun. Once you get the hang of dodging, finding weak points, and comboing, the combat feels great. The equipment/enhancement/skill system is interesting and rewards idiots like me who love grinding in JRPGs. Enemies are varied, and even though there's a lot of palette swaps used there still feels like a lot of enemies (and even the palette swaps have different skills, weaknesses and item drops). Boss fights are fun and memorable.
The plot is bland, but the characters themselves are a lot of fun, thanks in no small part due to the excellent English voice acting. Skits let you see the characters play off each other, often for offbeat things (like Magilou putting together a comedy act) which helps develop them. You can also play dress-up with them which is always a plus. The game is long, too. My playtime is inflated (because there's minor in-game unlocks for stuff like "idle in the menu for 50 hours", and I'm dumb) but doing the main story and extras at a normal pace will run about 70 hours. Prepare to spend 150+ hours if you want to grind for equipment mastery.
Graphics run at 4k 60fps flawlessly on my GTX 1080. They're done in a pleasant, colorful anime style, though again, this doesn't show for the first few hours; the starting area is nice to look at, but then you're stuck in bland, monochrome mines for the next few hours. Later dungeons look great though; in particular the beach/lagoon dungeons and final dungeon look great. Character and enemy graphics are great.
For a minor but important gripe, the game really punishes you as not playing as Velvet, as she's absurdly broken in the hands of the player, but the AI will just use her abilities incorrectly and die horribly. Odds are you'll either want to play as Velvet or move her out of the party when playing as different characters. And you should play as different characters, as that's a lot of the fun in the game.
Pros:
+ Fun battle system with lots of equipment to find, enemies to fight, and skills to learn
+ Memorable and enjoyable cast of characters
+ Great English VA
+ Graphics are nice to look at; facial animations well done
+ Few technical issues (had one crash over ~200 hours of play)
Cons:
- Really slow start; game doesn't pick up until 6-10 hours in
- Some dungeons, particularly the early ones, are bland
- Movement speed is slow, takes a long time to traverse anywhere
- Battle system isn't explained very well in game
- Mouse is bugged in the combat system, better to use a controller or keyboard
- Unmemorable music
Overall this is worth a buy if you want to scratch a JRPG itch.

(this will be a sort of long review, bear with me if you're interested in this game)
Tales of Berseria, Tales of Berseria, Tales of Berseria
this is easily the BEST modern era tales game that i've ever played, and I've played most (close to all) tales games. Let's dive into this a little further.
for people who've played Tales of Zestiria, this is a no brainer. This game is a continuation and actually answers plot holes created by Zestiria. I won't go into details on how they fill these plot holes, or when it takes place, but know that this game improves on all aspects that Zesteria introduced from story to gameplay to aesthetics to character dynamics.
now if you haven't played Zestiria, have no fear. This game's learning curve is very low and the controls are very forgiving. it's a great place to start and really join the tlaes JRPG fanbase! The characters are all really dynamic and relatable, and the controls are pretty easy to grasp. Pretty crisp and great attention to details, lots of adventures to have, commanding your own ship fleet, collecting items in towns and dungeon, unique bosses and monsters etc. It's an easy pick up for teenagers and adults alike! The writing in this game is fantastic.
Lets actually talk about the writing for a second. MOST tales games are these happy go lucky experiences where the main character is this ball of idealism that seriously rubs people the wrong way. You know the type: the overachieving try hards that are like "bro stop for a minute". This game is sincerely different. It's the first game in my opinion that truly is "dark". Murder and vengence and revenge and those themes are all tied to each of the characters in some ways, and are even their motivation to cotinue with their daily lives.
In short. If you want to get into the tales series but don't know where to start, but dont have the equipment to play the "classics" like Symphonia, this is a great place to start.
if you want a better zestiria in practically all ways, this is an amazing place to start.
if you want a refined tales game with much darker themes, you will get EXACTLY that.
I have very little criticism for this game: there are tons of aesthetic DLC, and the developers give you 5  sets of bonus items to help your adventure from medicine to crafting (yes crafting) items. The crafting is so much easier to understand and is incredibly rewarding.
This is a great game. Buy it.

shows i have almost 80 hours in ToB, that's with a a complete game, all side quests, the end game dungeon, and finished grade farming for ng+.
I think at this point i have a good idea of the game.
the Tales series has a reputation of being a hit and miss beast. For every Symphonia, there's an Abyss. Luckily this game is the former, and i'd say it's actually my favourite game in the series.
The gameplay is really strong here, this game is in the same universe as Zestiria, so a lot of the same elements are applied, however the best feature of Zestiria's combat, the armatisation isnt here, in it's place are the importance of Break souls, making the player sacrifice combo stamina for guard breaks and hp. It's a nice system that makes the main character at least have a risk reward system of high  power at a cost. I really enjoyed the difficulty of the game, even if chaotic is stupid at the start of the game.
The writing is actually the tightest in the series in my opinion, and not just the story,it's little writing is quirky and adds a lot of character to the game. there isn't a bad character (once you get past the garish character designs) and each go on an interesting arc that keeps you engaged in them. Usually in Tales games i dread watching the skits, but here it works. The voice acting is also pretty tight, I gave both the Japanese and english voices a chance and found myself enjoying the dub a lot more. the delivery was perfect. Not to mention the individual story elements and characters, the game is generally well made.
The story, as i said, is quite good too. It's pretty self absorbed in that it does tend to refer to zestiria a little too much, but the strong antagonist gives the game flow where you don't feel like you're just doing random stuff. I don't wanna get into too much, but there's a lot of serious overtones in the story that gel well with it's world, like slavery, the cost of human life, and so on, it doesn't take itself TOO seriously, though, and all it's ethical questions are cemented in the story.
To cut it short, it's probably the best made tales game, there's a few complaints though. It's camera is quite shoddy, as is usual with tales games, and it's postgame is really lacking, one quest per character and a dungeon doesnt really keep you occupied for long.
It's a solid 8/10.

IN ITS CURRENT STATE
Game concept             7/10            Not Original, but many unique parts
Graphics                     7/10            one of the best out there for a manager
Game stability             2/10            Pretty awful, completly unplayable at times
Matchmaking              0/10             It doesnt exist, no really, theres a raking system, but the game doesnt compute it in any way shape or form when matching players.
The game has a lot of potential, and if you want to support a decent go at a racing team manager game drop the 20$ by all means.
As it stands right now, the server instability absolutely kills about half the races run. In a game where split second decisions cost you wins/top 5's having server latency issues as often as it does makes the game near unplayable at times.
The races where the server doesn't lag, you are always matched against players with a lot more invested into thier team. EX:  I've had a top 25 world player in just about all of my first 14 races, which makes it nigh impossible for a win, or a top 5, just finishing above mid pack is pretty good. I'm not sure if this is due to not enough players to populate more races or just a completely non-implemented matchmaking system.
If you don't mind losing, trying to figure out the game while racing vs fully invested teams, and you love to beat your face into the keyboard grinding 1.5k a race to maybe have a chance a month or so down the road, this games for you.
There is a sick satisfaction when you actually finish a race though, kind of like...wow did anyone really just witness that whole race completing with minimal lag, and some actually decent racing?!
The devs seem to care about the game and community and have been trying to fix the server issues, but until something drastic changes the game does not have a big enough draw to keep this gamer playing through the L...La.......Laggggg.

EDIT 3/11/2017
Please don't misinterpret my review. I'm not angry about anything. I had a lot of fun within the first hour of gameplay but it ended up being the same thing over and over again.
I stated in the review that I know it's early access, and knowing that, it will obviously be missing some features.  However at the same time, there is never a guarantee that developers will continue with a game, as stated in the "Early Access" description.
The point of early access is so you can get a feel of how a game will turn out. My review was only so developers could have an idea of what some people would like to have implemented in their game.
Sadly, steam only allows you to recommend or not recommend a game. That is why I marked it as 3/5. The repetitive concept is something that deterred me from continuing to play.
I'm looking forward for the future of this game. I've learned from past experiences to never get hyped up for a game, so that is why I refunded. As more content comes out, I'd be glad to check it out again. But for now, I will this game refunded in case I dislike it in the future. When more things come out that I would like, I'll consider buying this game again.
I understand that people would be upset by this review -- but it was not written in any way to insult the game at its current state, nor the developers. It was simply written to encourage developers to think about more features, as I am sure they already are, as well as address other issues within the game.
Developers -- this was a great game. Keep doing what you are doing. I'm looking forward to playing this in the future. I know I marked this as something I would not recommened -- but that is simply due to the repetitive structure of it, and so that you guys can notice what parts of the game you should improve on. This game plays much in the same vein as the formidable Artemis Bridge Simulator or the once great fun Guns Of Icarus (Which has since become really bad due to incompetent developers) with some often requested additions in it.
Generally you will join a crew of one of three ships on either the British Empires or the undefined "Pirate" side. As of this early alpha review, two types of ships exist - the large, multi-deck Galleon and the smaller, more maneuverable Frigate. Pitted in an Arena against each other, it is your job to work well with your fellow crewmen as well as the other ships in your fleet to defeat the enemy. Your work consists of reloading cannons, putting out fires, repairing various broken ship components, pumping out water and, in the case of the captain of the ship, steering the damn thing into advantageous positions.
So far so simple, but what makes this game great is not only the very tongue-in-cheek community (Expect long sessions of everyone talking like a pirate regularly) but also the various forms of playing the game. Don't like your captain? Call for a mutiny! Bored of just shooting at your enemy? Board them and engage in fistycuffs! Want to try something completely different? Ask your captain to let you off at the nearest island and declare it yours!
This simple concept really lends itself to a ton of fun, and the final cherry on top is the developers being genuinely interested, friendly and motivated people who seemingly REALLY just want to create the most fun experience you can think of.

EDITED: June 2017 (I keep this review up to date as the game evolves)
This game is definitely becoming a full fledged AAA title.
When this game first came out I wrote a review not recommending this game. It simply had too many flaws for its retail price. Later, as the game improved, I changed my review to a cautious recommendation. With the latest update fixing a number of my remaining issues with the game and the lowering price I now strongly recommend this game. The developers don't just sound committed to making changes for the better, they've actually gone and taken them and so I'm excited to see it continue improving.
THE PROS:
+ Very strong fighting game at its core, and it always has been. SFV looks and feels as intense to play as it does to watch. Matches are fast, momentum can easily shift, and victory is never a foregone conclusion.
+ The game is far easier to pick up than previous Street Fighter titles. The game is extremely lenient with inputs and even the most difficult combos in the game can be mastered with a few minutes in training mode. How well you do has less to do with grinding muscle memory and more to do with your knowledge of matchups and tactics.
+ The cast is varied and balanced. This is not a game with strong tier lists. The initial roster is packed with straight forward characters with familiar mechanics while many of the DLC characters have been quite experimental. The way it seems to work is that DLC characters are initially released but tweaked a little weaker than the rest of the cast and then in the next balance patch, once the developers see how people are using those characters, they tweak them up to be equal with the others.
+ The game comes with a semi-helpful tutorial for general play and for each character. It's not in the same league as the Skullgirls tutorial but it's not totally absent and can get a new player started with enough to not completely drown.
+ The Capcom Fighters Network feature now has full functionality. You can view a wide range of stats about your own play with and against each character, friend and blacklist other players, and searching for other players in your skill range is easier than before.
+ Now contains 20 trials for each character (except Ed and all future DLC, who only have 10, because they now appear to be releasing trials by season).
THE CONS:
- In local versus player 2's menus might not be all that you would expect.
- Battle Lounges now support up to 8 players but still feel like an incomplete mess. The "chat box" can only be filled with premade messages chosen from a list and it is impossible to sort through Battle Lounges by region, connection, characters, or give them any sort of useful titles to attract particular types of players.
- Survival is one of the most infuriating RNG-based ♥♥♥♥♥hows ever attached to a video game. However, it is no longer required to obtain alternate colors. Still, feel no shame in using mods to beat this without effort or just don't play it at all.

Update 2/18
Updating this review now that many server issues have been addressed.
Pros:
Looks Great: No frame rate issue from my computer. Game looks nice
Plays Well: If you played USF4 then you kinda know what your getting into. Game on the surface feels similar but the more you play the more the difference come out.
Lots of promise: Capcom is looking to support this game long term and there are 6 characters promised. No matter how you feel about the pay/grind gate, this game looks like its going to have a lot of characters and be supported for a while, and hey, that costs money guys.
The game shows hope now but still needs time. Its a fun play but...
Cons:
Long loading time for online play: Once you find an oppenent the game will essentailly freeze for about 20 -30 seconds sometimes a bit longer before launching you into online match.
Matching can(rarely for me) be a bit laggy: Honestly not a huge problem for me but occasionally you will come against someone who seems to have bad internet and they'll lag. Seems better then SF4 though.
Online Lobbys 2 Man until March: Probably for server stability or otherwise haven't built out all the features yet but online lobbies are limited to 2 people. There is not spectator option. Only really a problem if you have a bunch of friends you want to play with.
Limited Single Player Options: The story is not yet fully completed will take about 2 hours to complete all the missions for all 16 characters. After that your left with survival and training. Survival is just match after match and is used to unlock bonus colors, and training is training.
Over all I think the game shows some promise. Given a few months the game will be filled out and it most if not all my complaints will be address. I'll try and remember to update this review in march.

"Give in to your guilty pleasures and start fighting for Heaven or Hell in the best version of Guilty Gear X2."
Guilty Gear X2 Accent Core Plus is the definitive version of all things Guilty Gear X2 related. And trust me; there is plenty of stuff related to GGX2. For the record, I don't count Guilty Gear Isuka as part of the Guilty Gear X2 re-releases. I don't care how many A.B.A. fans I upset when I say that, either. After Guilty Gear X2's initial release, fighting game fans got hit with plenty of remakes of Arc System's crazy chaos combat contest. Thus, you might be wondering if you should bother picking up this game. Well, yes, you should. Look at it this way: do you want the most up to date character roster, the most balanced move set, the most information regarding the Guilty Gear mythos and the most modes alongside the classic arcade and versus? Of course you do! Anyone can see that GGX2ACP is the game to get for those who want the most out of the world of Guilty Gear. Trust me when I say that there is plenty of “most” for everyone.
Those new to Guilty Gear might be a bit lost in terms of story. The cast of Guilty Gear is eccentric and wild; the types of people you want to hang around with at a party. Due to the aggressive and dangerous nature of Gears, bounty hunters and The Sacred Order of the Holy Knights alike waged a century long war to end the existence of all Gears. Tournaments have been held in the past to extinguish any remaining Gears and the ruler of all Gears: Justice. In doing so, the victors are granted money. Lots and lots money. That's the basic premise behind the Guilty Gear world, but the characters and their eccentricities are what make the game so special. There are no Ryu/Ken types here, thankfully. Instead, you have a huge cast you'd never expect to find. There is Bridgette, a transvestite who fights with yo-yos, stuffed animal and roller blades. There is also Slayer, a vampire with more power than a generator that controls a continent. Seriously, he blocks attacks with smoke from his pipe! We also have the beautiful Millia Rage, an assassin trained to use her gorgeous hair as a weapon. All of your favorites are back and one of the draws of Guilty Gear Accent Core Plus is the fact that two fan favorite characters have joined the roster: Kliff and Justice. While these overpowered jerks are rarely used in normal play or in tournaments, it's still great to see familiar faces and have such a huge variety of characters. With the up to date story mode, you can find out more about each unique character as they battle the entities known as Gears and the mysterious figure known only as “That Man.” All characters have multiple endings in their story modes. Since each arc is short, you can see different sides of the tale.
Alongside Story Mode, there is a new Survival Mode that allows you to level up your characters as you battle the computer. You can also play the regular Arcade, Training, Versus, M.O.M, Versus Computer and Two-vs.-Two Modes. Accent Core Plus will let you go on-line provided you have the proper PS2 attachments. Once a mode is picked, you select a character and once a character is picked, the fun begins again. The fighting is as hectic as ever yet still retains the familiarity of all of the predecessors. Characters have a variety of attacks, skills and the potential to chain them all together to create impressive combos that demand respect. All characters have strengths and weaknesses, but knowing how each character performs will lead to huge combos and a better understanding of how to battle other opponents. As usual, there is plenty to offer in Accent Core Plus in terms of strategy that goes beyond a standard combo. Techniques such as Faultless Defense, Roman Cancelling, False Roman Cancelling (more on those in a minute) and others are needed to fully get the most out of the fighting. All in all, fighting is a blast. The computer controlled AI does not pull any punches even on the easier difficulty settings. Practice makes perfect when it comes to picking a character that's right for you. This leads me to my biggest complaint about the game: the lack of a good practice mode. Sure, Training Mode gives you some options but it would have been nice to include a mode that gives you hints about the basics of 2D fighting, combo ideas and strategies. Considering this is the best version of Guilty Gear X2, an extra mode would have helped to sell the package and set it apart from the other releases. One of the good things that the Training Mode offers is that it allows you to learn the input of executing a False Roman Cancel. False Roman Cancels, or FRCs, allow you to stop most attacks mid-animation and either follow up with an impressive combo or dash away in case an attack missed. They're very important, but also very trick to learn. Since all characters have different FRCs, learning the timing for each of them will take effort. However, this effort is worth it and it was a good move on Arc's part to include the FRC practice feature.
Despite the lack of a more involved Training Mode, there are some great things to point out that you can only find in Accent Core Plus: bonus material. As you complete the various challenges, you'll unlock stunning artwork. Fans know that the illustrations in Guilty Gear have always been amazing and what better way to see them than as a reward for winning a tough match? Get ready to see the Game Over screen and hit the start button while a countdown begins. Luckily, the rewards for your troubles are well worth it. Once again, anime is the central theme in the graphics department. Animations and scenery look like they should: excellent and full of vivid details. The rock and roll inspired soundtrack is back in full swing, as well. For those of you that buy the game new, you will get the OST on a separate disc so you can rock out with your...well...you know....when not playing Guilty Gear. Finally, all of the voice acting is in Japanese.
The best thing about Guilty Gear X2 Accent Core Plus is that it has everything a fan of the series could want with just enough extra stuff to set it apart from other remakes of X2. To me, the best part is the free soundtrack. However, even without it, this is still an excellent 2D fighting game from a legendary franchise. Overall: This game was super fun. There's a lot of interesting stories with each of the characters. Solid character development. Nice world, and pretty good graphics. I loved the combat, although it does become a bit tedious when you have solid combos laid out. In combat, you get punished for mistakes and can be a bit reliant on RNG for stuns or other ailments.
(POSSIBLE SPOILERS)
My biggest complaint with this game is how massive the dungeons are. It got to the point where I encountered a new dungeon and thought, "Oh boy how long will it take me to get across this place." and the use of Geoboard didn't improve that to much.
The story was awesome and I wanted to keep playing to see how the story turned out and what not. Quite tragic, but a very compelling and entertaining story with some sweet themes. Although the themes are kind of shoved into your face, but still nice themes none the less. The character development in the game was spot on. As the game progresses you can get a feel to how everyone in the party is growing on one another and the party dynamics. You literally see a character go from mindless drone to someone making their own choices about what they want to do and how. You see how characters influence one another in decision making. The party goes from rag tag group of random people, to an established group in which each person helps out one other in some way. Each character grew in their own way, and after doing lots of side quests, some even found closure in their lives. or accepted parts about them they didn't like and stuff of the sort. It's quite inspirational.
Combat wise: as I said before can become tedious, but feels awesome when you unlock new abilities that link with previous combos more effectively and what not. Mystic Artes felt awesome to use especially when you get extra damage on the hits. Getting an over 60k damage Mystic Arte felt amazing, sometimes a little difficult to achieve, but felt so rewarding. Although as Velvet I found myself just spamming a couple different combos, it didn't matter what type of enemy it was, I could just spam 2 different combo strings over and over and win every time as long as I got a little lucky and relcaimed souls from stunning and what not. I would just break soul every time Velvet's therionization out so I never really felt like I was in danger to often, even if 3 allies got wiped in the first 2 seconds. It's literally how I beat the final sequence of battles.
Graphic/Sound wise: Eh, the sounds and graphics aren't bad, but there not revolutionary or anything in my opinion. I guess what I'm saying here is that it feels standard.
The world did feel alive, espcially when introduced to Class 4 Islands. Although late game it's like oh boy another class 4 to beat. but when you're still in the early mid game and learn things about the world or hear about something from npc's you felt like the world was alive. Especially as you progress through the game, the NPC's make remarks about rumors of events that you participated in, mkaing the world actually feel like it moved as you progressed through the game.

This is a review from a longtime fan of this long running series.
The Sono Hanabira ni Kuchizuke wo series of Visual novels is a purely yuri series, centering around the interactions between the all-female student body of the St. Michael's Girl's academy.
Most the installments of the series tend to be light on choices, and contain a fair amount of adult content. Each chapter of the original 11 (drawn by Peko and written by Jun) feature an individual couple from the series, with the 11th installment, Maidens of Michael, featuring all the couples from previous chapters.
This chapter, along with the overly chibified Hanahira are the exceptions to the rule of adult content as they are both all ages chapters.
This (as far as I know) is the first chapter to receive an official western localization, and is a very light entry into the series, telling the story of Azumi Risa and Ayase Miya, a couple first introduced in Maidens of Michael and receiving their own chapter known as "Maidens of the Atelier"
This is simply the story of how they met. It's as cute as any of the pervious chapters, and features no adult content. Definitely recommended for anyone who likes Yuri, despite it not having any choices to speak of.
Definitely work picking up if you have any history with the series (like me) or if you like Yuri at all.

It's great that steam is uploading more yuri titles and I can't wait to see wether or not they will upload more from this series. Okay enough fangirling/fanboying and on to the actual review.
This is a visual novel and since it's a flashback based prequel, no choice options are given; therefore, while I, a self proclaimed bibliophile, enjoy this genre, I advise those looking for more interpersonal styled gameplay to rethink their purchase. Reading speed is subjective, but I managed to finish the game in about 1.4 hours; however, that might be too short for some people. The characters seem to simply be archtypes, but there is actually a deep layer of complexity underlying their personality traits. The dynamic between the characters is great and they contrast each other perfectly.
The size of the fullscreen window could use some adjustmet, but otherwise there is nothing really wrong with the technical aspect of the game.
In summary, I really enjoyed this game and recommend it as a great addition to one of the best yuri based series available.

Sleeping Dogs is kind of like Grand Theft Auto in Hong Kong, mixed with the fighting system of the Arkham games.  In fact, you'll be beating people up in this game far more than you'll be doing any shooting.  I guess that's just how they do it in Hong Kong.
So you're an undercover cop with a troubled past that's only hinted at  (a bedside picture of a woman and child, a sister who died to drugs).  So naturally you're a hardass rogue cop who plays by his own rules, and because of this you're chosen to infiltrate the Triads and take them down from the inside.   As the game goes on, you'll have to be reminded that you're actually a cop from time to time as you kill dozens if not hundreds of people in gang wars, wreck half of Hong Kong in street races, steal any car you want to and squash the occasional civilian in high speed chances.  But as long as you're cleaning up the streets in the end, it's all good right?
As far as the game itself: is it any fun?  Yes it is, or I wouldn't have finished it, but the fun has its limits and I'd have to say the game overstayed its welcome the further I got into it.  The fighting is pretty slick, but since you'll be doing a LOT of it, it can get old after a bit.  Especially when you get caught in unfair fights against 20 guys and die, and then have to start the fight all over again.  The gunplay is simple but entertaining enough, with a duck and cover system that kind of reminded me of playing the Uncharted games.  The missions have a nice variety to them as far as the story, but usually end up in you figthing at least a dozen guys hand to hand, or shooting your way out of a building by mowing down enemy after enemy.  The driving itself is superb.  This was probably the most fun I had playing Sleeping Dogs.  Each car handles very differently and the driving has a nice realistic feel to it.  I especially love using drifting to turn sharp corners and escape cops, (who are the lamest and easily avoidable cops in any open world sandbox game, by the way.)   And the Hong Kong setting is really fun to drive around in.  I'd say it feels authentic, but I've never actually been.
As for the story, it's well acted and fairly well scripted, but it's also pretty predictable.  You have the over-zealous super-intendant of the department that is borderline corrupt, a fellow cop who constantly thinks you're going too far, your best freind in the gang who you try to protect from the cops, so on and so forth.  By the time the game was nearing a close, I was compelled enough to keep playing for the sake of resolving the story, but most of my predictions ended up being correct.
I'd recommend Sleeping Dogs for anybody hungry for another sandbox game.  It won't leave a lasting impression like Grand Theft Auto, and it's not as outrageous as the Saints Row games, but for a low price, it's a good distraction for a while.

I never grew up with an Atari 2600, but I did grow up with an 80-game disc with the same games I got out of a cereal box. I got this Steam version of the compilation because I couldn't play the disc anymore, and this is a great, vast mix of 100 very old 2600 and Arcade games to play and waste time on.
It should be noted down that most of these games are very small and short. Some games require two players to play on, some require instructions outside of booting up the game, and even some can be unplayable like having immaculate and unforgiving AI. But overall, these games are highly minimalist and are very fun to play given they appear highly authentic with all the beeps and bloops to go with it.
Other features include manuals to read through for each game so that you get an idea of what to expect when jumping into one of these games. As well as a gallery and 3D-rendered arcade cabinets and game boxes. The game also has support for USB gamepads, but it's mainly for Xbox controllers, and perhaps the Steam controller (I don't have one so I don't know *shrug*
This compilation of games is excellent for people who enjoy the older days of video-gaming or want to enjoy the staple of games in their bit-blocky, beep-bloopy states. It's about $10 for 100 small games and all kinds of bonus material, which is a good value. Again, not all games can be playable (Like about 5-10 of them).
I give this compilation 7/10

12 Labours of Hercules III: Girl Power is a casual resource/time management strategy game. This is the third in the series and the first time you don't start out with Hercules. You play as Megara as she tries to rescue Hercules from Charybdis. Its basically the same as the 2 previous 12 Labours games. At the start of each level, you have 1 or 2 workers who you direct to do various things ranging from collecting resourses to constructing and upgrading buildings or gold mines. You also have to contend with bandits trying to steal your resourses. About all Megara does is bring the fruit bushes to life. There are the familiar characters of Medusa, Cerberus, Cyclops, and Pegasus who help get rid of the minotaurs, ghosts, rescue sheep and move rocks to aid in the journey. If you find all the puzzle pieces in levels .1-.10 you can put the puzzle together and unlock a bonus level. Nice third entry of the series and overall it's a very enjoyable time management and if you're a fan of the genre you should pick it up.

For those that wish to 100% this, there is so much grinding that you’re sure to moan and groan just like the critters that your baseball bat wants to say 'hello' to...
Zombie games seem to be my 'Kryptonite'. I have no qualms and in fact enjoy, dicing, slicing, thumping, punching, stomping and decapitating anything that roams around the earth with the intelligence of a sausage roll. This seems to be designed purposefully to be a relaxed, no brainer, turn-based apocalyptic RPG and because it is very casual and relaxing, scores of negative reviews have surfaced pitchforking the yawning monotony of the grinding involved. Personally I don't condemn the developer’s decision for creating an easy/casual game. They can be fun and very welcoming among the gaming community making you feel great about yourself as your overpowered baseball bat sends them flying across the screen. However forcing a player to redo the whole game 6-8 times in a row from the start just so that they can get an extra achievement and an extra line of text, does not in any way add value to the game and instead festers some animosity among gamers for wasting their time on such trivialities.
The objective of the game is to help a group of survivalists last 42 days. As more and more join your party, you get to delegate which 1 or 2 of them join your party to complete tasks, while the others you assign to jobs to basically shield the camp and hunt for food. Each mission you successfully complete will help you to level your party up and each mission will give you time to scavenge for materials allowing you to shop or delegate people to be crafters who are able to create sturdier weapons, ammunition and clothes.
Originally at the start you are presented with 5 landscapes Forest day and night, Highway day and night and camp. There's really nothing much to do at camp other than meet people who request you to be there and it's basically just a single paged background. As for the other two area's you will be greeted with the minimum of 20 backgrounds with each battle being split up by scavenging goods or a rather limited visual novel. Day landscapes will often present you with two enemies at each battle scene and the night time ones while presenting you with the same backgrounds at night will require you to confront 3 enemies on each battle page. At the end of each 20 paged battle scene there will be a Boss which you will be required to defeat. The longer you survive, eventually you will be greeted with three more landscapes, city day and night and finally Desert. With the same mechanics basically being involved just enemies with higher health points.
The battle perspectives are easy to master, you seriously won’t break a sweat. You can win the entire game just by levelling up melee weapons and forget everything else. Syringes and the crafting of health kits I never even bothered with since my entire camp were baseball bat experts.
The only other negative grumble I constantly saw in reviews is that the user interface was abysmal and I whole heartedly agree. In fact it would only probably make sense to someone who might be completely cross-eyed after a long Christmas party. Unfortunately, more than likely, you'll only begin to understand how to craft, travel and delegate jobs, through trial and error as one of your party succumb to a walking sausage roll. Needless to say, without your guidance your team ai are as intuitive in defending themselves against enemy drool as much as a fluffy pillow is.
With all these gripes placed aside the artwork, animation and graphics make the apocalypse look sexy and the musical soundtrack perfectly fitted the Armageddon scene like a mad max Cinderella slipper. The story board was keep it simple just like the game itself was, but there were interesting secrets to discover as your forced to identify a traitor in your group, the secret brother and sister relationships that some had, what happens if you take away a certain persons weapon and finally even the secret bio weapon at the end of the game.
The biggest in game smirks will probably come from your amassed critical hit strikes that you perform on enemies, or maybe the low brow special attacks that some enemies will do to you. For instance there is a zombie clown in the game which breathes into your mouth and forces you to fart health points. Charming I'm sure you will agree. It's something you just have to see to believe.
In final a colourful, imaginative beautifully rendered visual story board with an extremely fitting audio which places you in the scene. However the cumbersome grinding mechanics is a sure downfall which does not add true pleasing value for money. In fact there is no way on this planet that the game is worth it's normal current advertised price of ($15.00) especially since you can buy the game as an app ($4.50) for a mobile tablet.
Yes for $15.00 I would much prefer to go to my local bakery and grind away at all the sausage rolls in there. For casual no brainer, apocalyptic survivalist enthusiasts, I would still recommend to wait for a sale.

Oh geeze where to begin.,,
If there was ever a fighter that got me into the genre it was the guilty gear series. I cannot count how many hours I poured into these games by myself doing survival mode struggling to unlock secret characters or constantly urging my friends to play with me until we all where sporting callused thumbs like badges of courage.
For me This is not just a good game, its down right nostalgic.
Guilty gear X2: Accent Core Plus R is a fast paced hyper fighter. Its your stylized anime type of fighter and probably has the claim of being one of if not the first. This particular version is the most up to date version of a game that began back in 2003 and while it shows its age a little I cant help but have nothing but love for it. With this particular version you have a rather extensive roster each character with perhaps the largest move set they've ever had, exceeding even that of their modern day variations in Guilty Gear Xrd. Also present in this version is the much desired online functionality with suitable net code. Its nothing to write home about but gets the job done.
As I mentioned before however the game can show its age at times. Sprites arnt as slick as one might remember, also lacking is a "challenge" mode method of training present in newer fighters so if you want to pick up a character learn their moveset and hash out some combo's be prepared to spend some time in training mode.
For its price however you are getting one hell of a deal with more then enough content to keep you entertained for quite some time.
Gamepad or Fightstick strongly encouraged.

I recommend it to some degree. I've heard people only say good things about it, but some aspects of it disappointed me. I wouldn't say it's a bad game, but surely not as fantastic as some were making me believe. It holds some good points, but others I found underwhelming or irritating.
The game's style is very colorful, there are some neat backgrounds and some levels have nice, sometimes "magical" and "transcendental", "dream-like" settings, but the level design/layout felt underwhelming, often rather short and branching out into all kinds of directions without great sense of direction and meaning. The levels building up in front of you with every step you take seemed like an interesting idea at first, but it became repetitive and boring quickly and kinda slowed down the game flow. Without good reason: I don't remember any proper explanation story-/plot-wise as to why the levels were building up like that instead of being already there with your arrival. The "Calamity" shattered the world, but why was it floating and "waiting" for your steps? It was a very artifical, mostly stylish feature.
The narrator explaining things as you do them and reacting to some degree to your specific reactions and ways of handling stuff seemed interesting, but lost it's appeal over the course of the game too. His talk became rather repetitive, he was very eager trying to emphasize in a badass-ish way how "The kid" (= you) was going into unknown, dangerous areas and fighting things. Again, again, and again. I did understand that the first time he mentioned it already, there was no need for him telling me this all over. He didn't say the same lines, of course, but the whole direction of his talk was always the same. And maybe a less raw and hard-boiled♥♥♥♥♥♥ish Solid Snake-ish voice would have done better too. You meet the narrator as an NPC in the game, and his voice didn't fit his appearance. It felt pretentious and forceful. The developers apparently desired a badass narrator for the sake of having a badass narrator alone. A rather artifical feature too.
The story holds some interesting points, and there is some interesting lore too. Sadly it's not fleshed out as much as one may hope. Most of the time the story wants you to travel the world (well, what is left of it at least) to collect items to rebuild your home, the "Bastion", which I found to be an underwhelming concept. At some point you get captured inside a conflict between some factions  and rivalry, there are serious tones and themes in this game like racism and the suffering of refugees, the hardships of seeking a new home, of finding one's place in the world. These were the more interesting aspects of this game. It's not some simple good vs evil thing, you sometimes get to question your actions and need to make decisions slightly altering further events (there are at least two different endings, but I don't think your actions mid-game matter, you choose "your" ending in the very last moment of the game with one specific, obvious action).
The combat is alright, there are quite a lot of different weapons to use. I quickly found my few favorites though, and while you could improve your gear and boost the difficulty by using "modifications" to make the enemies harder (while giving you more XP and stuff) I never really saw the need/enough motivation to do that. Those who seek some challenge will surely find it there though.

Netcode is acceptable. Not at a level the game really and truly needs, but honestly no netcode out there is.
Regardless, Guilty Gear is another one of the classic fighters to hit Steam. It was one of the first fighting games I played more than a little bit and the one that got me hooked on to the fighting game genre. The game is fast paced and even now remains one of the most technically complex 2D fighters out there. If you're looking for a "deep" fighter with a diverse cast, look no further. Guilty Gear has it all and is a pleasure to play at both low and high levels. It is quite a time sink though if you take it seriously, but still enjoyable casually. I honestly feel that the game is more accessible than something like Street Fighter 4 since it generally relies on chain combos rather than links making lower level combos not too bad. But at the same time the combos at the higher end can be much more difficult.
Unfortunately the port doesn't really polish much (or anything?), though the only real glaring age issue is that the sound effect audio quality (not the soundtrack) is extremely low. Worse than I remember the original XX in fact. Don't let that scare you off though! This is a great game!

I have unlocked all achievements today, and decided to write a review:
This time, the story felt like a breath of fresh air, because, right from the start, you realize that you won't be saving
the world this time. That's pretty original, for a "Tales of" game.
The characters were amazing, and one of the best. Each of them, have different goals and motives. It's not "all about the friendship", it's
this time.
The battles were great fun. You can fully customize your artes and, sort of, design your own combos.
It felt like the characters had a few more skills, than in previous game (Zestiria) and, actually, there's a lot more mystic artes. Break soul, is what makes each character fight differently. Overall, the battles felt a lot more dynamic.
The loot you get aka your inventory, has a clearly defined cap, which is great (in Zestiria - the closer you got to the cap, the lower the drop rates). Even without any grade shop drop enhancements, it never felt like you were lacking item drops.
Arena battles are also great, because you can use all and any characters you want.
There's also surprise encounters, in form of "dire foes". That was a great addition.
However, there are flaws, which are evident, once you reach max level and chain monsters together in max difficulty.
Even if you have max HP on your characters, they will most likely get 1-2 shotted.
So basicly there's a flaw in this design - the enemy stats get so inflated, that they become almost impossible to defeat.
Even the best gear does not help.
This would be my biggest issue with the game. That endgame dungeon enemies are OP. And I didn't even mention caster enemies yet.
+Refreshing new story
+VERY different and great characters
+Improved graphics (better than Zestiria anyway)
+Improved battle system, with more skills/artes
+You travel on a ship
+Treasure finding with said ship
+Improved fast travel and movement (geoboard)
+Lots of mini-games
-endgame enemies feel way too overpowered (on max difficulty)
-caster enemies are an even bigger problem, than they were in Zestiria
-towards the endgame, the game feels rushed/unfinished (mainly dialogue/voicing problems)
-some mini-games could have been a bit better (fishing, for example)
-the costs of materials, when it comes to tales coins, were too high (getting the coins feels like a huge grind)
-endgame dungeon consists of already visited areas
-lack of dungeons
I'd say yes. If you're a huge fan of "Tales of" series and still wondering, if you should buy - then go ahead. Otherwise, if you have something else to play - get it on sale.

As the fall season begins, Risa Azumi reminisces about how she and her now girlfriend, Miyu Ayase, first met, hence the title. It's the first visual novel in the nearly decade long Sonohana franchise to be officially released in the west, and the first non-spin-off entry to be non-H.
The story is that, when Risa and Miyu first met, Miyu, the newly transfered student, would quickly start to skip classes very frequently which irks Risa, the newly chosen class representative, particularly because the teacher asked her to help Miyu get adjusted to the school. What follows is a series of events which leads them to develop feelings for each other.
While it's a sequel-prequel to three other entries in the Sonohana series, it is somewhat newbie friendly due to the story concerning how they first met, even though there is a noticable gap between the flashback and the present day. On the other hand, it doesn't give newbies any indication how pornographic the series can get, even though the not so subtle raunchy parts of the dialogue from the beginning and the end is a clear nod to the fact that this series is an eroge series first and foremost. For those who aren't into eroges, Remembering How We Met is still good as a stand alone story, although some small details go nowhere without the context of the other installments.
Clocking in at approximately 3 hours with auto enabled at a brisk reading speed, Remembering How We Met is a short, fully voice acted kinetic (linear, with no branches whatsoever) visual novel with no replay value aside from picking up some details in the dialogue you might've missed the first time around. Aside from the main story, there are a couple extras; a CG gallery, BGM player, and a set named Memories, which is essentially the entire visual novel cut up into multiple chapters, which is good for people who didn't make their own bookmarks (although the game will return you back to the Memories tab once you reach the end of that section of the story). The UI is pretty standard for a visual novel, and everything runs pretty smoothly, although the text will occassionally hiccup when set to auto as it will fail to roll out and most of it will pop up at once instead (thankfully, those hiccups don't affect the audio as well). At $8, it's pretty reasonable if you compare it to the cost/hour of anime (which, given that it's a kinetic visual novel, is a fair comparision) and it's a must buy for any yuri fans.

Atari Vault is a compilisation of 100 Atari games ranging in from the arcade to the 2600 console. Like the Sega Genesis & Mega Drive Collection, this compilisation is a perfect way to experience all of the popular Atari games from the company's heyday. The menus for each game are very decorative and stylish matching the decade of the 80's. Each game has its own "virtual" arcade cabinet or 2600 cartridge to make you feel like you are virtually seeing the game of choice. Original game manuels and box art help offer depth and history to each of the avalible games of this collection. The games themselves are the same as they were when they all hit the market, vintaged 8-bit wonders that helped shape the earlier gamer generation. Keep in mind that this doesn't include all of the Atari games, as there were at least 565 titles(excluding prototype, unreleased, and homebrewed games) for the Atari 2600 when it was in the market. But due to royalty rights and space capacity it was logical that the developers of this collection only included the titles that are free from any third party companies' control. Plus 100 games is plenty to enjoy for those who are die hard Atari gamers or for those who are trying them out for the first time. If you're an avid history gamer then this collection is a must, cause Atari holds an important spot in game history that shouldn't be ignored.

After being in early access for roughly more than two and a half years, Chucklefish has decided that Starbound's version number is 1.0 - the fully finished product. Unfortunately, another 20-something hours does not show an honest effort put in for those seeking adventure.
From the last time I reviewed the game, the basic gameplay loop remains mostly unchanged except for a few changes at the start of the game to accomodate for its 'tutorial phase' and story. The loop starts with gathering a planet's available materials and metals to help get yourself various crafting stations and some sufficient kit and especially armor, because it practically decides not only how tanky you are but also how much damage you do.
The difference at this point is that the main quest also wants the player to find settlements of a specific race and scan certain scattered decorative objects, demonstrating the game's feature where your character's race influences the remarks they have about them. After that, an instanced mission is given to retrieve a MacGuffin from the race, including a mandatory boss fight in each as well. And then you're asked to do the same thing but for another race that is supposedly easier to find on a different type of planet or galaxy that's a tier up, restarting the loop since your old armor won't do you much good and you can't just 'jump' a tier without the materials to survive the specific atmosphere of later planets.
Another big thing thrown in the loops are settlements, which provide a never-ending supply of terribly simple, generated quests asking you to fetch items, talking to NPCs that are very close by, or killing something on the other side of the planet; just as awful as Skyrim's radiant quests. Thankfully they share another purpose in that you can practically freeload from their containers without consequence, giving you an alternate means of obtaining some materials than just digging deep down. And of course, why you can do this just raises more questions. The shops do at least provide a source from where you can get armor from other races, though.
One big thing Chucklefish has never seemed to really address since the beginning of the beta are planets. You know there is a problem when the setting allows for all kinds of crazy worlds to exist, and yet are much less diverse than Earth. For those unfamiliar, Starbound practically treats planets as single biomes (before settlements/bases), such as dedicated forest, desert, ice, ocean, and even volcanic worlds. These are quite literally are what they're advertised as, and the smaller sub-biomes that do exist are mostly there for wacky visual flair like trees with eyes and so only provide little different use compared to the primary biome's resources, so something like a beach or ocean will still only be found on an ocean planet. All planets aren't so different underground and actually do share many of the same sub-biomes regardless of the planet's type, so it can get repetitive there too. For such an important aspect of the game, world generation is seriously neglected.
The game also runs quite poorly overall.
Ultimately, not only development has been thin and slow overall, but Starbound is also a victim of having no real design plan for many game mechanics since the start. Much of these two and a half years of early access have been wasted on trying to redesign how various game systems are handled multiple times along with adding and even removing content (racial bonuses, temperature, and a lot of craftable weapons) to the ire of others. The one major new thing - the main story, is an unremarkable 'an ancient evil awakens' plot that has clearly been rushed out especially around near the end, so the devs could call the game 1.0.
Players who like to do many vanity things might find Starbound alright, but if you are looking for a more technically impressive 'Terraria but in space' kind of game, you will be sorely disappointed. Until Chucklefish steps it up with a huge update or an ambitious modding project blows off everybody's socks, Starbound right now is a large waste of potential that could have been more.

Before Nintendo’s old classic video game systems like the Nintendo Entertainment System/NES, the Super Nintendo Entertainment System/SNES, and the Game Boy, and before Sega’s old classic video game system which was the Sega Genesis, it all started with Atari and their first classic video game system which was the Atari 2600. And there were also Atari arcade games as well. Atari Vault is a great collection of old Atari arcade games and old Atari 2600 games from that era. My introduction to, and first experiences with video games as a young kid were with the Nintendo Entertainment System/NES. At that time, I was not familiar with Atari. Eventually as I got older, I did learn of Atari and I learned that Atari is what came before the Nintendo Entertainment System/NES. So Atari Vault is interesting because it allows gamers to see, play, and experience how it all began with regards to video games. Before Nintendo’s classics such as Super Mario Brothers, The Legend Of Zelda, and Tetris, to name a few, Atari’s first classic was Pong. Atari paved the way for the successes of Nintendo and Sega. The games in Atari Vault are all emulated excellently. The games also come with their original game manuals, box art, arcade cabinets, and other interesting stuff that you can view and read from within the Atari Vault game itself. Atari Vault is a game that I do recommend because people that played Atari games back then will most likely adore Atari Vault. And people like myself that didn’t get to play Atari games back then because they started with Nintendo games, can see, play, and experience how it all began with Atari. While it is true that anybody can just download any Atari emulator program and the Atari game ROM files for free, and then just play Atari games that way if they want to, the Atari Vault game does a great job at presenting the games with their original box art and arcade cabinets. And the games come with their original game manuals as well. These are things that you most likely won’t get with a third party Atari emulator program. One of the unfortunate things about Atari Vault which others have also mentioned is that there are some Atari games which some people really wish would have been included in this package. Sadly, Atari was not able to include certain games because those particular games are not owned by Atari. Those particular games are owned by other companies like Activision. The games in Atari Vault are games that Atari owns the rights to. Maybe in the future, Atari may be able to work something out with these other companies so that the Atari games from these other companies can be released as DLC for Atari Vault. Whether that happens or not, Atari Vault already has a huge selection of different games. There’s something for everyone. And there’s even local and online multiplayer as well. And online leaderboards too. Atari Vault is a great collection that is definitely worth checking out and I definitely recommend it

There are very few times in a game where the ending makes me feel horrible, but for all the right reasons. I will say no more about this, but I must concede that I've played this games many times through on both Xbox and PC, and no matter how many times I play it, I still enjoy it.
The mechanics and gameplay iaresimple at the base, and the progression is fairly linear, but that isn't a detraction at all; honestly, the game feels like a novella you play, coupled with a kick♥♥♥♥♥sound track and narrator that bring the entire experience together into something... above the standard ARPG.  Even with the simple gameplay, there are challenges and higher difficulties that require creative use of these simple mechanics that can make it quite difficult to play if you feel like going for the challenge.  However, if you also want to casually stroll through the game with minimal difficulty, there's an option for that as well.
But, as you play through the game, you'll find that the simplicity of the game's mechanics makes it that much easier to enjoy the ambience, atmosphere and allure presented by the visual and story aspects. That's where this game excels. As to not spoil anything for those interested in the game, I will only say that the story is... satisfying, no matter the paths taken, and there's a fair bit of backstory for those willing to be adventurous. And though it's a short game, I'd highly recommend it for my friends, full price or while on sale.

Now that the game has been out for a while and we have most of this waves dlc I wanted to update my review. Street Fighter V is in my opinion the best Street Fighter since 3rd Strike. It has a variety of fun, viable charachters, each one with a unique V skill/trigger which provides an opprotunity for much deeper gameplay and charachter design than any of the SFIV series games. Gameplay wise this game has nearly no flaws, I could nitpick a few things I prefer from older SF entries but this game accomplishes what it set out to do very well. Graphically SFV is a mixed bag. Some charachters look better than ever while some make me wish that the game was still sprite based. I have to take a few points off for the graphical variance, and I wish Capcom had opted for a different graphical route (ala Guilty Gear shading, or Skullgirls animation). The story mode really added nothing for me, I enjoyed playing the dlc charachters early but thats about it. My main complaint for this game is the price of the dlc. Even with a season pass you have to throw more money at the game to unlock all of the content. Besides the ridiculous pricing and grind for fightmoney, the game has fixed most of its flaws with the netcode, and lack of single player content. I would give this game an 8/10 it loses points mainly for the lack luster graphics.

As a Guilty Gear Fan this was pretty much an immediate buy. Thanks Steam!
The good
-----
-Large cast of characters that are quite diverse in terms of what they do and what their backstory is. A rule of thumb, the farther from the center of the character selection screen the character is, the more complicated that character is going to play. You'll sure to have a unique experience with many of the characters in the game.
-The game goes through constant rebalancing as the devs know this is a game that players like to compete in.
-Awesome soundtrack and art design.
-There is much to do in terms of unlocking. Each character has an alternate EX version that plays in a "similar but different" form of the original.
The Bad
-----
-Limited graphic settings. The game is locked to 4:3 (understandable, the original was in 4:3 back in the last decade). If you play in full screen, the only way to exit the game seems to be ALT-F4 at the moment. Thankfully, the game runs fine in 144hz, unlike some other 2d fighters released on steam.
The Ugly
----
Having to reunlock the EX versions of the characters yet again if you played earlier console versions (All of the original roster is unlocked from the get-go, including Justice and Kliff). Here's hoping someone finds a way to re unlock the EX characters asap. :P

This game is fantastic. I would highly recommend this to anyone that enjoys turn based combat. The War of the Chosen DLC is a must.
I'm not going to list all the pros and cons - instead I'm just going to mention the #1 pro in my mind:
-Replayability - random level generation and multiple difficulty levels that drastically change the gameplay (everything is tweaked including alien behavior and ability usage - combat tactics, health, cost, time etc...it's not just a simple "they have more health now" type of adjustment).
My recommendation would be:
1st - to learn - play on veteran difficulty without ironman for your first playthrough. There's a ton to learn and figure out throughout the course of the game and you'll need to reload saves.
2nd - most enjoyable - Then play on commander difficulty with ironman enabled - this is where the game shines beyond belief. The difficulty level is perfect for an enjoyable but challenging game that can be won most of the time by an average player that knows what he is doing and takes his time, and ironman adds a ton of stress and excitement to the process. Expect to lose a few soliders and maybe a mission or two over the course of the game - that's okay, don't take that as a failure, you can lose a few battles and still win the war. The reason this difficulty level is so perfect is that the bad rolls and occasional mistakes that can occur won't doom you to failure here. The only potential criticism I would have is that the very end game after you've researched everything and have fully leveled up soldiers can feel like a sure thing where you are just going through the motions for the last few missions.
3rd - for an insane but possible challenge - Finally, after you've conquered the game on commander ironman, give a shot at legend ironman. You will restart many times, but you'll learn something new each time and adjust your plan accordingly and will have to employ strategies you never even thought of in the lower difficulty levels because they werent' necessary.
This is the best game I've played in a quite a while, however it's also my preferred genre so take that for what you will.
Advice if you are struggling:
-Too hard, feels unfair? - lower the difficulty and/or figure out counters to what is messing you up - flash bangs prevent special abilities, drastically decrease movement, and interrupt mind control, heal restores someone who is stunned, EMP and bluscreen ammo destroys mechanical enemies, AP ammo works wonders against high armor non mechnacal enemies, mimic beacons are a life saver. Go in with the expectation that you will miss 90% shots sometimes - instead of thinking "90% chance to hit" think "10% chance to miss". Sometimes I feel like people come away thinking the game is BS because they miss one or two 90% shots....that's gonna happen that's how percentages work lol.
-Alien rulers messing you up in WOTC - just avoid the facilities that say they are guarded by a strong enemy - definitely not necessary to attack these to keep the threat down.

You  already know what you're getting into, and you also know if you're going to like it or not. So, if you enjoy these, i recommend Berseria as well. It's a good entry to the franchise, despite some of the gameplay aspect being streamlined, or "dumbed down" a little bit to make the game more accessible to new players. Better character cast and storyline makes up for them pretty well.
You might be looking at this, and thinking to yourself "what the hell is this game". Tales games are almost a genre in themselves at this point, every game follows a certain formula (with some changes every time) that some of the people will enjoy, and some other will not. I'l ltry to explain what you're getting yourself into:
As every main Tales game, Berseria is a JRPG focused almost entirely on the gameplay, with the highlight always being the insanely fun combat system (which is the major reason people enjoy the series). Looking at the screenshots you might see a lot of exposition and cutscenes but don't be fooled, what you'll be doing for the majority of the game is dungeon crawling, with light puzzle elements, and beating the crap out of A LOT of various monsters. Anything that happens outside of it is there only to be a breather to the player, and an excuse for your characters to keep doing what they're doing. In the case of Berseria we actually got a pretty flavorful cast of (mostly) interesting characters, with a story that, while being a standard revenge plot, is surprisingly competent compared to what we usually get. But don't go in expecting an overworld straight out of Witcher 3, this game is played for it's gameplay. You won't find fancy storyline, great dialogues or complicated characters, it's all there to be a distraction. And this is actually a part of what we sign up for as the fans of the franchise, without all the silly dialogue, over the top moments, corny one liners, the game would just not be the same, it just wouldn't work if the game took itself seriously all the time.
Enough about story and characters, let's talk about the meat of all Tales games, COMBAT. This time around we got introduced to a streamlined, four button combo system (fully customizable) which will make skill managment and making perfect combos much easier for begginers. Essentialy your character can chain up to 4 moves into a combo (this number changes depending on various factors) , and each one of the four buttons represents a different skill that will be executed during a part of that combo. That gives you 16 skills you can put on those buttons, in whatever order you like, you can even change your setup mid-fight if you want, neat huh? Well, that's just the tip of the iceberg. Each of the skills can be put into 3 categories, which changes what stat it uses for scaling. Eeach one of them has different elemental and monster properties, making it effective against different kind of enemies, which is essential knowledge if you want to be effective. Each skill places the character and the enemy in a different position, making some other skills better suited to follow certain combos. Skills have different costs, which must be considered so your character doesn't run out of fuel mid-combo and get destroyed by the enemy follow up. There are special burst skills that will let you do a powerful move, that will allow to chain combos together into ridiculous lenghts if used correctly. Skills have status aliments, that will help you extend your combos when applied to the enemy. Guarding changes your attack properties, dodging at a perfect time will give you opportunity to extend your combos. There are six playable characters (4 max in a party), each one of them has different and expansive moveset, and special abilities that make their playstyle different...
There is way too many things about the combat system to explain on paper. If you think that's WAY too complicated, don't leave yet!
about all this is that the combat is only as complicated as you want it. If you look at all this and thin kto yourself "this is way too much, I don't get half of this, I just want to kick♥♥♥♥♥" as you wish, just set the difficulty to normal or casual, and kick the crap out of the monsters using your favourite characters and skills. But if you enjoy a challenge, want test your mettle and master every aspect of the advanced combat system of a Tales game, you can crank the difficulty up, and make the most optimal combos, character builds, and combinations you can! The game provides good tutorials that explain the game mechanics very well, and it paces those tutorials so you don't get too overwhelmed by the knowledge.
Aside from the comabt, you got the typical gameplay elements of a JRPG, things like: equimpent upgrading, minigames, and such. Nothing to write home about, but good additions nonetheless.
At this point you probably already know if you want to play Berseria or not, so I'll leave the rest for Your judgement. Have fun!

12 Labours of Hercules III: Girl Power it's the third installment from the series. This time, Hercules managed to get into trouble and got captured by an evil enemy. He needs to be rescued, but by who do you ask? Of course by his dear and sweet wife, Megara! So the roles got reversed. Instead of Hercule, you have the chance to play with his blonde wife, which has a habit for gardening. She can grow plants that will give you food for the period of the game. As you can see, the gameplay has been changed a little bit while the concept is still the same as the first games of the series. A simple and fun time management game in which you have to gather resources to help you build farms, workshops or gold mines. That later on, it will provide you with enough resources to reach the goal of the level. Like in the second game, you have to be fast because the thieves may happen to take them before you do.
PS: Megara isn't as strong as her husband, so there will be no more boulders in the game to move.
PS2: Servants have to do all the job while Megara stays and watch, she has the same habit as her husband, they really complete each other.
The third installment from the series has yet come again with some new features for the fans of the series. Like a new character named Charon that can bring you resources for one piece of gold. New maps to keep you company for the entire duration of the game and 44 more levels to play through and have fun. The most important segment introduced into the game is the new main character that joined us in battle to rescue Hercules, Medara. But they have also removed some things like boss battles and mini-games which may be a bit sad for the veterans of the series. But the difficulty was also scaled a lot, which will prove to be a more challenge than the last game for the achievement hunters, as they have to think fast, click rapidly and to not offer their souls to the god of rage quitting.
- Support for Achievements, Trading Cards and Steam Cloud.
- Won't get boring easily since pretty much every level has to offer something else.
- Touchscreen support, a wonderful opportunity for the Windows 8 and 10 users.
- Same gameplay mechanics as the previous games, which is a relief for many fans.
- Say bye bye to the boss battles, but while the developers removed those, the hardest difficulty it's a lot more difficult than the one from the previous games.
- Colorful graphics, which shall be a very nice friend to your eyes.
- Hidden puzzle pieces around each mission for collectors to find, which later on will let you play a bonus level.
- Plenty of achievements to keep you determined in completing the game.
- The minigames got removed.
- Same music as the first games of the series.
- A short story that won't find it's place in your heart.
While the game may look exactly like the first games of the series, it still ranks amongst the best time management games of this type out there. So if you're a fan of the series, then go ahead and buy it as you will find in it the same excitement and fun you've found in the previous titles. For the newcomers, I advice you to start with the first game because that's where everyone else started. And it won't be nice to start from part three, would it?
I definitely recommend this game for the casual players that need something nice and relaxing in their life. And even the achievement hunters can benefit on the back of this game that will provide a nice challange for them to test their skills.
