I have played this game for a long, long time.  This game was actually the first game i've ever owned on steam; i've played it since the beta kuala version.  At the time, this game was just a good idea and I feel like every hope that there was for this game was exceeded.  The things you can do are really endless; with friends or alone.  Get ready because this is going to be long, I've learned pretty much everything there is to know about this game; yet i still feel like there is so much left to learn.
1) Replay Value
First off is something that I feel is really important for sandbox games; replay value.  After completing the story and getting all there is to the best gear and things like that, the game still has things left for you to do.  The building in this game is clean, simple, and expansive; there is so much to do.  Obviously you may get bored of your character after playing with him/her for months and you may want to try a new one; this is what I love about the game so much.  When I start a new character, it's exciting.  Of course it may be rough and you will regret having little to no good gear...but that's the best part.  Building yourself back up, re-experiencing the story, and creating the new character is exciting.  Coming up with a new name and designing a unique character from one of the 7 playable species is fun and interesting; and building up a new ship with a different design is just an experience that never gets old.  This game has so much to do and never feels repetitive and I truly feel this game will never get old, especially with the modding community to back it up.
2) Modding
Steam Workshop makes this easy, as well as the expanding community that wants to add more to this game.  Chucklefish can't make everybody's dreams come true; but modders can.  The developers both encourage modding and they work towards making their game easier to mod.  Mods are a reason alone to buy this game, they all make the game feel even more diverse and creative.   Whether its a mod that allows you to craft new armour, or one that adds twice as many worlds to explore; it's all worth it.
3) Exploration
This has to be the best part of the game (besides the music).  Especially with the newest update, exploring is fun and it's exciting to never know what you will find.  There are diverse planets and so many of them to explore as well as exploring dungeons and the most satisfying part of it all is the loot and money you gain from it all.  Now with the mechs, you can explore space and even friendly or agressive ships and this all helps with the idea that you aren't the only out there that is exploring all of these planets and solar systems.
4) Progression
Armour has multiple tiers and you are always working to get the next best thing and this just encourages exploration.  You can go mining or explore dungeons and find the ores you need there.  Besides the basics; finding gear and crafting armour, there is a crew ot worry about.  Having your own crew is exciting, and also required to upgrade your ship (unless you are loaded in pixels).  Working towards a crew just encourages helping people and doing the randomly generated and endless quests, its both rewarding and interesting since you never know what role your potential crew member may have.
5) Colony update
I know this was still during the beta and has been around for awhile, but it cannot be ignored.  This part of the game encourages everything, exploring, progressing in gear, and building especially.  You can now move colonists into your creations and feel like you started a real society (like the opes you see when exploring planets).  The colonists not only pay you in rent, but they also offer endless quests.  These quests bring in new people (non-colonists who wonder around your town and bring more life to it) and force you to build new homes to move in new people.  Along with this are mystery bags; which serve as a basic reward for completing a quest, and along with this is the reward that your colonist may wear a uniform and offer to join your crew.  What I love about these colonists the most, is the progression and attachment with them.  The longer you have them, the more interactive they are.  Quests often lead to new furniture, secret letters that are sent between your colonists, and even new hats and clothes that they wear; this adds personality and allows you to appreciate them the longer they stay.
6) The Community
Many people may avoid games because of a toxic or an un-friendly community...this game is nothing like those.  Joining online servers may be worrying; while you can do anything you want, that includes stealing and destroying others' creations.  Only one time have I seen a player who wanted to steal from another player in this game...the community here is good.  In the servers I have played, people want to help eachother, they like sharing both loot and explorationss with eachother.  When you are alone and need help on a mission or progressing in a quest, people WANT to help you.  Making friends is easy in this game and fun, everybody loves exploring and it's even more fun with more people.  Don't freak out about potentially being "griefed" or "raided" by others because the universe is basically never ending (the chances of someone finding your home planey are very very slim) and the chance of somebody actually wanting to take things from you is slim as well.  The community is accepting and also open to new players.
7) Cons
Now there is so much more that I have not discussed, but this review is starting to be way too big (i've been typing this for 20-30 minutes) but I can't make a review without adressing any problems.
-performance; i experience lag spikes even with a pc that can probably run two or more strabound's at the same time.  these are usually uncommon but they do happen; personally they don't take anything away from the game for me
-party size; i am having a hard time fixing this, but you can only have 4 players in a group at the same time and thisdoes bother me (although i work around it)
-bugs; i have experienced bugs in this game before; they usually get patched but every update comes with them.  sometimes my vehicle just dissapears (cheap to repair tho) and other minor bugs that don't really affect the game that much for me
-not enough vehicles; there is little diversity in vehicles but mods fill these in easily and i think it was left empty so the community could fill it in
8) Last thoughts
I haven't even adressed how amazing and fantastic the music is (I could listen to it all day) or the pet system; but this would be waaaaaaay to long if I wrote a paragraph for every amazing thing this game has.  There is so much potential for this game and even though it is out of beta, chucklefish continues to push for gamechanging update and I believe this game deserves even more praise than it already has.  It is both fun and exciting, but also peaceful and calming.  If you made it to the end, I appreciate it; if there is anything really important i missed or more problems that I did not mention; lemme know and i'll add em' in.  This game means a lot to me and deserves a long reviews like this.

Updated review:
I experienced the double GPU  problem (can't use high end card), then the slowdown issue when both .exe were set to compatibility mode.
This gentleman's workaround finally allows me to play the game (in windowed mode)
Additionaly, Nvidia released their 364.51 driver and I can now play the game in full screen too.
Because the game itself is actually excellent, for both newbies and veterans alike, and will certainly develop well, I'm updating my review to positive. Capcom took a much better direction than the SF4 system, removing braindead option selects and ridiculous 1f links (yes, 1f links are simply bad game design, execution barrier is fine but it should be implemented in better ways like many other titles do... besides, why allow laughable stick input leniency but require 1/60th of a second buttons presses?).
Some new mechanics and game designs were inspired from the Arc System Works titles, probably thanks to consultants like Guilty Gear top player Woshige, refreshing the series and quite frankly, making it more interesting while staying true to the series' spirit.
Now it's all about hit confirms, frame traps, reads and decision making. Looks honest enough.
DPs are a huge asset to get out of pressure, moreso now that most defensive OS are gone, but the guaranteed counter crush combo for the opponent makes up for a whiffed of blocked one.
However, Capcom still badly botched up this release and needs to release a ton of fixes asap.
On the bright side, the March patch content has just been announced.

So for a year or two I've known about most of the half-life series and how good the games are. So durring the steam summer sale of 2017 and the ENTIRE half-life bundle (which includes all the half-life games and DLC) was only $3.48, so I decided "Hey! the games are so popular and the entire bundle is ONLY 3 and a half dollars until July 5th, why not get it?" and since the day i started playing the first half-life game (not the source remaster), which was exactly 6-25-17, I now know why the games are so good despite its age. And here's why
-The gamplay: I've played many FPS games like COD or DOOM 2016, but i can tell you the gamplay is WAY better than
your average FPS game!
-Weapons: like doom, there are diffrent weapons as you play the game, each with its diffrent purpose and gamplay, and
NONE of them are left to waste.
-Many clever and intresting enviroment obstacles and secrets: Valve did a REALLY good job of inventing the most
accurate puzzles and secrets ever created in gaming history. While enviroment puzzles and secrets have been seen in
other games, prior or later, but they dont do it as well as half-life.
-No cutscenes or long black loading screens: all important events in-game are taking place in the game inside through
the player's eyes, and there IS no limit to maps (but there is a loading icon when you reach a curtian point of the map
to load more)
-GREAT storytelling: unfortinatly, I had some spoilers on the series. But even then, it did a good job of what's happening
around you.
-Good 3D graphics (at it's time): I've seen 3D games like quake (which the game's engine, the GoldSource engine, is
based on), but the only game that would be good looking at its time is half-life.
-The game is not dead and people still play online multiplayer and single player: Thankfuly, this game is still being
supported by custom mods and is still having online multiplayer servers (though not as much as TF2, but still enough
players and servers to keep you pre-occupied.)
In short, I give this game a 5/5. I think this game is worth your time and money. Play if you want a intresting FPS experience.

A great take on the open world genre by the people over at Square (EIDOS). The combat is very fluid and easy to pick up, the world is different but relatable, and the story is relatively gripping. The game kept me going for about 21 hours in total. I'd definitely pick this game up if it goes on sale again.

Bottom line: Decent game but short. Do as I did and buy it for under a dollar. Worth at least twice that much though.
The good:
* It's Time Management with a unique queueing system (ie you can queue unavailable items) that actually makes for interesting gameplay.
* The graphics, sound, gameplay etc. are all good.
* The visual and audio feedback work a treat allowing you to know where to spend your attention (and where not to).
* The addition of puzzle pieces is a nice touch. You can even find them before starting the level so you don't have to waste time searching during gameplay.
The bad:
* It's short. I played thru it twice and it still felt like it wasn't worth full retail price.
* It's a little too easy. I got gold on most levels on my first try.
* The effects and tooltips can get in the way of seeing what you're actually supposed to do.
* The "cutscenes" are pretty awful. Badly written and presented poetry sound off above non-animated paper dolls.
* The story itself is a bit confusing too. Perhaps you need to have played to previous games but I doubt it.
* I didn't bother getting the last 3 achievements as I never get anywhere near the developers scores. Maybe you have to click a whole lot of birds. Either way, not worth it.

Queen's Quest 2: Stories of Forgotten Past is one of the better hidden object games from the creators of the Demon Hunter series. It's set in a strange world, that's a weird mixture of fantasy and English folklore and uses the popular feature of recent HOGs: alchemy. Altough not as great as the Artifex Mundi originals or some I've had the pleasure to play with lately, it is certainly an enjoyable one.
After watching the rather in medias res intro (which doesn't make much sense as we later find it out), we step into a nameless female alchemist's shoes, who receives an urgent call from the king. We have to investigate the murder of a wolf (!) who was apparently an agent (!!) of the king. There isn't much about the story to be praised, but we do get to meet interesting characters mainly from the previously mentioned English folklore (Robin Hood, the Sheriff of Nottingham and even Merlin the wizard). Actually the creators went overboard and stuffed so many renowned individuals into the game (we meet Hansel and Gretel as well for example), that it feels utterly ridiculous.
The trendy alchemy feature freshens up the game quite a bit (plus we are an alchemist after all), but isn't as well implemented as seen in other games (like in the amazing Lost Grimoires: Stolen Kingdom): the recipes just pop out of nowhere from time to time and it always means we are to be transformed into an animal (druids don't need recipes for that by the way :P). It has its fun parts though, as we can (or MUST rather) follow animals (like a snail or a hamster) in order to acquire important items or just talk to them (yes, we can talk to them and sometimes we don't even have to transform ourselves to do that).
The minigames are usually the same ones already seen in the Demon Hunter series and there's no problem with them, most of the time. There are some crazy ones towards the end though, which require luck mostly and feel they are just there to prolongate gameplay time. The morphing objects in the hidden object scenes are also present in this game, which the player may like or not (I don't, but they are only considered as minor annoyances).
Again, the use of alchemy is a good course, but sometime it feels a bit forced: when we have too many items in our inventory we most certainly have to reach for our apparatus and create a potion, which means the key to progress. In the first half of the game it works well and we use it logically to get things from otherwise unreachable locations. Oh and don't panic if you can't use a potion, the game isn't bugged, it's just that each alchemy potion has to be used on the correct scene, so you might need to backtrack a bit.
Fortunately there are no twice used HO scenes, so they don't feel like a burden, their locations are logical and their numbers are evenly balanced with the minigames.
There are 2 types of collectibles: puzzle pieces and figurines of fantasy/mythological creatures. It's a nice touch, that the puzzle pieces can be assembled after we found all of them and we can read a short résumé about the creatures matching the figurines.
The game is fairly short (less than 3 hours probably if you get lucky with some of the minigames), but it also has a bonus chapter, in which we get to see Hansel and Gretel (and another familiar "acquaintance") again. It's a very good little expansion and doesn't feel like a chore.
The graphics is great, the scenery is both well designed and colourful plus the fantasy setting makes it even better. We get to visit beautiful highland areas, gloomy forests and royal courts. The quality of the character models seems variable, most of them look very good, some don't. The sound effects are likewise good with fitting music.
The game is enjoyable and feels refreshing with its appealing setting, altough due to the large amount of characters from different tales and folklore it feels awkward and the story suffers from it as well. The fantasy landscape is pleasant to look at and the whole game is relaxing apart from some time consuming minigames. All in all, Queen's Quest 2: Stories of Forgotten Past is a good HO adventure and is certainly recommendable.
PROS
+ interesting gameplay elements, alchemy
+ fantasy setting
+ great visuals
+ good minigames
CONS
- the story isn't that great
- some of the minigames are frustrating
- a bit too wide variety of folklore
RATING
6.5/10

This game is one of my favorite of all time in its genre - it is very emotionally involving and well-written, full of interesting characters and relatively fresh situations. Assuming that you are okay with games with a heavy focus on story and fairly limited gameplay, this is well worth a look.
There are a few winks to the fans but it's completely comprehensible to a newbie. This game actually convinced me to give the show a chance.
Premise: You are Lee, a man on his way to jail when the zombie apocalypse strikes. You stumble upon an abandoned young girl and must protect her through the chaos of the biggest disaster in world history. Along the way, your choices will decide who among your ragtag band of survivors lives and who dies!
The Good: This game really makes you care about its world if you go in with an open mind. The relationship between Lee and his kid protege Clementine is excellently done, starting on a basic level as a protective instinct towards a lost child and developing into a very believable father-daughter type situation. Clem, as kid characters go, is one of the finest gaming has to offer, bringing humor, vulnerability, and a certain moral malleability that forces you to be careful about how you behave, because she will watch and learn from you. The supporting cast is full of different personalities ranging from "psychotic ***hole" to "total Mary Sue" and the way they play off each other when put under the intense stress of the apocalypse is one of the more engaging storyline elements (especially your first time). You never quite know who to trust; some of the most useful allies pull some of the biggest d**k moves at times and some of those seeming the most weak and useless have their moments to shine. As you might expect from the source material, the death count is pretty high. It's about a 50/50 shot whether the next one to eat it will be a beloved friend or cannon fodder they just introduced to have someone to kill off, but the ones that hurt REALLY hurt. The user interface is pretty solid, merging an old school point-and-click adventure setup with a series of quick-time events in action sequences. Most of the time the QTEs are not particularly challenging, but once in a while they'll sneak up on you with something difficult out of nowhere. If you hate QTEs this game will wear on your nerves, but I thought the action sequences were reasonably well done. Meanwhile, the writing and scripting of the game's major events is good in communicating the danger, stress, and difficulty of surviving in a world full of zombies, and definitely does a better job than the television show of commenting on the human condition by way of the various stages of evil, insanity, love, and heroism that manifest in those you meet along the way. The pacing of the story is good, although a segment or two drags on for quite a while.
The Bad: While your choices do matter in the personal journey of Lee and Clem, don't expect multiple endings or big-time changes in the world based on your dialogue choices - this game has a nasty habit of offering you a major dilemna that seems important, but bringing you to the same point ultimately either way. As an early example, a vote to kick someone out of the group leads to the loss of your vehicle if you keep them around, but if you kick them to prevent the problem it just comes up with a slightly different reason to jettison the vehicle a few minutes later. It's also pretty inconsistent whether zombies are a life-threatening horror or a background annoyance - one moment you'll get a scary music sting and frantic button-mashing for a zombie encounter with no story significance, another moment the biggest death in the game is caused by a stupid out-of-nowhere zombie fight that takes three seconds. While I enjoyed the range of personalities in the side characters, I think it would be very easy to be so annoyed with a few of them that it detracts from the game rather than just effecting your in-game relationship with them - so manage your expectation and try to relish in your disagreements with people. Finally, the dialogue and voice acting can veer into the campy realm at times, which occasionally detracts from the very serious problems going on onscreen.
Conclusion: In the end, this roughly splits honors with The Wolf Among Us for my favorite Telltale game and my favorite action-light/story-heavy game. Unless you have something against "interactive movie" type games (which to be fair, this is more than simple an interactive movie), give The Walking Dead a try. For me, it was a memorable, emotional journey that I'll come back to again.

Anyways, this is a nugget sized piece of Black Flag, only with a slave freeing side activity. You get a small area to sail around in and get into ship battles. Little islands to find chests in. I'm gonna go on a whim and say that most of you all reading this review have probably already seen the full playthrough from someone on YouTube... However, if you haven't seen it in a long time I do strongly recommend buying the game. It's just so much more fun making your own decisions in TWDG rather than watching an infuriating playthrough where the player picks the opposite of what you would've picked.
What I love most about the game is that there is so much emotion in it. You will feel bad if you hurt someone mentally by perhaps saying something you shouldn't have. Raise your voice to someone who might feel bad for something they've done. Killing loved ones because they've been bitten etc etc. Sure you may stumble upon a character that you really dislike, it will most likely throughout your playthrough either just kill him or her without you willingly choosing for them to die. Or you'll choose their fate. But then the game will also sometimes kill someone you really like, which kinda upsets you. Or you might not like that character at all but another character in the game likes or loves that person, and then that character might as well be your favorite character in the game which upsets you because he or she is feeling slightly depressed even if you hated the character that died. What I'm trying to say here is that one of your emotions will always click in when playing the game, could be sadness, happiness, anger and so on. It's a great experience.
The downside to the game is how characters can sometimes end up out of place and jitter while they walk like if that specific character was capped at like 15fps. Which is very odd and kinda nasty to look at but it doesn't ruin the experience. It doesn't happen all the time, only in some scenes. I've come to understand that other people have had other bugs that kinda kill the immersion, but me myself never ran into anything like that.
There were however two factors that I was missing when playing Season 1 and that is about the gameplay, and yes, yes, yes... I know it's a point and click game. But whatever they did to TWDG Season 2 was so much better than Season 1. Season 1 was literally just walk for a bit and click which kinda got boring when having to walk back and forth in a room looking for something
Saying that brings up
... In Season 2 you can move faster, it would be nice to be able to do so in Season 1 as well, but unfortunately that's not a thing.
more action with dodging zombies left and right with you analog sticks.
I missed this in Season 1 because I feel like it would've added up to the gameplay a lot more. But that doesn't mean that you should go out of your way and buy Season 2 and not Season 1... Season 1 is a must in my opinion, even if you've seen a playthrough. It's still a great experience without these features and I strongly recommend this game for anyone who just feels like jumping onto a rollercoaster of emotions. It's a great game.

Whether or not you're going to be into Atari Vault comes principally down to your personal taste in retro games. If you want to experience some of the oldest entries in the Atari arcade and 2600 catalogues, you've come to the right place. If you want to experience what many consider the best games on those two platforms, maybe not so much.
The package of Atari Vault itself is largely excellent. Code Mystics specialises in bringing retro games to modern systems and they did a great job here. The emulation is excellent, the presentation of the menus and the bezel artwork is well done and there are a bunch of visual historical extras you can look at, though the scan quality varies. All the games that support two players have full local multiplayer capabilities and to my great surprise, online play! I have no idea how well it works as I unfortunately couldn't find any games. The arcade titles also have online leaderboards which is a very nice value add.
The controller support is a bit of a let down. Controllers are indeed supported and you can remap the buttons to boot but navigating the menus with a controller is clumsy and unintuitive and there's really no reason for it. You'll often find yourself getting frustrated trying to figure out how to get them to pick the thing you want. For a collection that begs to be played on a TV, this is kind of ridiculous. This can definitely be patched and I hope it is.
As for the games, they're some of Atari's oldest offerings. Many of the arcade games are vector based and look quite good, plus Code Mystics added some options to adjust the vector display intensity. Some true classics like Tempest, Major Havoc, Asteroids, Crystal Castles and more are in this lineup and they play quite well for the most part. This is the part that really impressed me. The Atari 2600 line is decidedly more of a let down for me. There's some gems in there like Yar's Revenge but to me, most of the best 2600 games came from third parties like Activision and this being an Atari published package, you aren't going to find those here. Many first party Atari 2600 games haven't aged well at all and if you really are gushing with nostalgia for them, you'll find them pretty rough to play and largely uninteresting.
Overall, this is a very nicely put together package that's had more effort put into it than many others. Whether or not you like the games on offer is going to be down to what you like so take a look at the list first and make sure it's what you want before putting down money. If you are into those games though, there's no better way to play them.

The core purpose of the Achievement Hunter series is to play off the desires of achievement hunters seeking to maximize their scores. Sadly, I am one of those individuals looking to climb the ranks of astats.nl and other such sites. Thankfully the bundle option and a refund on a broken game basically paid for this also broken title.
Yes, the insane amount of achievements seems to be glitched. At the time of writing this, twenty-four of them do not unlock. If you're hoping to tack on another 100%, this one won't fill the void it's designed to fill until an update fixes it. Given similar glitches in others like Run Away, don't expect that correction any time soon.
Achievements start popping as soon as you reach the main menu with the swastika windmill, and don't stop. Atari Vault is a collection of over 100 Arcade and Atari 2600 ranging from sports to blowing up asteroids in space. With this massive selection of games to choose from you will likely spent hours just trying all the games and staring at the included scans of the box art, arcade machine or cartridge for each title. It is both a love letter to those that loved the old Atari company and a great introduction to games of the past in one convenient package. These are quite clearly decade old games with no graphical improvements whatsoever so they will obviously look outdated and the only addition to the graphical presentation are some nifty borders unique to each game. The biggest feature to this collection of games is the ability to use controllers for each game and have custom bindings on a game per game basis which really helps keep you playing as you can fine tune to your liking and never worry about it again.

Most of the games had optimal controller bindings but games like Brickout or Warlords that require a paddle simply do not play well on a controller and makes precise movements much harder. Along with the controller you can use either mouse or keyboard which can also be rebinded however you please. For games that were originally for the paddle using the mouse is really the only way to properly play them if you plan on being any good at them. Now highscores have much more reach than bragging in your local arcades hangout as each game has their own leaderboards to compete against your friends or people around the world. The second biggest feature of this compilation is the ability to play with your friends or random people online though I was sadly unable to use this feature over the course of four days testing as no one plays online. You can be the host and try to set up a match while still being able to play games which is nice but without a community it is kind of pointless. Hopefully it gathers a following in the future but if you are looking for online play you will need to find a friend with this title as of now.

While the games themselves have no improvements I was pleasantly surprised to see the Atari Vault running at 2560x1440p @ 165hz. It makes little to no real difference in the games but it's always nice to have it running at your monitors native resolution and not locked at 1080p 30fps like so many modern games. With Arcade games you can change the lives, difficulty and various other factors while the Atari 2600 games require you to first boot up the game before being able to change anything. It's a nifty little selection screen that is a far better alternative than getting up, flicking the “game select” switch on the console and wondering just what it did if you no longer had a manual. For those that don't know, most Atari 2600 games had multiple modifications to the core gameplay that you could choose from in order to keep the game from getting stale. It also retains the Atari 2600's feature of being able to choose whether to display in color or in black and white if you so choose.

100 games is quite a lot of content no doubt but keep in mind that these are very old games where the point of them is to play for fun or for the highscore. It is primitive compared to today's games and most don't even have music, only bleeps and bloops. With that out the way they are still as fun to play now as they were back then. Even without the realistic graphics and captivating soundtracks of modern games there is still something immensely charming about a pure focus on gameplay and sound effects so primitive that you can't help but kick back and relax. These are the type of games you'd play when you are short on time and want some quick fun. Get in intense dogfights in the Red Baron, continue to suck at Centipede and out drive bandits in Fatal Run all before work or school. With 97 more games to try out and plenty of them having different modifiers to the gameplay you’re bound to find a couple of games that will have you hooked and wanting to make your way up the leaderboard. Atari Vault is definitely a must buy title if you have fond memories of playing Atari's 2600 console or arcade machines and a perfect title for those wondering what gaming was like back then.

Tales of Berseria is an exciting and unique take of the "Tales of" series. You play as a perfectly human character with flaws and passion, and embark on a journey not to save the world, but for revenge at any cost. The best part about this game are the characters and the interactions between them. I never skipped a skit as they were pure gold and the characters really felt like people.
The story is also really gripping. There's twists and turns and is not always predictable like other "Tales of" games. It's also not so bland as Perfectly Good vs Completely Evil either, but rather varying shades of gray. It's hard not to sympathize with the antagonists and realizing that both sides are doing what they believe is right.
The environments of the game are also beautiful. There is nice variety from forests, to volcanos, to tundra, to plains. I have an Nvidia GTX 550 Ti and I believe my settings were High, though not Ultra though I could probably have highest settings at the cost of a small fps drop, but I chose to go with recommended. So the game isn't overly demanding on the GPU.
The combat is also pretty good. You have 4 elemental types and then 1 physical type. Enemies usually have 1 or 2 weaknesses, and the most resistances I saw was 3 on a boss. If you can hit all the weaknesses you should get a soul, though sometimes that didn't happen, especially when I had 1 or 2 souls.
The souls mechanic is difficult to master, as when I was down to 1-2 souls it was often very difficult to get up to 3. The breakpoint combos didn't seem to grant souls when I was at 1-2 souls. I never liked going below 3 souls, and would only do breaksouls when I had 4 or 5 which is the max, even though you can do so at 3 souls. Perhaps the only thing they could have changed was that as Velvet, when you use a breaksoul, you can't die. So against the final boss when my only person with Ressurection died, I had no life bottles, and no healing items, I continually used breaksouls for the last 15-25% of their health, using items to restore my souls when I needed to. The soul restoring item isn't common, I don't think it can be bought, but it was enough that I used 2 or 3 in the last fight. The BG guage fills slowly, and certain characters could unleash multiple Mystic Arts in the same fight when I couldn't activate it once. Perhaps they had lower costs, but the BG guage seemed to fill slowly for Velvet.
The game took me approxmiately 50hrs to beat on medium difficulty. I never lost a fight, and I only ran from one fight that I tried to avoid. The Red Alert demons are pretty difficult after the first few, and these are optional bosses.
If you're a "Tales of" fan, you will probably love this game the same as the rest. If you are new to the franchise, there is still something to enjoy here and is a great entry point.

A clear improvement from Tales of Zestiria and one of the best modern Tales games.
As a general RPG fan you will find this game easier to jump into then Zestiria but as a Tales fan you just need to accustom yourself to new battle controls and your all set. If Steam's character limit will let me I will go over each aspect of the game.
Graphics: 8.5/10. A clear improvement over Zestiria. The engine cutscenes, especially fight scenes, are much more fluid then Zestiria and animations in general are less rigid. Movie cutscenes are fantastic but it does have Zestiria's problem of having many in the first couple hours and having very few toward the end. Characters are well designed except for Velvet's nose (HOW DO U BREATHE VELVET O.O)
Story: 9/10 Easily the best overall story in any tales game I played (I haven't finished Symphonia so I can't compare there). Only one character is remotely generic, your band is a mixed bag of selfish and borderline psychotic people but they manage to mesh together so well, there is not a clear weak link in the cast this time which most Tales games have (Soray/Laliah, Ludger, Cheria, Harold etc). Finally: A revenge story where I actually love the character seeking revenge. Velvet bae af, waiflu for life. She manages to be a psycho seeking vengence and a loving sister all while retaining her general love of cooking and cleaning and a sense of humor. The emotional journey alone is a great story. You don't need to play Zestiria to understand things but it is far more intersting if you have. Certain areas are clear precursors to areas in Zestiria and it is great fun to speculate about the story with knowledge you already have of Zestiria.
Sound Design/Soundtrack: 7/10. The weak point of this game. Sound effects are amazing but the soundtrack is rather weak for a Tales game especially compared to the masterpiece of Zestiria. A few good tracks jumped out at me but mostly the music, though fitting in many places, felt more like backround sounds then an emotionally investing part of the game,
Gameplay: 8.5/10 A clear improvement to Zestiria in item crafting. Gone is the horrendous fusion system and in comes Item Enhancement, a much simplier version that focuses more on RNG loot then fusing skills. Battle feels a bit different because of the new controls but I grew to like it. Break Souls are interesting but I prefer Armatization as my ultra power up. Maps are fantiscally varied, another great improvement over Zesiria but for some reason you move through thses maps far slower, even with the Geoboard. Bosses feel a bit gimmicky at times, to many have reflect damage as a thing. Main story bosses are a bit better though not on par with Vesperia or Graces (I loved Graces bosses for some reason)
Overall Score: 8.5/10. Tales Score: 9.5/10. As a general RPG this is a great game though you might want to wait for a sale if you aren't a Tales fan. As a Tales fan I can easily tell you to spend your money here as I haven't enjoyed a Tales game this much since Vesperia (My golden Tales game) 82 Hours and not even started my second playthrough, that says something about this game :D

It's a shame it didn't sell better, because this is a very, very good game. An excellent and expansive open world, tons of detail, a really terrific storyline, good combat system and plenty of things to do make for a really fun experience that I'd easily recommend over GTA4 or even Saints Row 3.
The storyline, especially, deserves extra mention. Rather than not dealing with the strange dichotomy of Wei being a cop as well as a gangster, it's definitely on the forefront in the whole storyline, and is dealt with well. The triad wars are believable and build at a good pace, and the voice acting is overall excellent. (and you'll have many "hey, it's that guy!" moments.)
The game does have a few pretty big flaws. The driving system is, sad to say, abysmally bad. It feels as if the roads of Hong Kong are covered in four feet of caramel. The Kung Fu system is deep, but it takes several in-game upgrades to become enjoyable. Expect the first few hours to just be punch punch punch punch punch, and it does get a bit boring. Also, the strange kung-fu vs guns issue in the game sometimes leads to situations where you're without a gun, facing off against goons with weapons. Not fun times. The game also has a hand of spawning enemies 5 feet behind you. With assault rifles. :(
The biggest missing mark, however, is the lack of flyable craft. I would have enjoyed flying around Hong Kong's skyscrapers.
But all that doesn't negate the fact that this is an easy 20-25 hours of excellent fun. I feel bad I bought this for only 10 bucks, so I'm going to go buy 30 bucks worth of DLC now.

I don't usually write reviews, but this is an absolutely superb game. After four years of this game and almost 500 hours logged, this game still doesn't get old. I would value the game atmosphere alone at 20$, and would be willing to buy the whole game at a solid 60$.
Pros:
Unique storyline: The dichotomy between the moral thought and loyal obligation is an interesting psychological idea that is portrayed in the main character of Wei Shen. The story gripped me the whole way through, and I still find myself starting to new game just to experience it again.
Atmosphere: The overall feel of the game is also very natural. Between the vibrant colours of the sprawling metropolis of Hong Kong to the the packed streets of the night market, the developers and designers at United Front genuinely put thought and effort into designing an atmosphere that is both authentic, natural, and immersive.
Graphics: I dont need to say much on this one. Brilliantly beautiful.
Fighting/Gunplay Mechanics: The fighting mechanics in this game are generally intuitive and can be picked up easily. The satisfaction of landing a punch on some punk's face also helps. Only gripe with this one is tht the reaction in the game isn't as responsive as I would like. While gunplay isn't the "main" focus of te game, it is definitely polished. The game often helps you lock on to targets (even with a mouse/keyboard), something that I felt was a nice touch (even though it may turn off some people). The guns also have a satisfying punch to them, exactly what I like to see/hear.
Audio: Audio design is very authentic, and gives of the perfect urban feel of Hong Kong. Dialogues are natural (for the most part), and the sprinkles of Cantonese here and there makes the storyline memorable. The audio and visuals also complement each other well. Soundtrack is also impeccable.
Misc. Mechanics: From stuffing gangsters into trunks to gambling in a♥♥♥♥♥♥fight, there are plenty of things to do even when all story-related activities have been completed.
DLCs: Good amount of extra story in the three/four extra story DLCs. It's best to buy these on sale though.
Cons:
Driving Mechanics: Driving doesn't exactly adhere to real-world physics, which gives it an arcadey feel, but it can still suit some people. Drifting is a must.
Glitches: There may be glitch here and there, but overall, really rare.
Animations: Some of the non-cutscene animations can be a bit clunky, but if you don't look too close, you'll hardly notice 'em.
Concluding Thoughts: If you still haven't bought it by now in 2017, you're really behind the times. Buy it now!

tl;dr: Not great, but it's good, and I don't regret buying it.
---------
10/10 would laugh hysterically at a high-level enemy with low health using Clamp Jaw and killing itself without dealing damage again.
For real though, this is a pretty solid Survival RPG.
There are plenty of annoyances:
-Enemies that get a first strike in combat and like to use it to stun a party member.
-Thieves that steal large quantities of resources (like roughly 50% of your stock of them), forcing you to chase them through numerous areas, possibly into areas too difficult for you to handle.
-Only having six slots for healing items, and not being able to just use a new healing item if you don't have space for it (Carrying six medkits, no party members under 80% health and find a burger? Too bad, leave the burger to rot).
-Speaking of your healing item capacity, sodas, cake slices and burgers stack 50 to a slot, but other items don't. So basically, a single syringe or a small medkit takes up the same amount of space and weighs as much 50 cans of soda, 50 slices of cake or 50 hamburgers. Uh... huh...
-Character that has no skill with rifles gives you a difficult side mission (though thankfully not time-limited, like 99% of the missions) to get a sick-awesome AK, then insists on being the only one who can use it, and if you give it to someone else, she throws a hissy fit and leaves forever, keeping any items she had equipped.
However, I do like it enough that I also bought it on mobile (It costs a fraction of the price on mobile, but does have some technical issues the PC version doesn't, such as chugging pretty bad before and after battles, and apparantly crashes on some devices, though I haven't personally had any crashes), and I don't buy a game on multiple platforms unless I find it very enjoyable.
I do think that, provided they iron out the wrinkles, it's kind of better as a mobile game than a PC game. Still, I consider this a good example of why it's generally better to make something for PC then port it to mobile, rather than the other way around. I mean, there's a reason why most people say 'mobile port' in a voice dripping with loathing. Okay, probably not most people, but still, you get my point, yes?
It may not be as grand a project as something from the Final Fantasy series, nor as brilliantly written as the Telltale Walking Dead games, but as a turn-based RPG with a twist of survival that tries to do something with zombies that isn't an FPS... 's pretty good.
I do kinda feel that being 3D maybe hurts the game a bit, I think it might stand out more if it was 2D with an interesting artstyle. More variation between enemies and party members would be appreciated, since several enemies are are basically just reskinned versions of previous ones (or, in the case of a Rager variant, with a fire particle effect on it. Also, sad you didn't call it a Burning Rager, because, y'know... just do it. Just Burning Ragers!).
Scratches my TBRPG itch without being so long that I'll probably never finish it. Not sure if I'd say it's quite worth $15, $10 or so seems more reasonable for what you get, so maybe buy it on sale.
... But seriously, let me use newly found healing items without needing to stuff them in my limited inventory first. I don't even care if you balance it out by making food items not stack, I just don't want to have to leave things behind just because it's a waste to use what I have.

First off, this game is amazing, and a must buy.
Let me tell you why this is so.
This game has a very unique artstyle, and not in a bad way. It's probably one of the best looking games I've had the pleasure to play. The art really gives an atmosphere to the game, which is lacking in most games (In my oppinion).
Another thing done to almost perfection, is the music. The music in this game blew me away, it's action-packed when needed and it's a bit.. "toned down" and emotional, when it's needed. This contributes alot to the atomphere of the game aswell.
The main focus of the game, and the thing you'll be doing the most, is using various weapons to kill creatures, critters and other living things. The game ALSO does great in this part. The combat is responsive, and does not feel like a "mash-to-win" thing. It also requires an amount of skill to master. This is empathised by the game it self, as it has "Training Grounds" where you can unlock 3 tiers of rewards, depending on how good you do a task, where the third tier is perfecting the task (Which is very difficult). This combat system if what I'd call an "easy to learn, hard to master" kind of thing. The game has around 10 weapons, where around half of them are ranged and the other half melee. You also get a "secret skill" which is like a special move, but you can't use it all the time, it has a resource attached to it which you can hold 3 of. You can upgrade your weapons aswell, It's almost impossible to upgrade them all. That's all I'm going to say on that.
Now I think it's time to talk about the story. It's great. I'm not a "story guy" as I apreciate good mechanics instead of a great story. But since this has great mechanics, I started to focus on the story aswell. I'm scared to say anything about it, I'd recomend you to go experience it for yourself.
The levels them self don't get boring either. They are kind of being built, as you go along the path. That's the way this game does secrets aswell, which there are a few of. This makes the levels feel very dynamic, as they're kind of built on the spot.
So now I'm going to repeat my self... Go buy this game. It's worth the price.

I played this game when it came out, and the bug that did not let me progress if encountered, as even reloading save did nothing, infuriating me beyond no belief, shows how much I was into this game. The moment it was patched, I loaded up the save and beat it. Psionics are more accessible than in previous game, and involvement of commander compared to before is bigger in the campaign. Some bits might seem more limited, but with the DLC and everything this game feels far more complete than it did before, could even be considered more than the previous Xcom.
The stealth is a welcome and interesting mechanic and further shows the fact that you ARE a resistance trying to fight against the world.
However, mission timers were a failure of game designers in this game. This punished players that were trying to play patiently, like in previous xcoms, and felt forced. So much that mods were made to get rid of them. I get it that we're resistance and our enemy controls the surrounding areas so they can keep sending reinforcements if we take long, but it feels so counterintuitive to everything the Xcom games stood for.
However, I will still reccomend this game to anyone that likes strategic games. It is well done, it is visually pleasing. I wish there were more customization options than there are now, but it's just a nitpick.

Atari Vault collection is some of the greatest games the 2600 platform offered and it doesn't disappoint. Upon first loading I intended a quick 5min look, 2hrs later I was still glued to my screen. "They don't make them like they used to". While some other packs might nickle and dime, Atari provides great value for money with a well arranged group of classics. Some may only entertain a few minutes for nostalgia sake but I can all but guarantee others should keep you coming back for more. Personally I feel there's enough to justify the price with the included 'arcade/cab' games.
Few things that made it stand out was UI. Both clean and quick to navigate with some well thought out categories. Most games instantly loaded and I was able to drop back to the main screen without troubles. Didn't have many issues with controls but I agree with some other recommendations in saying rebindable options for certain games would be nice. What impressed me most was the overall 'performance' and when I say this I mean how things looked on modern screens. Often when emulating older games I've run into issues with screen tearing and otherwise. Not only was it smooth but currently using a 120hz panel that some modern games have had issues with.
Inclusion of leaderboards and local/online multiplayer for many of the games is just the icing on the cake. Atari Vault gets my recommendation as one of the best retro collections on steam and is well worth checking out or adding to your wishlist. Cheers.

This is the first Tales game I've ever played and damn, what a first impression!
This honestly might be one of my absolute favourite story-driven games of all time, with a story that flows fantastically thanks to great hooks in the early game that keep the action apropriately high all the way through, I never felt like I was wasting my time.
This game is supposedly a prequel to Tales of Zestiria - I found that out when I looked up trivia on the game after beating it - but I would never have guessed that with how well Berseria builds its setting and characters so that they can completely stand on their own. The main party in particularly really are a bunch of lovable rascals who all manage to feel relevant to the plot - particularly impressive since even highly acclaimed games like Final Fantasy VII often aren't quite able to do this.
Honestly my only real beef with this game is one that has already been voiced a number of times, and that is that the dungeon design is a bit crap - but for the most part the combat system was able to keep me entertained enough that I didn't really take much notice until the bonus dungeon which is, sadly, really repititive. And I guess the music is servicable at best? I'm grasping at straws here - other people have talked about technical issues, but I experienced none myself so I can't really talk about them at all.
I guess what this boils down to is:

GAMEPLAY: 7

as with zestiria, this isn't a stellar game. it's a solid jrpg with obscure side-quests, collectables, mini-games, dungeon-crawling, and trope-y, over the top characters. if you like this stuff, and you're not expecting anything absolutely revolutionary, you're going to like this game. especially since the world now feels much more *dense* than zestiria's because the maps are actually filled with stuff and not just huge open plains.
my biggest gripe with the game is the protagonist though. velvet is that special brand of female protagonist that was cleary created as a "strong female character", and while i do want more female protagonists, i'm also sad that very few developers get them right. rose from zestiria, while not being the protagonist, had a much more varied personality (as much as the jrpg formula allows), and, most importantly, she didn't have to be a gender-swapped cloud or squall to prove that she was "tough enough". rose was a tough cookie while still showing emotions - like an actual *person*.
also, since the game does have a female protagonist, and apparently the devs thought this would make people uncomfortable, the game tries to humiliate her (and the rest of the female cast) every chance it gets. especially the "women are deceitful" skit, followed by the "men are simpletons" skit, actually got me decently angry. just like the character bienfu. not only is his english voice actor the most annoying thing to happen to gaming, ever. his personality is that of the stereotypical "otaku pervert", and i get it, they thought it'd be cute if those creepy things were said and done by a mascot character but no. i just feel creeped out most of the time he's on screen. he is my least favorite thing about this game.
jrpgs *always* play with gender stereotypes and most times i'm fine with that because i know ahead of time what i'm getting myself into, and i can still enjoy something ( a lot!), even when i don't like everything about that thing. but in berseria it's painful, and sometimes creepy.
another smaller problem i have with the game is that it constantly feels the need to remind me that "we're the bad guys". i get it. you're fighting against the established religious institution. you don't have to tell me over and over again. *i get it*, jesus f*cking christ! but i guess this can also be chalked up this being a jrpg, so ultimately, it's fine, i guess.
nonetheless, i still recommend the game. it's no revelation, but it's solid, it works well, it flows nicely, and the characters do have their moments. i wouldn't get it at full price though, maybe wait for a sale. and get zestiria first. in my opinion, zestiria has an overall stronger narrative and better characters.
P.S.: best thing about this game: background information on eizen. and eizen in general.

=====Major Issue======
Players are intentionally DCing from matches to fabricate their Online Rank and Winstreaks - otherwise known as "Ragequitting".
Ragequitting has been far too popularized over the past 2 days and is running rampant as there is no punishment system in place to even attempt to enforce honest play. As of the last 2 days 1/3 of my ranked wins were ragequitted out having nothing to show for the matches other than a few screenshots. Thanks to the absurd amount of server issues and rage quits I have 40+ hours in this game and next to nothing tho show for it to no fault of my own.
Leaving this Review as negative until Capcom addresses this.
===================
Less than 24 hours post (early) launch and the server issues have been heavily mitigated and are functioning just fine. The game lacks a serious story mode and pure arcade ladder but survival and early story modes should suffice as Capcom did state that the full story mode would not release along side the game.
In the current state the game caters to players who want to play online. If you are looking for a solid single player experience you can easily clear though all the basic solo content in a few sessions. Survival and training could easily net you a ton of solo play time if you are interested in getting gud. So be warned single players.
The "main issue" (so to speak) is controller support - but if you are the kind of person so splurge on a fightstick then you should be willing to spend 5mins implementing a temporary work around. Should Capcom have had implanted D-Input support at launch? Of course. But its far from a deal breaker.
The game is fun, the mechanics are solid, and there is a lot to do if you are looking to hone your skills and climb the online ladder or just play with friends. Netplay works very well albeit it can be difficult to find a match at times. There is a guaranteed years worth of updates planned for this game (both free and paid) and there is likely many more years of support to come. If you are looking for a solid fighter and your key interests focus on learning mechanics and playing online then look no further. This game will have solid post launch longevity and, as the newest entry into the Street Fighter series, the online community will be around for quite a while.

If I could describe SF5 right now in one word that word would be rushed.  As it stands this game is very much incomplete with basic fighting game features with promises to fix things next month in a content patch.  What we have at launch is a story mode which is embarassingly easy and feels tacked on in the last minute if you see the content of the story and the laughable quality of the artwork. Seeing as how we're keen on giving Capcom a free pass on the quality of their single player story mode that leaves the online multiplayer and local multiplayer. I don't have any real experience with local multiplayer yet but in regards to the online mode the netcode is worse than USF4's which is to be expected considering it is a cross platform game but that alone doesn't excuse Capcom considering they've had a beta for six months. While It's commendable that the dev team has focused a lot of attention to balancing the game it's absolutely deplorable how they treated the rest of the game.
With all that said, unless you're playing local vs. mode or if you have a group of friends that will play with you you should consider waiting until March when the patch arrives with much needed online matchmaking features, more single player content, and a plethora of bug fixes which should have been fixed during the beta.
The foundation for a good game is there but I can't in good conscience recommend SF5 to a new player unless they already have people diving in with them until all these issues are addressed. When that day happens I will be happy to change this review but until then, it's just a shoddy rush job.

First off, this game is amazing, and a must buy.
Let me tell you why this is so.
This game has a very unique artstyle, and not in a bad way. It's probably one of the best looking games I've had the pleasure to play. The art really gives an atmosphere to the game, which is lacking in most games (In my oppinion).
Another thing done to almost perfection, is the music. The music in this game blew me away, it's action-packed when needed and it's a bit.. "toned down" and emotional, when it's needed. This contributes alot to the atomphere of the game aswell.
The main focus of the game, and the thing you'll be doing the most, is using various weapons to kill creatures, critters and other living things. The game ALSO does great in this part. The combat is responsive, and does not feel like a "mash-to-win" thing. It also requires an amount of skill to master. This is empathised by the game it self, as it has "Training Grounds" where you can unlock 3 tiers of rewards, depending on how good you do a task, where the third tier is perfecting the task (Which is very difficult). This combat system if what I'd call an "easy to learn, hard to master" kind of thing. The game has around 10 weapons, where around half of them are ranged and the other half melee. You also get a "secret skill" which is like a special move, but you can't use it all the time, it has a resource attached to it which you can hold 3 of. You can upgrade your weapons aswell, It's almost impossible to upgrade them all. That's all I'm going to say on that.
Now I think it's time to talk about the story. It's great. I'm not a "story guy" as I apreciate good mechanics instead of a great story. But since this has great mechanics, I started to focus on the story aswell. I'm scared to say anything about it, I'd recomend you to go experience it for yourself.
The levels them self don't get boring either. They are kind of being built, as you go along the path. That's the way this game does secrets aswell, which there are a few of. This makes the levels feel very dynamic, as they're kind of built on the spot.
So now I'm going to repeat my self... Go buy this game. It's worth the price.

The community of this game is nice and everyone is usually kind to each other besides the occasional scammers and spammers (like every other MMO). The game is not for everyone and I understand that, but if you enjoy murdering everything and going through dungeons with friends this game is for you. There is something of everyone in this game, for people who like to build you can join a club and creat whatever or simply design you cornerstone (base that moves throughout worlds). Or if you like murdering people in PVP and mounting the trophys of people you killed on your wall (literally) then you can do that to!
No this game is not a PTW (pay to win) game. It's optional to use money but if you don't you still can play the game fine. There are new things being added all the time and millions of weapons, hats, masks, costumes, ect. The art style for the game is called Voxel and easy to make new items and submit them and potentially have them added to the game! There are many different classes to choose from if your into games with diverse characters. And yes some are better than others. One of my favorite features in this game is the cornerstone. Within Different worlds you will find a cornerstone plot and pressing E on the sign will build your cornerstone, if you build/destroy anything on it those edits will be transferred throughout worlds (every world has cornerstone plots).
The controls for this game are simple (or many just because I'm used to them). Some controls are weird so just ask in global chat and people usually respond. Another great feature is if you have a weapon that looks bad but does good danger you are able to "collect" the good looking weapon and change the appearance of the bad looking weapon but still keeping the better stats, same with hats and masks. Anyway this game is a lot of fun and you should stop reading this and go play it. Thanks :3

For Those who played enemy unknown:  It has plenty of similarities, but is very different as well, you have much more of a feel of flying around frantically trying to deal with every problem, and the biggest difference (even compared to EW and meld timers) is you always feel like you're on a clock, especially at the strategic level.  Many Missions have a time limit and this adds a lot of urgency.  Sometimes the time limits can feel unfair or frustrating but I think its a fair tradeoff to a boring game of overwatch crawling as soon as the meld is gone.  Another change is the game is really pretty (which can be a performance problem on a loer end machine), but it looks really cool when you blow stuff up.  There are a lot more character customization options too, and mods add a ridiculous amount of different props and voicepacks.
For those who haven't played any xcom:  A very fun and engaging experience, guide your squad from 4 starting noobs to be the badasses the aliens fear, get all sorts of upgrades and so on along the way and face ever more scary aliens.  If you can think of a way to kill aliens you can probably do it in this game; shoot them, stab them, blow them up, light them on fire, poison them, even kill them with fall damage.  There are also many hilarious moments in this game, like when aliens fail to hit your decoy beacon.
The biggest feature for me is the mod compatibility, so the game can really be what you make of it, it has a core tactical sqaud based gameplay that can be built on massively by mods.

Here it is -the ground breaking first album!!  This game has been held up as a shining example of games story-telling and begs the question - when does a game become art?? I had not watched the walking dead, or read the comics prior to playing this game and other than knowing its about zombies, knew little else.  I was very surprised at what i found, quickly realising that the whole point of 'The Walking Dead' is that it isnt always readily apparent who the monsters are. (I subsequently watched 5 seasons of 'The Walking dead' - I know I'm behind).
I have to point out that as a dad the emotional attachment you develop with Clementine, really does work and you do become emotionally attached to what is essentially a series of 1s and 0s, you do care for the characters and that is a testament to the quality of the writing here.  I have completed numerous tell-tale games since and this is still one of the best (psst - get tales from the Borderlands !!), though this really was the trailblazer with the - 'x will remember that' after you put an axe in his head. Though the writing is sublime as you can expect from what is essentially a point and click game - the game play isnt gound breaking.  You should play this for the story not an adrenalin rush.
it is an experience and do youself a favour - play it through once. go with it and play it, see whre it goes - there are no wrong answers, trying to get a perfect run through will ruin the game for you. On my first play through I just went with it - i have subsequently played it through on numerous occasions and seen the various story arcs etc and where it leads, like the guy looking to learn the magicians tricks, going for the perfect response all the time leads to disappoinment.
I wouldn't pay 18 quid for it now, but if its on sale, and you havent played this give it a go.  Its another one of those 'gateway' games which you can play on the couch with the other half (providing they are not screamish) and it has that -whats happening next vibe that will keep you going.

While the job that the developers have done is very admirable in bringing back authentic replica versions of every arcade and Atari 2600 console game in this collection, for me.. a kid who grew up loving these games..
All of these games have aged considerebly since I loved them so much back in the early 80's.  For almost every game here, there are probably dozens of games that do it better in every way for FREE available online.
If you are wanting to buy this to try and re-create all the fun and joy you remember having playing these games back in the 80's, like I was hoping for.. you might feel disappointed.  However, if you go in understanding that this collection will really only hold a significant value as "nostalgia", then it might be worth the price.
I used to be a Missile Command and Arcade Asteroids fan back in the day.. but this collection while true to the original games just didn't have anywhere near the same appeal today.  This collection was a refund for me, with the possibility of picking it up again if it goes on sale at 50% to 80% off.. should that ever happen.
Hope this helps someone make a choice while not making too many people shy away from a purchase.  ..Remember that you always have 2 weeks and 2 full hours of game time to refund this collection if you decide the value isn't there, just like I did.

As a sort of prequel to Tales of Zestiria, I would recommend playing it or watching the anime before delving into Tales of Berseria. The world building is insane with the amount of cameos and references to Zestiria, and you learn what happens to some key characters in this game. That being said, Berseria is a much better
, with its upgraded gameplay mechanics and better story. I ran it at 1440p, highest settings at 60 fps with a i7-4790K and a GTX 1070. That being said, this game probably isn't very demanding, so most people should be able to run it. The graphics aren't as realistic as newer JRPGs like FFXV or Nier: Automata, but this is a Tales game and it absolutely shines with its Tales-esque theme; it's gonna grow on you. The difficulty ranges from Simple, Normal, Moderate, Hard, Intense, and Chaos. For your first playthrough, I wouldn't go over Hard unless you buy the DLC that gives you all those bonuses.
Some think that the game is simply too long. It took me about 70 to 80 hours to complete all the main and side missions while playing on Hard and Intense. I am currently in the EX Dungeon, which is a whole another thing. The story follows Velvet Crowe, a 16 year old girl living a complacent life in the relatively peaceful village of Aball. You go about hunting prickleboars and tending to your sickly younger brother, Laphicet. Then, everything changed when
your older brother in law ♥♥♥♥s up everyone and everything you knew to build an ideal world and throws you into a hellhole to fester your hatred.
3 years later, some events happen and you are out for blood. Joining you out of rather weak, convenient, and rather funny motives are a whole slew of other playable characters. At the end, your party consists of 6 people, most of which play very differently. They're pretty happy-go-lucky about your plans to kill the savior of the world, and you really begin to fall in love with these characters with the cutscenes and skits, which are just images and text between characters. However these skits are one of the primary ways this game does world building and character development, so I don't recommend skipping them. Honestly, this whole story is very tragic as almost every character is flawed or broken in some way before, throughout, or even after the game. The whole spin on being the Lord of Calamity rather than the Shepherd, as in Zestiria, was something I can really appreciate and I rate the story as one of the best I've played in JRPGs. Seriously emotional if you took the time to watch and read the cutscenes and skits.
I began this game on Japanese, as I do with the majority of my JRPGs, but I eventually switched to English due to not being able to understand anything during more intense moments of gameplay where I couldn't afford to read since I would probably die. The switch however, was surprisingly welcome, as all of the characters were superbly voice acted. Some have their quirks but I honestly attribute that to their character and how the VA wanted to interpret them (Bienfu, Turtlez, Katz). The only lackluster part of the English version were the NPCs daudling about in town, but honestly, it's probably not going to bother anyone enough to make them hate the English dub. Rokurou, Shigure, and Magilou were among my favorites. The music... well, the ambient music stays pretty much the same within the set areas and it's unfortunate because the character themes themselves shine. Go listen to Velvet's theme, Magilou's theme, or some of the later battle themes and you'll wish the ambient music could step it up a bit. During the game, you unlock costumes which override the default battle music, and I recommend trying them out. Eleanor's outfit in particular.
As with every Tales game, there are artes, which are just basically "moves" you can perform. You chain them, cancel them, mystic them, link them with other characters to bring down enemies. Since there are so many, you can really customize the way you play. The combat system is more refined than Zestiria's, as I found it to be smoother and easier to chain combos, although that could just be because Velvet is utterly broken. The AI honestly isn't that bad and they even managed to carry me through harder battles. Just take off Magilou's mines and some healing artes/revives if you dont want them to be unnecessarily spammed.
Each area has their own set of mobs, and if you manage to kill a lot of them, Dire Foes show up to ruin your day by being at least double your level and accompanied by unkillable allies. The bosses consist of Code Red Hunts, which are optional hunts within dungeons which reward money, the bosses from the main story, and sidequest bosses, which are honestly some of the hardest fights in the game (Phoenix...). The previous advantaged and disadvantaged encounters return from previous games and I recommend disadvantaged for grade farming, if you wanted to do NG+. Berseria brings new things to the table like Expeditions which help with cooking, which is pretty key to the game, and who doesn't like free stuff?
One of the cons I can think of would be the equipment. So, there's a whole plethora of equipment of varying rarities and you eventually get bonuses for how many times your worn equipment have been upgraded. Unfortunately, upgrading the newest gear takes a lot out of your inventory like Odorless Fluids and the types of Tempering Powders. I can barely manage +15 across the board and I've beaten the main story, but the last of the bonuses come when you've enhanced a total of 50. And within those equipments come various random skills of various tiers and numbers. If you play on harder difficulties, you'll probably get items with 3 random skills of tier 3 rarity, while simple or easy will probably net you one random skill of probably the lowest rarity. RNJesus help us.
So if you've stuck around enough to read all this, I'm surprised and appreciate it. All in all, I think this is one the best games I've ever played, especially in the past few years. I've spent over 500 hours in the Witcher 3 + all its expansions and loved the vast majority of it, and Tales of Berseria is what I would consider the JRPG equivalent. It takes concepts and gameplay elements from its previous games and gives you a great cast of characters, none of which I hated (edit: actually, screw Zavied, holy crap. Great musical theme though), and a tragic and engaging storyline.
Honestly, I didn't like the game at first because I couldn't move around quickly or the game would send me from point A to point B to point A to point C to point A to point B. But I guess the Witcher kinda did that too and I had to mod for fast travel anywhere :/. The references to other Tales games is ridiculous and if you've watched or played Zestiria, you get another dose of remorse and look at the characters in a new light. However, much like The Witcher 3, you don't need to play the previous games to jump right in and enjoy the game. I'm really excited for a second playthrough, once I beat this EX dungeon and get enough grade for NG+.

A quick and fun indie puzzle platformer, Dyadic brings back local co-op with it's intuitive controls and simple mechanics. There are some quirky interactions with traps and doors that I discovered by accident, but used effectively, can hinder or kill your partner. When playing this with friends the local aspect really increased the chances of messing someone up to steal back the glowing statue.
The music also provides a nice ambience and feel to the aesthetic stages which also provide information needed to solve some of the more difficult puzzles.
The game is quite short, but you can have a decent amount of replayability with new friends (because you'll know where all the traps are).
Overall quite an enjoyable indie title, especially if the local co-op feel of the game appeals to you.

The visuals in the game are fantastic. As you move, the ground around you lifts into place, as you rebuild the world after 'The Calamity'. Everything looks great, from the characters and objects, along with the terrain and backgrounds.
The music is very good for every level, but there is one song in particular that I loved - it is a reminds me of the Firefly opening theme song. Other video game music has been great to listen to, like the Halo soundtracks or some 8- and 16-bit songs, but this one is my favorite and I don't think anybody would hear it and say "that's a nerdy video game song."
And on top of the music, there is another great audio feature where what you do triggers narration. It is very cool to walk around in the game and have a someone narrate your actions, even sometimes small things.
Rating - 88
Overall - There are about 10 different weapons you can choose to use, but I stuck to about 4 of them, except when I was forced to use the other ones. Unfortunately, mastering all the weapons does help you unlock things you need to complete the game to 100%. There is another feature where you can enable specific challenges during a level, but I never tried doing one of these and didn't feel like I missed anything. One of the things I kept wishing for was the ability to jump - you do get a 'roll' maneuver, and it is a necessary thing to master, because you move faster for some reason while rolling.
Despite these detractions, the gameplay was challenging but not stubbornly difficult and the variety of weapons lets you play however you like playing. The visuals, music, and narration are polished to perfection. You don't get much in the way of character development, but the story is better than average. I was tempted to play through a 2nd time, which is not common for many games to achieve.

Just finished the game last night. This game is RIDICULOUSLY good. It's probably one of my favorite 'Tales of' in recent years. While I enjoyed the Xillia series, Tales of Graces, and the previously released Zestiria, this one in particular puts you behind a character that's hell bent on nothing but revenge and takes you on this roller coaster of an emotional journey.
The battle system in Berseria is a huge step-up from Zestiria, where the battle does NOT take place there-and-then when you encounter an enemy! Each face button corresponds to whatever move set you want, even choosing particular elemental attacks that could make it easier to win in battle. You could also swap between two other characters in battle in case your character is nearing their death, a nifty change in pace during battle. But of course, at the cost of a Blast Guard (BG). The improvement in the battle system is big for me because it's really all you're going to be doing the majority of the game, and having nuisances like narrow corridors (*cough*Zestiria*cough*) can be a pain!
The story is amazing. It got me easily hooked, much quicker than Zestiria and previous Tales of titles. Seeing everything from a much more darker perspective is "refreshing", and the supporting cast does a great job as well.
It's not much of a review, but I just wanted to at least write something on here and give you an insight on how the game is from my end. If I had to score it out of 10, I'd give it a 9.
