My only complaint is that you have to play through all of TWD 1 to play S2.
I do understand this choice, but they should of added the save creation mechanic like TWD S3 did.

In short
I can recommend this game, assuming you know what you are getting yourself into. As stated by other reviewers, the tag "game" is stretching it a bit. The tag adventure ... seriously Steam. You basically watch episodes of The Walking Dead and at certain intervals you can make a choice or shoot a zombie (and this can be quite enjoyable if you are into that kind of thing).
The Wuts
As said, you are put in an episode of The Walking Dead and basically make the same choices and mistakes the characters in the tv serie do. It matches the setting of the series quite well. You'll recognize many locations and situations. Ever thought you'd do things differently? Well maybe now you can. I say maybe, because the game will also make a lot of choices for you. Some characters are really engaging, like the little Clementine. Without her I would probably have stopped playing halfway down the line. She is awesome and kewl.
The BUTs
Even though the game can be quite enjoyable, there are quite a few BUTs. Some are pet peeves of mine, others might be important to other players as well. As I was expecting a game, I was a bit dissapointed by the game elements. There aren't actually that much actions and choices. You will be mostly watching cutscenes. A lot of those cutscenes will be people bickering and staring at eachother (or just off in the distance). This makes the game very, very slow. The cellshaded graphics don't help unless you consider it to be art (which I do not). Movement is very clunky and the world is littered by invisible walls. A lot of the time you'll be guessing where you are going (luckily you can't go that far). The point & click part is very limited as well. So it's basically about the choices. The game invests heavily in the "illusion of choice" and does it quite neatly. It states if people remembered or liked your remark and at the end of a chapter you can see if other people made the same choice. However, the further you progress in the game, the more you'll detect that most of you choices don't actually matter. The same people will still die, the same♥♥♥♥♥♥will still hit the fan. Actual choices that matter are horrible for game designers because they need to add huge amounts of content. Hence I can imagine players are pushed towards the same outcome. Howeverrr, the game actually advertises the game adapts to you choice. Then it should make good on its promise right? As the game is quite short, I expected more impact based on the choices I made.
All in all, if you are a fan of the series you'll probably be able to enjoy these extra episodes. If you expect a fullfledged game, you might want to pick up a different zombie game.
ps. the 400 days DLC is silly, it only contains a few very short scenes that actually end when things get interesting. Even at 4.99eu I can not recommend it unless you are a HUGE fan (apparently there are lots of those)

Berseria starts off as Tales of Dark Souls.
The game begins with you sent to a remote prison for cursed people, and the only way out is blocked by a large demon. You're also going to need a key from a sword and shield soldier with blue armor named Oscar. This is all so you can go out  into the wide world to find a left-handed, one-armed holy knight named Artorius who made a pact with an ancient serpent creature at the bottom of a dark pit. This isn't even mentioning the souls you have to pick up along the way; glowing white orbs scattered seemingly all over the place.
Did I say Tales of Dark Souls? Sorry, I meant Tales of Bloodborne.
On a night with a red moon, men turn into vicious monsters (often werewolves), and it's up to a handful of elite hunters dispatched by a seemingly all-good church to deal with the horrors before more people fall victim to whatever mysterious disease runs rampant throughout the kingdom.
On a more serious note (really the similarities stop there, but you can tell *someone* on the dev team is a Soulsborne fan) the game's story begins happily and cheerfully in an idyllic little village. This, of course, isn't Stardew Valley so the entire situation goes♥♥♥♥♥♥up really, really fast, and then things get worse, atrocities are committed (mostly by you), people die (many thanks to you), lives are ruined (by you), children get kidnapped (you, again), etc. etc. All this in the first 2-3 hours!
However, the game never loses that classic Tales silliness that makes it such a fun series.
-Oh, there's an assassination that needs doing? Can I play waiter for a few minutes instead?
-The time has come for revenge, the final showdown... and no, I will not take off my pompadour with a kitten riding on it.
-Need a new blade to cut through the eldritch horrors blocking your path? I think that kid in turtle pajamas has one for ya.
The only real complaint I have is just how dull revisiting some of the dungeons can be. Most of them are pretty copy+paste with few branching paths, and those that do sometimes have just irritating mechanics (like turning on and off different colored gates, and you don't know what color you need up ahead so you'll often need to just backtrack.) This is a pretty minor complaint though.
Overall the game has an excellent plot (you will think it's predictable, but then you see how far it goes), great characters, an adequate setting (made better if you've played Zestiria, as you'll notice some of the ruins you crawled through in that game are, well, NOT ruins in this one), an addicting and satisfying combat system -- assuming you don't get unlucky and get stunned to death because you got greedy.
It's absolutely worth your money and time if you're a Tales fan, and it's a damn good introduction to the series if you can put up with the tonal whiplash between very dark and horrifying scenes intercut with extreme goofiness.

Assassin's Creed: Freedom Cry.
While not throwing stealth away completely, this game trades up stealth for some head on action sequences.
You play as Adewale, 15 years after the events of Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag.
Older, wiser and now a fully trained assassin. He even gets his own murder hood.
Much of the in game assets were from ACIV:BF so the graphics are more or less the same. Gameplay wise as well, but again more action than stealth really. And his attack animations, though not as fluid or graceful as i expected assassins would be, he has a sort of brutal flair that really defines him as an assassin. Not just Edward Kenway reskinned to be Adewale.
Weapons in Freedom Cry are different as they got rid of swords and daggers. You get machetes for Adewale instead. (This does not prevent you from picking up and using a sword from a slain enemy.)
No flintlock pistols, just a blunderbuss for you, Ade.
You still have your own pair of Hidden Blades of course.
The whole campaign itself is short and sweet. It left me wanting more from it, more of what happens to Adewale, more of what becomes of the liberated slaves and their resistance and more of what happened to the Assassins after Black Flag.
For a DLC turned standalone game, it has a lot more content than one would expect.
Honestly i thought it was just gonna be a bunch of uninspired self contained missions, but this totally blew me away.
I dare say Adewale was more fun to play with than Connor. But of course, that is my opinion.
Get it on sale if you feel that $15 is still too much. Get it however you can as it is a very good game and you won't really regret playing it.

In this review I want to state the five biggest reasons why I hate this game.
TL;DR:
(This video is not by me)
Fallout 4 doesn't have anywhere near the RPG elements of the Fallout games from the past (excluding Brotherhood of Steel and Fallout Tactics)
The ♥♥♥♥♥♥ quests.
The dumbed down leveling system.
Creation club. ♥♥♥♥. Creation. Club.
Ok so first off I would like to say that I have a lot of time in this game as far as RPGs go for me, around 100 hours. The biggest problem with Fallout 4 when compared to other games is that if you want to play as two people; a distressed parent, or a distressed parent who murders everyone.
I feel that a big reason many people defend this game is it feels better than every other Fallout game in the actual shooting and combat mechanics, which is definitely true, but that isn't the point of a Fallout game. If I wanted good gunplay, I would play Battlefield or any other of the hundreds of triple A shooters on the market. I would take Fallout New Vegas's sub par combat paired with it's absolutely amazing role playing features over Fallout 4's good gunplay supplemented by ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "role play" any day.
The game's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chat wheel function only allows for 4 options, minimum or maximum. This is really stupid, as sometimes you need more options, sometimes you need less. You can see this in Fallout 4, as often times different choices on the chat wheel say the exact same thing. I think that the reason they chose this system was because they had voice actors, and didn't want to have to voice more than 4 lines for every dialogue.
I for one, do not much care for having my character voiced. It takes away the "be anyone you want" feel, that this game is already lacking.
Another problem is the way quests are set up. Every single quest, excluding the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ radiant quests, is just a stupid fetch quest. There are never any interesting quests like you find in Falout: New Vegas. Take "One for My Baby" from Fallout New Vegas, where you have to do some detective work to find the right person to be shot, or, if you want to, just haul some random sucker out in front of the dinosaur and watch their head explode. You also have quests like "Ain't Nothin' but a Hound Dog" where you have to get a new brain for Rex the dog. You can get the brain from multiple places, and depending on which one you use, Rex will get a new trait. Compare these with nearly every Fallout 4 side quest where it is either a fetch quest or a radiant quest. Also, Bethesda, can we please not have another missing family member storyline in the next Fallout game?
Next we have the dumbed down leveling up system, where everything is a perk you can get based off of your special level. This leads to boring perks like +20 percent damage. The only reason these perks exist is to make up for the lack of skill points, which, in other fallout games, did all of the boring leveling up, and the perks were always fun.
I feel like many of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ or removed features, excluding the chat wheel, are a direct result of Skyrim's success. It had terrible fetch quests, and everyone loved  it, but I've been typing for a half hour now and I'm not reviewing Skyrim, so you can  just watch the video by MisterCaption, where he basically says what I've said.
Lastly there is Creation Club, which should be called "Give us your ♥♥♥♥ing money."

Fallout 4 has become a chaotic and controversial topic online.
The truth of the matter is that Fallout 4 underwhelmed with the dialogue system and quest variety. This wouldn’t be so much of a problem if it wasn’t for the fact that the combat was so good in stark contrast to the role playing and the fact that the game is set in the Fallout universe.
Fallout is supposed to be about choice and dialogue. That’s the whole thing! The combat is supposed to be an afterthought—not the priority!
That being said, this is an entry that gels well with the rest of the games. If you want to go deep into dialogue, you can play the first ones. If you want action, you can play this one. And if you want something in the middle, just the right amount of both, you can play Fallout 3 or New Vegas. They all have their place and they all excel at what they do best.
Would I recommend Fallout 4? Absolutely! It’s the game that made me fall in love with the series and go on to buy the rest of the Fallout classics!
Is it the perfect Fallout game? Absolutely not. That’s simply impossible.
At least we learned something from all of this. Never pay more than 20 bucks for a Bethesda game.

If you like tower defense games, you will probably like this one!
But it's not exactly a tower defense game!
It's a combination of a tower defense, RTS and something called an orbital shooter.
Tower defense?
You just build towers in the key places.
RTS?
Send your units to take over structures and defend them... Again, seems simple.
Orbital shooter?
Click on the map and you'll shoot there. It takes some time for projectiles to hit, so you need to aim to keep in mind movement speed and direction of the enemies.
When these three simple elements are put together, the game becomes really interesting!
- In classic tower defense game:
You would build/upgrade towers and watch enemies getting killed by them.
- In this game:
You will be shooting enemies from orbit and praying to get enough resources to build a tower before you will get overwhelmed. With tower placed, you can then get more resources, because you can send your units to gather them.
Your units will move and you will try to keep enemies away from them. With air strikes. Don't hit your units! Meanwhile, enemies will also move towards your base... Or bases in some maps. And control points. God help you if your control points get re-corrupted by enemies! Then you will have fewer towers, with fewer towers enemies will overwhelm you, taking away your databases, your resources and finally... It will be the end!
There's also good guys moving with enemies, DO NOT SHOOT THEM! You will be like: Oh no, my control point is attacked by yellow triangles! NUKE EVERYTHI- Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥ there's good guys! Need to switch to a smaller gun.
While you will be slowly picking yellow triangles one by one with the small gun, the evil giant yellow triangle will approach your base...
But hopefully there's red power up near your base, so you will shoot it, it will explode and probably you'll prevail. Too bad you accidentally hit the good guys and they died anyway.
BUT WAIT! While you were fighting Bill Cipher, your database got re-corrupted and it no longer produces delicious blue squares. Which are, like, super important, because without them you can't build towers and launch air strikes.
And that's only if you aren't crippled by challenges! Sometimes you aren't allowed to use big guns, sometimes you need to not lose a single unit, sometimes...
Still reading? Go buy and see it for yourself.
EDIT: Just completed the game, enjoyed every second of it! Last levels are extremely intense and it feels really good to beat them.
EDIT 2: Added missing articles, corrected grammar.

I want to give this game a good rating. I really do. But sadly, this game does not deserve it.
I've tried this game a couple of years ago when it first came out. It was absolutely broken and pretty much unplayable. Now that I got an opportunity to try it for free I checked it out again.
It got only a bit better than it was before.
List of weird stuff I've experienced:
1. The AI is REALLY stupid. The cars bump into each other (some of them fly away when it happens).
2. When you're looking for a criminal, you can find him often being stuck at the wall of some building.
3. The car still gets damaged pretty much all the time (especially when at the gas station) and the fuel runs out very fast.
4. Pretty much 50% of the down population have serious problems. Most of the cars they drive are damaged, they're often drunk.. sometimes when you drive through the city, people get out of their cars and try to shoot me. (as far as I know the bullets still do nothing to the cars)
5. Spending time with people is a joke. Why would I get a round of applause every time I spent some time with someone?
Afterwards, I get teleported to their homes and there's a police vehicle parked in there. What is the point of it? I can't get into it when I'm off duty.
6. The optimisation is still very bad. The game has very low quality models and terrain, visibility on low settings is like 10 meters.. yet it still runs like crap. As a hobbyist Unity developer, I know that it could be optimized to be much more efficient than it currently is. I think that the devs had just given up on it.
7. The vehicle controls are REALLY bad. I'm absolutely sure that for all the money that this game have made, the developers could have purchased a decent car controller script from the asset store, instead of having all the players struggle with the current one.
I don't think that the developers of this game have consulted any police officer.
Why would the officer have to go to the mechanic and repair his vehicle on his own cost, while being on duty? The same goes for refueling. It's paid for by the state/country. I guess that it's an unsuccessful attempt to prevent the game from being boring.
Absence of other police officers is also un-immersive. I suppose that it could be justified with the station being understaffed, but I can't imagine an officer responding to a kidnapping or an armed robbery alone and singlehandedly arresting everyone.
Also - Tazer is not a bow. The character doesn't have to aim at the sky to hit a suspect with it.
And the last thing - the price. This game at this state is definitely not worth this price.
On the other hand, I liked the car models and their customisation. Music is not bad as well.
I'm not impressed with the rest though, sorry.
Overally - I'm disappointed.

この作品に関してはそれすら考える事がめんどくさくなる程に本作をゲームとして楽しめる要素はありませんでした。ですが私はどうしてもこのクソゲーを間違って買う人が一人でも減る事を願い、こうしてレビューを認めています。とは言え、私の文章力では本作の一体どこが面白くないのかを挙げる事も出来ません。なぜならば、本作をプレイした47分間のただ一片とも「ここは面白かったな」と思える箇所が無いからです。
ゲームエンジンの問題からキャラクターのRagdollが突如プルプル震えただとか、85度くらいの斜面を車両でBig Rigsよろしく登りきれるだとか、なぜか自宅と警察署を除く全ての建造物の内部に家具などが一切なく、屋内でも外が雨ならNPCが室内で傘を差しているだとか、おもしろSSやネタ動画のソースとしては使えない事もない事を除き本作を楽しめる方はごくごくごくごく僅かではないでしょうか。
主人公であるあなたは理由はよく分かりませんが片田舎に引っ越すと同時に自動的に警察官になっています。あなたの自宅には専用のパトカーが友人か何かのジョージによって置かれたまま放置され、お前は警察官になったんだから自由に使っていいという事を自宅のPCのemail内で明かされます。おわり。
私はいたって真面目にこのレビューを執筆しています。先のあらすじを書いた本当の理由はこのゲームは一事が万事このようなノリのまま全力でプレイヤーを置き去りにしている事を伝えたかったのです。あらすじに関しても本当にこの通りであり、それ以上もそれ以下もありません。ゲームの目的も一切明かされませんし、チュートリアルも存在しません。更に言えば現時点ではSteam上にすらプレイガイドが存在していないのです。
私は47分しかこのゲームをプレイしていませんが、恐らくこのゲームの目標は「犯罪者を挙げ、報酬を手にし、自宅に家具を買う」事です。いえ、見間違ってなどいません。もう一度念の為に書きますが、このゲームは「犯罪者を挙げ、報酬を手にし、その報酬で自宅に家具を買う」事です。意味が分かりませんか？私にも分かりません。オチもありません。本当にそうですから。なおこの家具に関しては購入すると勝手に設置されていく為、ハウスカスタマイズという要素で楽しむことは不可能でしょう。
プレイを開始したら即座にワードローブに向かい、着替えなければ外に出ても何も出来ないため制服に着替えて外出します。すると間髪入れずに無線が入り、「検問をして怪しい車を挙げろ」というミッションが下されます。私にはこのミッションの達成方法が最後まで分かりませんでしたが、自宅のマイパトカーを左クリックする事によりカラーコーンを立てる事が出来、それを道路に並べる事で一般車両が停止することを発見し、車道に立ってみたら車がプレイヤーに激突しプレイヤーが車にめり込みスタック、カラーコーンを数個以上置こうとすると画面中にYou can't put anymoreというエラーが並び尽くしHUDを専有とい珍事が発生させる事は出来ました。尚、これはプレイ開始から3分で発生した出来事です。
結局当該ミッションのクリア方法が分からないまま散歩を続けていると、突如「空き巣が発生、現場に向かえ」という指示が無線で飛んできたのでマップ上で赤く光っているドットの地点に向かいました。その家に到着し、「ドアを開ける」を選ぶと礼状がないので開けられないと言われたので仕方なく「警察だ開けろ」を選択した所、そこには先に挙げたようにがらんどうの室内で傘を差したままこちらを睨みつける住人がいました。その住人の前でEを押してインタラクトすると会話ができましたが、選択肢が「何かありましたか」しか存在しなかった為、それを選ぶと「何もなかったわよ！ありがとう」と言われミッションクリアとなりました。おかしいだろ。
このようにゲームの面白さは皆無ではあるものの、プレイした時間＝話のネタが増えるという面で言えばSteamというストアの概念を既に超えたコミュニティー上ではもしかすると購入する価値はあったかもしれませんが、本作は超強気の19.99ドルが定価のためにおいそれとギフトする事も難しいのでこの面でも存在価値がありません。かと言ってBig Rigsのように派手にぶっ壊れた動画も恐らく撮る事ができないのでその筋の方にとっても価値が低いでしょう。残った用途としてはクソゲー実況用でしょうか？それでも盛り上がりに欠けると思いますが。

In short
I can recommend this game, assuming you know what you are getting yourself into. As stated by other reviewers, the tag "game" is stretching it a bit. The tag adventure ... seriously Steam. You basically watch episodes of The Walking Dead and at certain intervals you can make a choice or shoot a zombie (and this can be quite enjoyable if you are into that kind of thing).
The Wuts
As said, you are put in an episode of The Walking Dead and basically make the same choices and mistakes the characters in the tv serie do. It matches the setting of the series quite well. You'll recognize many locations and situations. Ever thought you'd do things differently? Well maybe now you can. I say maybe, because the game will also make a lot of choices for you. Some characters are really engaging, like the little Clementine. Without her I would probably have stopped playing halfway down the line. She is awesome and kewl.
The BUTs
Even though the game can be quite enjoyable, there are quite a few BUTs. Some are pet peeves of mine, others might be important to other players as well. As I was expecting a game, I was a bit dissapointed by the game elements. There aren't actually that much actions and choices. You will be mostly watching cutscenes. A lot of those cutscenes will be people bickering and staring at eachother (or just off in the distance). This makes the game very, very slow. The cellshaded graphics don't help unless you consider it to be art (which I do not). Movement is very clunky and the world is littered by invisible walls. A lot of the time you'll be guessing where you are going (luckily you can't go that far). The point & click part is very limited as well. So it's basically about the choices. The game invests heavily in the "illusion of choice" and does it quite neatly. It states if people remembered or liked your remark and at the end of a chapter you can see if other people made the same choice. However, the further you progress in the game, the more you'll detect that most of you choices don't actually matter. The same people will still die, the same♥♥♥♥♥♥will still hit the fan. Actual choices that matter are horrible for game designers because they need to add huge amounts of content. Hence I can imagine players are pushed towards the same outcome. Howeverrr, the game actually advertises the game adapts to you choice. Then it should make good on its promise right? As the game is quite short, I expected more impact based on the choices I made.
All in all, if you are a fan of the series you'll probably be able to enjoy these extra episodes. If you expect a fullfledged game, you might want to pick up a different zombie game.
ps. the 400 days DLC is silly, it only contains a few very short scenes that actually end when things get interesting. Even at 4.99eu I can not recommend it unless you are a HUGE fan (apparently there are lots of those)

Artificial Defense is (so far) mostly a fun stylish orbital shooter with some tower defense gameplay. I have played it for many hours over the last few days and will probably play for many more - it definitely has that "just one more game" feel. This game has a large amount of polish - it is pretty and has tons of nice little touches.
Most (but not all) of the time the player is using an array of weapons to shoot the enemies, mainly by leading them just the right amount. Then as the in-game currency RAM accumulates, the player can place towers or conquer local structures to help them. Each mission has a slightly different set of objectives (don't use this weapon or structure, gain this much RAM, conquer this structure, etc) so despite there being only a few maps, each mission still feels different. The game is fast paced, but not so fast that people with slower reflexes (like me) can't succeed. It often feels more relentless than hectic.
The difficulty of missions ramps up smoothly. The player progresses not only by becoming better, but also by upgrading their equipment to better models through collecting RAM at the end of each mission. So far this has worked well. I'm about half way through and have not needed to grind missions yet - once a mission has been completed successfully, I move on. I am currently 20 missions in and it has taken me about 6 hours - so there is value for money (although I got my copy for free).
The theme is supposed to be computer based: the enemies are computer virii and the player defends their CPU. However, this is a weak point of the game as the theme is applied very thinly. Why is there a DJ in the computer? I don't mind as I like the music, but it still seems strange. Same with the equipment - I'm currently using an Uzi to kill computer programs (huh?). Of course, this doesn't effect the compelling gameplay, so I just ignore it.
There are so many nice little touches in this game (apart from the good balance). There are fireworks when the player reaches certain achievements. The menus bounce pleasingly. It just feels professionally done - good work for a solo dev.
Definitely recommended.

First off, don't expect this to be your run-of-the-mill tower defense game.
This game focuses heavily on resource management and plays more like a hybrid shooter/tower defense. The tower cost scales up quickly so you can only afford to place a few strategic ones to back you up. The rest you have to shoot down with projectiles/missiles/bombs manually, and every one of those costs resources. So this is not one of those place towers and watch things die TD games. It is more challenging than most TDs, but has an interesting balance. I found it to be quite enjoyable, though frustrating at times in a type II fun sort of way.
The developer is very active. Just today I had an issue with the game, which I posted on the discussion board. Someone on the board picked up on it, notified me that the developer was offline at the time, that he has forwarded this to him. The issue was acknowledged, responded to on the board, solved, and patched within 24 hours of the issue being posted on the board. For an one-man-show developer, that is impressive.
In short, if you're looking to try a new TD hybrid that is challenging, I would recommend giving this game a try. It's a fun indie game with a developer that I feel is worth supporting.

My original review was negative for a very good reason - the game was not complete.  It was not ready for "prime time".  It should have waited for March or June or whatever month the game was ACTUALLY going to be complete instead of bowing down to a small minority of professional gamers.
But now it's March.  The update is out!  Some missing modes are finally in the game, and other previously lackluster or absent features are now adjusted.  So...
PROS:
-Great battle system.  Good for beginners and veterans of the series.  If you are a person who earns for the days of 3rd Strike poking with the accessibility of Ultra Street Fighter 4 attack inputs (a.k.a. "Safe Fiighter 4") this game is definitely for you.
-Great balance - for now - when it comes to the character roster.
-Online (when it works) is great.
-Training mode is rad.
-Game looks great and has an art direction that kicks the previous game's♥♥♥♥♥
-Trials Mode and Demonstrations are a great mode.
-Battle Lounges (lobbies) are awesome and are an improvement from USF4 (post update).
-Wall-to-wall, 20 lbs. of boobs and butts.  I'm looking at you, Laura...R. Mika...Cammy...Chun Li.
CONS:
-Online experience can vary greatly, depending on a lot of factors outside most player's control.  Not sure if an issue with netcode or the servers.
-When game first starts, you are (or at least were) forced into a tutorial.  Worked for the Beta, but definitely unwelcome in its current form.
-Game auto-assumes you are using a supported gamepad, which hurts first users on PC who are unaware.  Keyboard controls are not listed, so those who do not know to use H J K or B N M and enter are kinda screwed until they figure it out or look it up.
-Game does not support most older arcade stick controllers on PC - forcing most to use third-party app JoyToKey to map the buttons outside the game.
-Online is full of ragequitters that are currently unpunished for the most part - which makes Ranked matches and the scoring system kind of a "love it or hate it" experience.
-Still missing as of this review the full story mode (it gets released in June), a classic and standard Arcade mode, and a couple other features most modern games have.  Example: Online Training Mode with you and a friend - which even USF4 had...
-UI is kind of wonky for Steam.  Can't use Steam UI to invite players to matches.  Other UI choices still need some work, like inviting players and accepting them.
Despite some serious cons - the game has improved greatly and will only continue to improve with time.  Single player loving skeptics can breathe a little easier now, and the game practically throws free content at the community at this stage.
Buy it now or later, it's finally a solid purchase for fighting game fans.  True casual or singe player lovers may still want to wait until summer 2016 for the final major updates.  Will update the review if some of the cons listed are eventually fixed.

Unfortunately, I can't recommend this game in its current state. I had a hard time deciding on this, since I am a kickstarter backer, but I can't just ignore all the flaws. I am also aware that Saurian is still in Early Access. Thus, this is a temporary thumbs down, as I will look at the game again in a few months and change it accordingly.
So what's wrong with the game?
It is far too buggy to enjoy and has little to no content at this moment. Here's an overview of my first few tries:
1. I spawn and my Raptorparents immediately run towards a T-Rex, getting eaten up by it in seconds.
2. I spawn and my Raptorparents run straight into a river, where they stay for the next 10 or so minutes before getting eaten up by a crocodile-ish creature.
3. I spawn and my Raptorparents run into a tree and get stuck there two seconds into the game.
4. I spawn, immediately leave my parents and fall through the ground after about 15 minutes.
The Raptorparents are a huge problem but just ignoring them and going on your own journey from the beginning is not much better, as most of the other creatures act just as dumb. Often they just stand around and don't move at all.
The second problem is the lack of content. Currently, there's only the Dakotaraptor playable (there's going to be six in the future) and all you do is run around, try to find small lizards (or bigger snacks when you're grown) and drink from a river now and then. I am aware that this is how dinosaur survival was most of the time but at this moment - with all the bugs and lack of content - it is not enjoyable for me. There's also only a handful of other creatures, after about two hours I've seen almost everything the game currently offers.
Of course, it also has some good points. The graphics are nice to look at and it's obvious that the developers put a lot of effort into portraying the Hell's Creek formation and its inhabitants as realistically as possible. Once in a while (sadly not very often) the dinosaur AI works well and watching them roam around is fun for a bit. The dinosaur models are extremely detailed and beautiful. For a paleontology/dinosaur fan like me, that's very enjoyable.
However, due to the lack of content I got bored after about 2 hours and the constant bugs and barely functioning AI frustrated me most of the time. For the - in comparison with a few other Early Access games - pretty high price of 20€ I definitely can't recommend it in its current state. Especially not if you want a fun, long-lasting game at this point in time. Nevertheless, if you want to support the developers by buying their product and giving feedback, join the club :)
I hope the devs will continue to put their all into it and I'm sure I'll be able to change this review in a few months time. Until then, this is what I experienced with the game.

I've racked up eleven hours on this game plus a few more before linking to Steam and right now I'm really enjoying it.
(Right now is 5.30am on Sunday morning. If writing this review to wean me off Town of Salem so I can go to bed.)
Basically what we have is a 'Werewolf' style game but with none of the tiresome eye-closing/eye-opening and far less opportunities for cheating.
There are fifteen players in a game and each is assigned a role at random. The roles fall into three categories, Good Townspeople, Mafia and Neutrals.
- Good Townspeoples' goal is to kill all the Mafia and the Serial Killer (a Neutral)
- Mafia's goal is to kill al the Good Townspeople and the Serial Killer
- Each Neutral has their own goal, specific to their role
Some roles have the ability to kill other characters during the night, some characters are immune to being killed during the night but any player can be hung by hue and cry during the day if the majority of the town (including Mafia and Neutrals) agrees on it. This is where the real fun comes in. However well you deploy your role abilities, there's always the chance that you might be put on the spot and accused of being a traitor to the town. You often find yourself with little more than a few second to explain your actions (or tell a convincing lie) before the rope is around your neck. There's nothing more satisfying than talking yourself out of trouble when standing on the gallows. (Especially if you deserve to be there.)
In summary, buy this. It's not expensive and it's really good fun.

I was compelled to try 'Assassin's Creed Freedom Cry' after learning that slavery is the primary theme of the game. It is a game full of potential -- beautiful graphics, excellent voice acting, and a seldomly explored subject matter tied together with a commercially proven gaming formula. Yet, while 'Freedom Cry' was not horrible, it was not stellar or impressive as it should be. What we got is a game with a partially developed character, about whom I actually want to learn more, in a half-baked story that felt like 'Assassin's Creed' Lite.
It was innovative to play as a slave-turned-Assassin, who despite having gifts and talents bestowed upon him by the Brotherhood, still needed to be weary of slave jailers because of the colour of his skin. This was enough to change the usual pace of an 'Assassin's Creed' game, and I quite enjoyed that. Not needing to deal with modern day Abstergo/Animus story elements was also very welcomed, but it was odd to see the concept of synchronicity being left in the game. The modern day story elements in 'Assassin's Creed' had always felt like Ubisoft lacked confidence in a loosely historical third-person stealth action game. 'Freedom Cry' would have been the perfect opportunity for the franchise to distant itself from this extraneous story element, but that chance was unfortunately wasted.
My biggest complaint about 'Freedom Cry', is the naval combat. As someone who had not played 'Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag', I found the learning curve for naval warfare to be steep. There wasn't much of a tutorial and it took much trial and error for me to fully understand the basic mechanics. Plus, there was one mission that would have been difficulty to complete if I had not fully upgraded my ship through constant pirating. Such level grinding has no place in a game like 'Freedom Cry' as it slowed the entire game down. That and the repetitiveness and general lack of mission variety made the game rather tedious at times. Seriously, how many eavesdropping missions did 'Freedom Cry' really need for a nine-mission game?
The theme of slavery is both a shining factor and a major weakness of 'Freedom Cry'. I got much satisfaction freeing slaves in the game, but when the number of slaves I freed became the currency of weapon upgrades eligibility, I became frustrated. Shouldn't I be freeing slaves because it is the right thing to do and because it is the main character's motivation, not because of a weapon upgrade? Plus, why would black merchants, who knew I free slaves, only sell me weapons if I meet a quota? This game mechanic, while thematically important, was not very well thought out and well implemented.
For those who have played 'Black Flag', 'Freedom Cry' may appeal to you, but for those who haven't, your time may be better spent on other games than this somewhat mediocre entry to the 'Assassin's Creed' franchise.

I still remember when Flash games blew up on sites like Newgrounds, opening the doors to all kinds of small-scale platformers, puzzlers, and more. The most popular ones were always those that took the animation system to its limits, creating smooth, detailed movements out of roughly-pixellated limbs and parts. Intrusion 2 is very much a game in that vein, with a lot of attention paid to its look, and not a lot paid to its balance.
You play some Strider-looking fellow on an unarticulated crusade to kill lots and lots of of dudes on some snowy mountain. The controls are the common WASD to move and mouse to aim your hilariously flexible arms, but there's solid controller support here that I found to work much better. You start with but a pistol but soon come across weapons like an SMG, beam cannon, and grenade launcher. You'll need them, too, because the soldiers and robots of Intrusionland can take a lot of punishment.
What complicates this otherwise simple setup is the physics. Everything that isn't part of the landscape is affected by physics, including crates, boulders, weapons, enemies, and you. Killing soldiers ragdolls them, sometimes in really funny ways like when jetpack guys limply careen off into space. Blowing up robots or crates leaves debris you can kick around or stack. And of course, there are heavy rocks and such to push onto your foes. Areas can be pretty dense with objects, leading to literal piles of corpses or mountains of scrap metal.
I bet that sounds like fun, but sadly Intrusion 2 is not designed to make the most of the chaos you can sow. The physics system is one of the older, twitchier ones that can make objects explode off of each other just by intersecting the wrong way. While that can be funny, it isn't when they trap you between crates, or launch you into tough enemies, or fail to work as platforms when crossing piranha-infested waters. Enemies can do tons of damage very quickly since there are no invincibility frames, and checkpoints are entirely too far apart. I had to repeat one section almost half a dozen times because I kept getting glitched into boulders or knocked into guys with machine guns who just lay on the triggers.
There's so much cool stuff in here like riding wolves and fighting helicopters with arms, but the shoddy design of the encounters and the unpredictable physics make them more frustrating than anything. Your wolf, for example, is fully articulated which makes it look amazing in motion. However, its stride is dependent on its animation, so it can get stuck in platforms or take like eight tries to scale a wall because the limbs just aren't hitting the right places. And enemies are more than happy to blow you clean off of it with rapid-fire or hitscan weapons if you get hung up on anything.
It's a game built on precision that doesn't give you the control to be precise when you need it. Shootouts can be intense and rewarding, until you slip on a loose crate and your foes get a dozen free shots on you. Bosses are infuriating, with tight patterns that must be followed on top of whatever debris that has accumulated. I made it about halfway through the game before giving up, getting one-shotted by an unseen enemy with a grenade launcher after passing a platforming section over floating barrels that took me multiple tries. Intrusion 2 might look great but it feels terrible to play, and as we all know, looks only get you so far.

This game is really short, but I didn't particularly enjoy it. The story is... odd. I don't normally play point and click games, or games that are overall very dark, but I thought this would be a fun change of pace. Probably the biggest reason I tried it is because it was free, and I was looking for something different.
The game is a dark mystery story, with some horror elements. I don't want to give too much away, but there were some strange and creepy parts for me. The overall negative view of Christianity in the game felt rather unnecessary for the story, although it did give the protagonist slightly more depth, and gave a few more lines of dialogue to explain the setting and characters.
One issue that I had with the point and click playing was that sometimes it was hard to figure out what to click on. There were some objects I thought would give some response, but didn't, and some objects were pretty small or hard to click on. The bottle in the corner of the kitchen was one problem area, where I had to click in a very small area away from the object itself to look at it. Some objects tell you that you have to come back later, leaving you to look around for something you missed. I spent a lot more time than I would have liked just looking for objects to click on because they didn't stand out from the rest of the room. The controls aren't nearly as interactive as other video games, so it wasn't a very exciting game.
The protagonist is a writer who uses a lot of flowery vocabulary, giving him a very pretentious vibe. The whole game is mostly just him whining about how his relationship went wrong. Along with his amnesia and one-track mind, he just annoyed me the whole time. At the points where he repeatedly stated his longing, love, or hatred toward Serena, his character felt shallow because of how his personality just suddenly shifted. His mental state seemed really unstable and as the player, I couldn't feel attached to him at all.
I also had a problem with the game when my anti-virus software popped up while I was playing. I clicked back into the game but only got a black screen while the music kept playing. To get out, I had to hard shut down my computer, so I had to redo half the game because you can't save. But honestly, the game is so short, you shouldn't need to.
Of course, the game also has a lot of good points. What the game really excels in is the art and mood. The modeling and texturing is very good, and the lighting is pretty dynamic. There's hardly any animation, but that isn't something really necessary in a point and click game. The voice acting isn't bad, and there's enough variety in the dialogue that I enjoyed clicking on the same object repeatedly to see what he'd say. Even after finishing the story, I'm not 100% sure about what happened, which makes me continue thinking about it. The game focuses mainly on story and mood, which are two things I really look for in a good game. When it comes down to it, the game looks good and the story is different. The magazine in the nightstand gave me a good chuckle too.
Overall, I didn't particularly enjoy playing Serena, but it was a decently designed game. I'm not saying you absolutely shouldn't play it. If it sounds like something you can really get into, then go for it.

In this review I want to state the five biggest reasons why I hate this game.
TL;DR:
(This video is not by me)
Fallout 4 doesn't have anywhere near the RPG elements of the Fallout games from the past (excluding Brotherhood of Steel and Fallout Tactics)
The ♥♥♥♥♥♥ quests.
The dumbed down leveling system.
Creation club. ♥♥♥♥. Creation. Club.
Ok so first off I would like to say that I have a lot of time in this game as far as RPGs go for me, around 100 hours. The biggest problem with Fallout 4 when compared to other games is that if you want to play as two people; a distressed parent, or a distressed parent who murders everyone.
I feel that a big reason many people defend this game is it feels better than every other Fallout game in the actual shooting and combat mechanics, which is definitely true, but that isn't the point of a Fallout game. If I wanted good gunplay, I would play Battlefield or any other of the hundreds of triple A shooters on the market. I would take Fallout New Vegas's sub par combat paired with it's absolutely amazing role playing features over Fallout 4's good gunplay supplemented by ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "role play" any day.
The game's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chat wheel function only allows for 4 options, minimum or maximum. This is really stupid, as sometimes you need more options, sometimes you need less. You can see this in Fallout 4, as often times different choices on the chat wheel say the exact same thing. I think that the reason they chose this system was because they had voice actors, and didn't want to have to voice more than 4 lines for every dialogue.
I for one, do not much care for having my character voiced. It takes away the "be anyone you want" feel, that this game is already lacking.
Another problem is the way quests are set up. Every single quest, excluding the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ radiant quests, is just a stupid fetch quest. There are never any interesting quests like you find in Falout: New Vegas. Take "One for My Baby" from Fallout New Vegas, where you have to do some detective work to find the right person to be shot, or, if you want to, just haul some random sucker out in front of the dinosaur and watch their head explode. You also have quests like "Ain't Nothin' but a Hound Dog" where you have to get a new brain for Rex the dog. You can get the brain from multiple places, and depending on which one you use, Rex will get a new trait. Compare these with nearly every Fallout 4 side quest where it is either a fetch quest or a radiant quest. Also, Bethesda, can we please not have another missing family member storyline in the next Fallout game?
Next we have the dumbed down leveling up system, where everything is a perk you can get based off of your special level. This leads to boring perks like +20 percent damage. The only reason these perks exist is to make up for the lack of skill points, which, in other fallout games, did all of the boring leveling up, and the perks were always fun.
I feel like many of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ or removed features, excluding the chat wheel, are a direct result of Skyrim's success. It had terrible fetch quests, and everyone loved  it, but I've been typing for a half hour now and I'm not reviewing Skyrim, so you can  just watch the video by MisterCaption, where he basically says what I've said.
Lastly there is Creation Club, which should be called "Give us your ♥♥♥♥ing money."

Artificial Defense is a top down orbital shooter and tower defense game. It’s also got some strategy games elements. This game was developed by a single person and I was quite amazed at how much depth this game has.
The graphics are sharp and pretty straight forward. Most of the graphics are based on different shapes. E.g. the obstacles are square, the enemy creeps can be triangle or other shapes. The game is very colorful and pleasing to the eyes. The whole game has a PC theme going on. The levels are based on PCI card/motherboard design which has fans, USB ports, Audio ports, hard drives etc. This was pretty nice and I liked the fact that the creeps(enemies) come from the USB ports, which in real life also is most likely the places you get viruses. The game is very well designed visually and the tutorial and learning factor is made much easier the way navigation is done in the game. I had smooth over 100 FPS throughout the time I played and noticed no lag or slowdowns.
While the sound can use some variety, the soundtracks that come with the game are pretty upbeat and nice to hear. Voice overs are also present in the game with the announcer having one of those 80’s era robot voices. Some of the sound effects are a bit loud compared to other things though.
Now this game has innovated the tower defense genre. By combining top down orbital shooter mechanics, tower defense and RTS elements this game is pretty unique. There’s a lot of different missions to play. You have to defend your OS from creeps who are trying to infect it. Basically you have to stop these creeps form invading your OS. You can do this by placing towers or shooting them using your orbit guns. Using weapons and towers costs RAM which is your currency in-game. So keeping an eye on the amount of RAM is crucial as running out of it will most likely be a disaster for you. You can earn RAM by killing cookies, these cookies are harmless and spawn pretty frequently and they are trying to get to their cookie hole, so killing them nets you RAM. Other method of getting RAM is by building production towers or conquering things in the map.
To kill with your orbital shooting weapons, you have to lead your targets as the bullets/missiles take time to get there. You have a gun weapon, a missile and a nuke weapon. These are self-explanatory. The guns have the smallest hit area while the missiles have a bit bigger area and does splash damage to nearby creeps. The nuke has a larger area and does massive damage. When you start the game your weapons are not powerful at all (minus the tutorial, for tutorial they give you nice weapons). You can buy new weapons from the UPLAB by spending “kBytes”. These kBytes are earned when you do missions and the challenges earn you extra kBytes.
There are 3 types of towers you can place. Short range towers, long range towers and production towers. As their names imply, the short range has a short range of attack. The long range has long range attack and the production tower simply produces RAM from time to time. These can also be upgraded from the UPLAB. In addition to the guns and towers upgrades you also have hardware upgrades, this includes passive bonuses like health increase, fast forwarding etc.
You also have conquer option in the game. You can conquer databases and honey pots. Once you conquer them they will send out “datablips” and once these datablips reach their destination you will earn RAM. So this game requires you to do quite a lot and focus on many things at once, like placing towers, conquering stuff and concentrating on collecting RAM and shooting enemies. There’s 3 different difficulty levels so if you find the game hard you can always lower the difficulty.
The controls are probably the part which let this game down in my opinion. You can control the game in 2 ways, either drag the screen like you do in RTS games or the “move screen with mouse movement” feature can be toggled on. While this was my preferred method the mouse for some reason doesn’t feel natural. Like most of the times the mouse would move to another place instead of where I was moving the mouse. It’s like when the map rotates (which it does automatically) the mouse controls also move, so the mouse movement also moves along with the map, this can make the aiming consistently harder and you continuously have to “practice” your mouse movement before making shots. I hope the developer can add a static up, down, left, right 1:1 movement of the mouse, that can make the gameplay much easier.

The camp UI and crafting system are absolutely abysmal - design is terrible and the cost of making a new weapon doesn't really make it worth doing unless you have none. The upgrade system is equally poorly implemented - a huge number of supplies are needed for a 1-2 point damage boost. When your attacks are doing ~60 damage per hit, going from a 7-8 damage club to a 8-9 damage club is pretty meaningless. Character back story is cliche and not interesting.
That being said, the gameplay is "just good enough" that I don't feel like I wasted my time or that I didn't enjoy it, but it's not good enough for me to recommend someone else buy, even on a $5 sale. It's basically on par with a mobile game that I'd play at the airport when there's absolutely nothing else to do.

Alrighty, Let's see Town of Salem, what can I say about you?
Let me ignore the ~80 minutes I spent, unable to create an account.
It could've been a lot worse after all. And it was worth it!
First Impressions:
At first I thought "Oh no, I'm not prepared, what do I do when I get a role that's hard to have?",
but after a few moments of utter anxiety I decided to just jump in:
I joined a Classic, Classic Game, and the game gave me the role of the Sheriff.
I kept quiet mostly, I didn't see anyone suspicious. Also I noticed you could leave a message on death,
thus I simply filled in everything I found, everyone who was innocent.
And I didn't die. At the end of the game, only 3 of us were left. And the Serial Killer was trying to blame me.
I revealed my role and luckily the other townie believed me.
We won because the only other townie trusted me.
The Second Game threw me right into the Serial Killer role. I managed to kill 5 people without even popping up in the suggestions then someone just declared to "Randomly lynch" me. I was still happy, I mean, I learned from that.
The Third Game I was a vigilante. I didn't do anything and we won in the end by luck mostly.
The fourth game I was an executioner. They killed my target in the night though, so I ended up as a jester. Then I was killed in the night aswell.  The fifth game directly spawned me as a jester and I was killed in the night but it was fun.
The sixth game then spawned me as a Veteran... and I wasted my 3 alerts cause half the nights, nobody would get killed.
The seventh and my last game so far, then introduced me to the role of the jailor.
I didn't last very long, got killed in night two, missed the icon to take someone with me in night one.
I still enjoyed it very much.
The people I met were surprisingly mature and also had a decent spelling, something you can barely see in some communities and not once did I feel unskilled or scared of failure.
Failure is fun, it's amazing to see how it all plays out.
And I don't really have any complaints either.
Every role is explained by some boxes on screen,
there was no time where I thought "Oh gosh, what am I doing?"
The nights nobody attacked anyone made the game longer, sure,
but those few minutes? Oh Please! I'm very patient.
If you're a fan of tabletop games that are like this game,
e.g. One Night - Ultimate Werewolf, I can recommend this very much.
It may seem silly but that sort of Tabletop game is something you need at the very least
6 people to play and have it be fun. Here?
you can avoid the player count entirely because it's online!
Now that I think about it, I do have one complaint.
I can't seem to stop playing. Heh~!
Yeah, this game is a fun title and I can recommend it to you.
If you need numbers, here are some: 13 92 46 85.
And here are some of the other aspects I may have missed:
Sound: Nice Menu OST, but a tad loud, crank it down to 1% Volume and it'll be alright.
Graphics: You can see those in the videos and screenshots provided, Character models don't influence gameplay,
feel free to buy some for the looks if you want, but ultimately it doesn't change anything.
Gameplay: If you like the idea behind it, you'll love this game. That's all.
Community: Seems decent, except for a few lonely trolls who can usually be seen cursing and disconnecting,
nothing worth mentioning. If someone goes on about it being their first time and that they don't get anything in
the ingame chat? Most likely Jesters wanting to be executed, no trolls or griefers.
Yeah, the community isn't abusive but half the time they are incredibly thick, could be frustrating if you play to win.
I play for fun and guess what: That it is!
Overall (aka, the bit you skip to if this is TL, DR):
I love it. I recommend it. That's it.
Edit:
After 20 Hours of playtime it's STILL fun! Take that as you wish.

Assassin's Creed IV Black Flag: Freedom Cry Standalone game review:
In this Assassin's Creed game you are Adewale, a big black dude with a machete and a blunderbuss (Big shotgunny thing). You were formerly a slave, working on a plantation until pirates raided it. Although Adewale was previously the legendary Edward Kenway's Quartermaster, Adewale found that he wanted to save slaves, rather than be a pirate. In this game, you follow him across the Carribean, as he liberates slaves and recruits maroons.
The quality of the game is FANTASTIC! A new feature for the AC series (which was also introduced in Black Flag) is sailing across open world areas, rather than only whilst on missions (in Assassin's Creed 3). Sailing is incredibly simple as all you do is press the forward key, maybe move left and right, etc. A feature of the game (which personally had me excited) was the ability to board other enemy vessels. Boarding too is simple. All you do is press the S key (or whatever you have set stop to) whilst alongside another almost destroyed vessel, and it will automatically cause your ship to dock alongside. Your crew too will react, throwing Grappling hooks to draw your vessels nearer to each other.Your crew will then board the vessel and so on. The Graphics in the game are of a high standard, as Nvidia is involved (seeing as modern Nvidia games are awesome), so you will need at least a 2.6 GHZ processor and a decent graphics card to withstand the urges ingame. The fighting style in AC4 is incredibly similar to that of AC3, with only a couple of differences. For £11 I am incredibly happy, aand will be getting Black Flag soon.

Spectacular open-world 3rd person action / adventure. Visually vibrant environments, impressive world detail - especially with the free high resolution textures pack. Not a bad - however unrealistic - story line with good authentic to scene voice acting. Satisfying combat systems with lots of unique interactive environments & a cool bullet time mechanic. Great vehicle handling with an interesting ramming mechanic - all racing & driving is pretty damn sweet.
They've done a good job of mixing non-linear (reminiscent of its predecessors True Crime) like elements of multiple skill trees into a linear story, with all the freedom of sand-box & optional side quests.

My only issue is it suffers acute port-itis, where some keys are bound to two actions, the free-look camera constantly auto-corrects & menu / map navigation is slightly counter-intuitive for the mouse / keyboard user. Having said that it's still a great game & hell of a lot of fun!

XCOM 2 is a game about fighting a race of psychic ashkenazi space jews (spoilers!) that have enslaved the human race under an authoritarian government called ADVENT. Turn a group of drooling ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who can't hit the broad side of a barn into a team of badasses using weapons that would probably get you called a weeb if you tried to cosplay with one IRL.
First off, what to buy and what not to buy. The Alien Hunters expansion is painful, don't buy it. Shen's gift adds some decent new gameplay features. All other DLC is cosmetics, make of that what you will. War of the Chosen is great and 100% necessary. It adds three angsty weaboos to the game who will hunt down, capture and be generally complete edgelords to you and your soldiers. It also adds three new classes, a new espionage mechanic, zombies (literally hundreds), some new enemies, and actually makes melee semi-viable (not really though. It still sucks for everyone but the templar class.)
The combat is fastly improved since XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The viable combat strat in Enemy Unknown was to slowly aggro groups of enemies one by one and hope to god you didn't blunder into a new one while you were trying to take the current one out. XCOM 2 completely sidesteps this problem (mostly, anyways) by adding the new concealement mechanic, allowing you to spot the aliens before they see you and plan badass ambushes. Fun, satisfying to pull off properly, and makes frag grenades completely OP for the first few levels before the aliens start to beef up their forces.
The classes are all really fun and the different skill trees are all viable, except for the melee skill tree for the Ranger class which is godawful, never use it except for the major-level skill which is pretty good. Gunslinger snipers are some of the best mid-game units around, don't underestimate them. The spike between difficulty levels isn't as bad as it used to be which is nice. You should always play this game on Ironman and if you don't you're gay. Lots of cool custimization options to make your soldiers look as badass or autistic as you please.
The plot is okay. Someone on Polygon said "it has heart!" I think by this they meant that there is some occasional big bang theory-tier NEERDDDDD XD XD humour which has heart in the sense that it made me want to violently remove mine and splatter it all over my computer monitor so I didn't have to watch the cringe. Once you find out that the Elders have inbred themselves into a corner and are literally dying of a degenerative genetic disease that they desperately need a cure for, the plot becomes pretty predictable (HMMMMMM I WONDER WHAT THEY COULD BE DOING WITH ALL OF THESE HUMAN TEST SUBJECTS HMMMMM I WONDER WHAT THEY COULD BE DOING WITH THIS GLOBAL PSYCHIC NETWORK IT IS TRULY A MYSTERY) but the gameplay stays solid, and that's what I play XCOM for so it isn't a major complaint. The ending was very anime which I kind of hated because one thing I liked about XCOM: Enemy Unknown is it actually felt like science fiction and not science fantasy. Nothing wrong with either, but there is a lot of the latter being made right now and little of the former.
Overall this is a big improvement gameplay wise over XCOM: Enemy Unknown so if you liked that game you should purchase this one (with the new expansion, of course. The DLCs are negligable.) In terms of theme and premise, I'd say it took two steps forward with an interesting premise, two steps back with lukewarm implementation. That leaves it squarely where XCOM: Enemy Unknown set the bar in 2012, and that's just fine.

I don't usually "review" a game that i haven't fully experienced, but considering it's a fighting game, and how the community reacted to it, i feel forced to write one.
Firstly, i absolutely support reviews as a method of protest against bad habits, broken games and ports. And it's kinda what i'm trying to do here, but in the opposite way, it's the community the one i'm blaming today.
I see plenty of negative reviews blaming lack of content, lack of arcade mode, lack of keyboard binding and PS3/PS4 pads support, creating refund threads trying to influence in other people, etc.  And i'm afraid it's only your fault. Capcom said, and warned about the content the game was going to have on release. They said, crystal clear, the game was not going to have Arcade and Challenge mode until March. They said the game was not going to have keyboard bindings, PS3/PS4 pads supports on release, yet people bought it without getting proper info about the game before tossing 60 ♥♥♥♥ing bucks at the screen.
Yes, 60 bucks is too much for the current content, but you can find the game for 30 bucks pretty much everywhere else besides Steam. The single-player content WILL came in a month, the pad and keyboard support WILL come, and you'll be able to unlock pretty much every piece of DLC will ever have BY PLAYING. Which is nuts considering we are talking about Capcom. I played for 3 hours and i got 20% of a character price already. There won't be any Super, Ultra or any other payed revision of the game. It'll be free this time. If you really don't feel like waiting a month, then don't buy the game and wait.
Community ASKED Capcom to release it early with just Online and training, because Capcom Tour Cup is around the corner and with just those 2 modes people who really want to play competitive will have more than enough the first month. As i said before, it's only your fault if you didn't inform yourself about all this before tossing 60 bucks at the screen then blaming everything because you feel scammed. Your brain scammed you this time, not Capcom.
This is the first time, ever, that PC got a fighting game with cross-play. It was to be expected a couple of connection errors the first hours, because this is the first time Capcom did something like this. Yet you complained. I understand people against the new Naruto game, or MKX. Naruto devs lied to the community and didn't bring what they said they were. MKX was broken for half a year, they abandoned the game on PC and pretty much ♥♥♥♥ed up with the entire community, Warner Brothers style. But Capcom DID warn you guys. We knew what was coming from like 5 months to this very day.
7 years of SFV probably won't be possible and the game will die because you can't read, think, or wait. You want keyboard bindings? Use Xpadder in the meantime. Want PS3/PS4 sticks/pads? Use Xpadder in the meantime or any Xbox peripheral emulator.
All because you couldn't inform yourselft before buying, probably Street Fighter will die on PC. I've been a long time fan of the Tales Of franchise starting with Legendia on the PS2. But recently I've sort of fell off with the franchise as tiltles like Graces and Xillia failed to capture my attention. But this game has utterly rekindled my love for the franchise.
The story is one of the best in the franchise. Though it has its incredibly cheesy moments its full of down to earth characters with clear motivations, struggles and moments where they just seem like regular people. By the end of it I found myself absolutely in love with the entirety of the main cast.
Its great story is supported by solid gameplay as well. Traveling, something normally very mundane in RPGs is enjoyable thanks to the collectibles and optional bosses scattered around the world that give tangible benefits. The battle system is also a joy. At first I found it weird and sort of missed the more traditional systems of earlier tales games but this overhaul has actually added a lot of nuance to the Tales Of battle system making it enjoyable to explore and experiment with different techniques and combos. Additionally each and every character feels unique and fun to play as. Though Velvet is clearly stronger than the rest of the cast its not to the point where I feel like I need to play as her to win.
Over all at around 40hrs of just story content and numerous side objectives its a satisfying experience for any RPG fan and what a Tales Of game should be. It really makes me excited for the future of the franchise.

Most people who dislike Fallout 4 usually compare it to its previous titles, which is reasonable, since sequels are always compared to their predecessors. But with Fallout 4, it's apples & oranges. Compared to New Vegas, (hands down the best FPS/RPG) Fallout 4 is an absolutely TERRIBLE roleplaying game. You're forced into a character who already has their own backstory and main objective determined for you. For most fans, the first hour of Fallout 4 disqualifies it as a role playing game. And they're right.
Fallout 4 just isn't a role playing game.
Now, I know what you're thinking: "It's advertised it as one!" And you're right. But think about this: We're forced into characters with their own stories and objectives all the time in game series: BioShock, Borderlands, Mass Effect, Fable, etc. What do all these games have in common? They're story games with rpg elements, roleplay is not the focus.
If you think about Fallout 4 as a roleplaying game, it sucks. But, if you think about it as a FPS story game with rpg elements, it starts to make a lot more sense. When reading through people's opinions of the game, I often get the impression they were so jarred they couldn't choose their own story that it made it impossible for them to enjoy the main story at all.
If you want a great Fallout roleplay experience, go play New Vegas for Fallout 3. Fallout 4 is a novel, not a choose your own adventure book.

It's clear from the get-go that the developer, Rudder Games, set about an unprecedented task of telling the raw human story of existential panic with airs of subtlety that will creep upon you unexpectedly - one might even say silently, but deadly.  Although I must admit I am still cracking the walnut shell of the manifold puzzle and mystery of There's Poop In My Soup, I will attempt to peel away the deliberate obfuscation and touch upon the delicate interior of this postmodern tale.
You take upon the mantle of a nameless protagonist, clearly feeling isolated and ostracized from the rest of society, artfully symbolized by his or her separation from the crowd below.  The protaginst feels deformed, hideous, and vulnerable, made obvious by being completely nude and having a face that resembles the human derriere.  All attempts to communicate with normal society falls upon deaf ears, or worse, is filtered by the false pulchritude of pop-culture gone mad, rendering simple truthful words into "poop" by their savage reckoning.
You as the player attempt to break free from your angst-ridden prison by communicating, passionately, perhaps even
, your inner demons and hopelessness that fills the plastic environment around you with inconvenient emotions and startling realizations, piling higher and higher in the form of unwanted excrement.
You are given certain tasks to complete, such as pooping in soup as in the game's namesake, or an overpriced French coffee, or a young boy's ice cream cone.  Clear statements against society's consumerist disconnect from their food.  Other tasks include richocheting the turds of your experiential dread from one surface into another, symbolic of how one's words can reflect off the milieu that cages us, reverberating off the very walls like wails of constipated anguish.
This game, which is much more akin to a striking, disturbing. yet bold creation of vanguard art, is also rather short in length.  However, I prefer to think of it as
, conveying just enough of the message to digest and to allow for us to poop to our own conclusions.

For the longest time, this game has just been an enigma to me. Came out on Early Access with no advertising or fanfare, and most curiously almost no gameplay videos to be found. I can't tell if this is because it's so under the radar, or because YouTube autocorrects TAIKER as "trailer". However, now that I've had a chance to actually play the game, I can see it's just a sub-par mediocre platformer.
My first concern came when the launcher showed a lack of widescreen support. Even the most basic pixel art minimalist Unity experiments have widescreen support; why wouldn't a game like this? After that came the controller test, where not only is the A button tied to the "cancel" option with no way to change it, but you can't even do controller rebinding with the controller. You
to use the keyboard.
Once I got into the actual gameplay, things weren't much better. The gameplay isn't bad, but by god it's just completely mediocre. Half the game is mindless repetition, hitting the same X button until things die. Yes, there are other attacks as well, but what's the purpose of using them? There's no gameplay mechanic that punishes you for sticking with the X spam, nore is there anything rewarding you for switching things up. Some of the special attacks you learn ask for multi-directional inputs, and I was never able to pull those off naturally, only by wiggling the stick forward and up over and over and hoping for the best. So much of the game was an exercise in mashing X until problems are gone, occasionally dodging or shielding, and then finding out that doesn't make any difference because the giant robots that fire lasers across the screen can turn on a dime while firing.
I want to give the game credit where it's due: the artwork and character design is beautiful, and the main thing that drew me towards this game in the first place. Even just looking at the screenshots, you can see how good everything looks. The combat is dynamic and responsive, even if it is repetitive, and the only real issues I found in gameplay were the aforementioned multi-directional input attacks and some "I totally jumped, why did I just fall" moments. Which is still a problem in itself, but I'm trying to stay positive here.
But even that's difficult. Because even after I've set my other complaints aside, there are still weird issues that break my flow and leave me confused. Why are enemies placed right next to attack-activated switches so that every time I lock one into a combo, I'm turning elevator platforms on and off with each hit? How come enemies respawn when I exit and reenter a room, but unsolved puzzles don't reset themselves? Why does the music just stop playing entirely when I start talking to people? Why is the text so strangely formatted with the large space in between lines?
This isn't a bad game, don't get me wrong. It's just clearly unfinished. And under other circumstances I would say wait for it to leave early access, but here's the thing: it already has. They used early access to correct some glaring translation errors, but they didn't address any other issues with music or text or the general combat system. If I'm lucky, perhaps the developers will see this and work on some of the problems I faced, but unless that happens I just can't see a reason to buy this game over other, more strongly developed titles.
Under normal circumstances, I'd say you should experience the game some other way, such as watching a video playthrough, but you can't even do that, it's so obscure.

Taiker was a Steam Early Access game that I had my eye on for a good while now. Sure it looked a lil rough around the edges, but it had potential. I love metroidvana games and I love platformers that allow me to power up my character as much as I want. Taiker seemed like it would be my kinda game when it was finished in Early Access. So I kept it on my watch list and hopped for the best. A couple of days ago I was notified of it's release officially and I jumped right in.
That was a mistake.
Taiker should not have left Steam Early Access. The game is rife with control, writing, level design problems and bugs. I found myself able to get to the very last area, but have finally given up. Taiker's biggest problem besides not being good, is it's just not fun.

I've been playing this game for three days, and I'm finding it a pleasure and a challenge. I've been a fan of computer games for many years, and I find "Mad Games Tycoon" refects many of the aspects of computer game production you can read about in the magazines. Graphics, chipsets, game engines, consoles, production licenses, fighting for market share - all are featured in what feels like a realisic simulation of the games industry. You find yourself trying to update your technology quickly enough to sustain a competitive edge but not so quickly you produce a game no one can run on their machine. Even on the easiest level of difficulty you find yourself missing opportunities until you get used to the learning curve of it all.
The graphics are cartoony in their simple animations of employees bashing away on keyboards, occasionally getting up to use toilets and rest-rooms you'll need to provide for them. I smiled at the chance to build a production line for my newly developed games, watching the boxes roll off the conveyor to be stacked in a storeroom while a counter in the top right corner showed me how sales were going week by week. I've produced hits and stinkers in equal measure - you have to balance technology against playability with every game, and keep an eye on what the public enjoys at home. No use producing a great puzzle game about dragons when the teenagers want arcade adventures about pirates.
The game is full of lessons to learn about business and gaming, and offers an entertaining challenge to players who enjoy tycoon style fun. I'm certainly glad I decided to take a punt on buying it.

I would give Bastion a 10/10. It is a bird's eye view Action-RPG.
In Bastion you play as The Kid, one of the few survivors of a massive calamity that destroyed most of the world in which he lives. Your job is to restore the Bastion, a means or repairing mistakes and starting anew. Through this quest, you must accomplish a variety of tasks and fight through a variety of levels.
The levels themselves are beautiful and varied. They are revealed in a unique way: by dropping down in front of you as you explore more. It is like a fog-of-war mechanic, in which you cannot see something until you get close enough to discover it, and it works very well. The characters, enemies, and levels themselves are all very bright, colorful and beautiful. It was very nice to look at, and offered a variety of level designs.
As you explore the levels, another unique feature, and by far my favorite aspect of the game, is that everything you do is narrated by another character you meet. He describes parts of the world and the things you do in a way that gives more background and detail than initailly available, and it adds depth to the world. More so, it is downright cool. His voice is perfect for the role, and he nails all aspects of the stories he tells. It makes everything I did that much more enjoyable, and really enhanced the experience.
The experience is made better further by the combat mechanics and progression system. You have a dozen different weapons to choose from, and they are all different from each other with their own upgrades, strengths, and weaknesses to suit you preferences or playstyle. You have other passive or active bonuses you can imbue through gods you can invoke to make the game more challenging but give you more experience, or by finding artifacts in the world, buying different monuments, or carrying different potions to help your cause. All of this is unlocked as you go along and earn experience, and the new game plus mode lets you further explore ways to become a true badass.
Combat is fun and can be challenging when there are lots of enemies. You attack using your mouse while moving with the keyboard, and it works well and feels good. Your character is very mobile, but so are the enemies, so tactics must be used to block, roll, attack, and dodge, while keeping an eye on it all and whatever may come up. Enemies range from mooks to bosses, and they combine to offer a steady challenge. New enemies are introduced later in the game to offer more variety and force you to rethink your strategies.
The story is good enough for the purposes of the game. The main reason I felt connected with the character is because of the combination of the gameplay, the few characters you get to know, and the narrator telling the stories. Without that combination, as well as a good soundtrack of music, I would have cared about the story less. It isn't bad, I would classify it as good, but it feels like it maybe drags out a little through the later stages of the game. Overall I stayed engaged throughout the story, though not as much as for other games, certainly.
I would recommend this game at full price, but the great thing is that it goes on sale during summer and winter sales for very cheap. You will get great value with this game, as well as a good time.
